message:
Someone once asked me, “Is it really possible to be full of joy all the time?” Very quickly, I responded, “I’m joyful all the time!” Then, he said, “Don’t you think that’s a bit unrealistic?” “It depends on what reality is to you,” I responded. For some people, reality is their human experience, but our reality is Christ. In Christ, it’s possible to be joyful all the time. You can be joyful every day and be successful every day, irrespective of what happens to you or around you, because that’s God’s desire for you. He wants you to be joyful and successful.

The Lord Jesus came, lived, died, was buried, and rose again, all for your sake. He suffered that you might live in the glory of His sufferings. That means you should live joyfully every day, enjoying your life. That is what He died for: He died for you to live the best life, be the Father’s dream, and be a success in life and in everything you do, irrespective of the challenges that you might face. James 1:2 says, “My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into various trials.” The challenges that come your way are described in God’s Word as “light afflictions” (2 Corinthians 4:17).

There’s nothing that can overwhelm you. The distress is for a moment; it’ll surely turn out for your good! The problems you encounter that seem to be contending with your joy are temporary; they’re the springboards for your promotion and the next level of glory. Therefore, refuse to yield to pressures and adversities; subdue them with the Word. Stir up the joy of the Lord from within your spirit and laugh on in victory. Satan and his demons are discomfited in an atmosphere of joy, love, and laughter. So, live at the top all the time by maintaining a joyful heart.

My life is an expression of the glory of God. I live independent of the circumstances and situations around me, because I know that all things work together for my good. Therefore, I rejoice always in the Lord, conscious that I’m a victor for life. Glory to God

title: Born for Greatness
excerpt: In hereditary royal families, some princes and princesses receive their royal status because of the family into which they are born, not because they have first accomplished something…
scripture: “I will make you a great nation; I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing.”
subtitle: (You Carry God’s Potential)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for your seed of greatness that’s in my spirit. I will do great and mighty things that’ll bring you glory and honour, in Jesus’ Name.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Choose one task today—no matter how small—and do it with the mindset of greatness. Do it with excellence, with passion, and as unto the Lord.

message:
In hereditary royal families, some princes and princesses receive their royal status because of the family into which they are born, not because they have first accomplished something extraordinary. They may be young, inexperienced, or still learning, but their status isn’t something they have to earn through their achievements. And as they grow, their behaviour is expected to reflect the position they have been given. The same is true for you in God’s family.

Some teenagers grow up trying to prove themselves— to friends, to teachers, even to family. They wonder, “Will I ever be important? Will I ever stand out? Will my life really matter?” But here’s something powerful: greatness didn’t start with you trying to become something. It started with God’s decision. The Bible says, “...if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise” (Galatians 3:29). If you’re born again, you’re the seed of Abraham; the seed of greatness is in your spirit. Therefore, you ought to do great things. Great people do great things. When the seed of greatness is in a man, he’ll undoubtedly do great things that will be spoken of for generations after him. As a teenager, you might not feel “great” yet. You may still be figuring things out: school, friendships, purpose, your future. But greatness isn’t about your age; it’s about your identity.

If you’re born again, God’s Spirit lives in you. You carry divine potential. You’re not ordinary, and you’re not random. So, stop thinking small. Don’t say, “I’m just a kid,” or “I can’t do much right now.” Greatness shows up in how you think, how you talk, how you treat people, and how seriously you take your dreams. It shows in your discipline, your faith, and your courage to stand for what’s right. Tell yourself every day: “I’m born for greatness. The Spirit of God lives in me. I refuse to think small or act small.” You belong to God’s family—a family known for faith, boldness, and exploits.

## Prayer

title: Talk Right
excerpt: A GPS navigation system needs a destination to guide you. It only responds to where you tell it to go. If you input the wrong address, it confidently guides you to the wrong place.
scripture: “For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
subtitle: (Use The Right Language)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the revelation of your Word that enlightens my spirit. My words are full of grace and power, producing in me victory, excellence and glory. I speak always in line with your truth, expressing your divine thoughts through my words, and I’m continually transformed from glory to glory by the power of your Word, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, pay attention to your words—replace every negative or limiting statement with what God says about you.

message:
A GPS navigation system needs a destination to guide you. It only responds to where you tell it to go. If you input the wrong address, it confidently guides you to the wrong place. If you input your correct destination, it recalibrates every turn to get you there. Your words function like entering destinations into the GPS of your life. They determine which direction your energy, focus, and opportunities flow.

As a teenager, you’re building your world every day with your thoughts, your choices, and especially your words. When you constantly say, “I’m not good enough,” “I can’t do this,” or “Things never work out for me,” you’re forming a language of limitation. And that language will influence how you see yourself and what you expect from life. But as a child of God, you’ve been called to speak differently. This goes beyond positive thinking or motivational talk. It means speaking truth—and God’s Word is truth (John 17:17).

When you consistently speak the truths of God’s Word, those words shape your mindset, align your spirit, and produce results consistent with that divine reality. It’s not just the vocabulary that matters; it’s the system of thought behind it. For example, some say, “When we started worshipping, the presence of God came down.” It sounds spiritual, but it’s inaccurate. You carry His presence. He doesn’t come and go. When Christians gather, His presence is manifested—not imported.

Train yourself to speak in agreement with New Testament revelation. Let your words align with who you are in Christ—God’s dwelling place, full of His glory and power. As your language changes, your thinking will change. As your thinking changes, your experiences will follow. Glory to God!

title: Practise Who You Are
excerpt: When you were born, no one expected you to run. Growth was a process. Your muscles had to develop. Your balance had to be strengthened.
scripture: “But solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.”
subtitle: (Keep Training Yourself In Righteousness)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for training me through your Word and by your Spirit in the way of righteousness. I walk in your truth and function from the Kingdom’s perspective. My faith is strengthened, my understanding deepened, and I live every day in mastery and victory because I live in and by your Word, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Identify one situation today where you’ll consciously respond with the Word instead of your feelings—choose love, faith, or joy on purpose.

message:
When you were born, no one expected you to run. Growth was a process. Your muscles had to develop. Your balance had to be strengthened. You were lifted, supported, and encouraged until one day, you had enough strength to move. Today, you walk without even thinking about it. That’s how spiritual growth works. Sometimes, as a young Christian, you may wonder, “If I’m truly God’s child, why don’t I always get the results I expect?” But your identity isn’t the issue. The Bible says in Romans 8:16 that the Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we’re the children of God.

You’re God’s child—settled and established in Him. The question isn’t about your identity; it’s about your training. Spiritual maturity requires practice. You must be trained in righteousness and exercised in the Word. Christianity isn’t a passive experience; it’s an active life. We’re Word practitioners. You practise love when it’s difficult. You practise faith when circumstances challenge you. You practise joy when pressure mounts. You practise your divine authority until it becomes your natural response. James 1:22 reminds us to be doers of the Word and not hearers only. That means putting the Word to work daily.

When the Word says you’re victorious, act like it. When it says you’re blessed, speak like it. When it says you have dominion, live like it. Keep training yourself. Keep practising who you are in Christ. Just as a child eventually walks with confidence and ease, you’ll grow to a point where victory, health, wisdom, and prosperity flow effortlessly from your life. Refuse to be discouraged by temporary stumbles. Stay with the Word. Praise God!

title: Support the Gospel Financially
excerpt: Throughout history, God has used people who were young or seemingly unlikely to accomplish extraordinary things. A teenage girl named Joan of Arc led armies.
scripture: “And God is able to make all grace abound toward you, that you, always having all sufficiency in all things, may have an abundance for every good work.”
subtitle: (Learn To Give Cheerfully And Intentionally)
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for making all grace abound towards me so that I may always be self-sufficient, possessing enough to require no aid or support, and furnished in abundance for Kingdom expansion! Thank you for multiplying my resources for increased giving. I declare that I’m a financier of the Gospel, and my capacity to give is increased daily in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Make a plan to give for the Gospel this week. As you give, say, “Lord, I give this for the expansion of your Kingdom. I’m reaching the lost for Jesus through this seed.”

message:
Throughout history, God has used people who were young or seemingly unlikely to accomplish extraordinary things. A teenage girl named Joan of Arc led armies. A teenage shepherd named David faced a giant soldier whom everyone else feared, and his courage changed the course of a nation. A boy provided five loaves and two fish that Jesus used to feed thousands. You don’t have to wait until you’re older, wealthier, or more established to matter. The size of your resource matters less than the size of your purpose.

True success isn’t just about getting good grades, building a career, or having nice things. True success comes when you understand God’s vision and choose to be part of it. And what’s His vision? He wants His divine presence taken to the nations of the earth, and He’s counting on us— His kids—to do it. You might be a student today, but you’re already a Kingdom ambassador. Your talents, creativity, and social influence can all point people to Jesus. Everything you do should connect to this bigger purpose: winning souls and expanding God’s Kingdom.

Start now. Whether it’s from your allowance, a small job, or a gift you receive, learn to give cheerfully and intentionally. When you give towards church projects, outreaches, or missions, you’re helping someone, somewhere, hear about Jesus. Avoid the mindset that says, “As long as I have enough for me, I’m good.” You’re called to think bigger. God can trust you with resources when your heart is set on His Kingdom. As you stay committed to supporting the Gospel, He’ll increase your capacity and position you for greater impact.

scripture: “While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, winter and summer, and day and night shall not cease.”

message:
Think about how differently things worked just thirty years ago. If you wanted music, you drove to a store, bought a CD, went home, and played it. If you wanted a movie, you waited for it to air on television or rented it from a video store. Today, you pull out your phone and stream anything instantly. The waiting period disappeared. In the same way, God designed your spiritual life to operate on instant access, where harvest doesn’t require waiting for the “right season” because every season is harvest season!

The Lord didn’t say in our opening verse, “While the earth remains, seed time and harvest time...shall not cease.” Sadly, that’s how some folks read the scripture above in their minds. Someone may ask, “But what’s the difference?” The difference between the two statements is irreconcilable. To say “seed time and harvest time” suggests that there’s a definite time of sowing and a definite time of harvest. But the idea given to us in the Scripture, when it says “seedtime and harvest”, is that harvest is anytime. In other words, you might as well consider today the set time for your harvest!

What the Lord is saying to us here is that though there must be a time of sowing (seedtime), there’s no fixed time for your harvest; you can call it forth anytime! title: Living the Miraculous Life
excerpt: The life and ministry of the Lord Jesus was an unending stream of the miraculous.
scripture: “And there are also many other things that Jesus did, which if they were written one by one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that would be written. Amen.”
subtitle: (The Holy Spirit At Work In You)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for making it possible for me to experience your miraculous power in my life and in the lives of those around me. Thank you for channelling that power towards me, and also for making me a medium through which that power can flow to touch others. My life is an unending stream of the miraculous because the Holy Ghost lives in me! Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Expect something miraculous to happen today. Be ready to perform a miracle, for the power is in you. When you see it, give God the glory.

message:
The life and ministry of the Lord Jesus was an unending stream of the miraculous. He fed five thousand people with a little boy’s lunch, raised the dead, walked on water and did so many other mind-blowing miracles which are recorded for us in the gospels. These weren’t exaggerated stories or legends; they were real moments where God’s power showed up in amazing ways. Though Jesus has gone to heaven, He’s left the Holy Spirit here in the earth (John 14:16) to continue the work of the Father through us.

He said in John 20:21, “...as the Father has sent Me, I also send you,” meaning our lives ought to be an unending stream of the miraculous as well. You ought to expect miracles and participate in the miraculous since the Holy Spirit lives in you. He’s the power of the Godhead! He’s the doer and performer of miracles. Jesus said, “...the Father who dwells in Me does the works” (John 14:10); that’s the Holy Spirit! He’s the one that indwells us with the miracle-working power of God.

You don’t have to wait until you’re older to see God move. He can work through you right now. This is your set time to receive that miracle you desire. The Bible says, “...as He (Jesus) is, so are we in this world” (1 John 4:17). In other words, as He is supernatural, so are we. Hallelujah! If He had a daily experience of the miraculous, then the story should be no different with you. Recognise that the Holy Spirit is working in you, with you and around you, though you may not see Him with your optical eyes. That means a miracle can take place in you, around you and through you, in any place, at any time! Glory to God!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for making it possible for me to experience your miraculous power in my life and in the lives of those around me. Thank you for channelling that power towards me, and also for making me a medium through which that power can flow to touch others. My life is an unending stream of the miraculous because the Holy Ghost lives in me! Amen.

title: The Success Secret
excerpt: Horticulturists understand that you can’t judge a tree’s health by looking at one branch. A tree might have one branch loaded with fruit while the rest is diseased or dying.
scripture: “This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success.”
subtitle: (The Infallible Recipe for the God-kind of Success)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I’m a success. I’m prospering in all my ways! I have good success, and I deal wisely in the affairs of life because I meditate on the Word day and night. Whatever I lay my hands upon turns into undeniable success. As I keep the Word of God before me, observing to do what it says, my continual success is guaranteed and apparent to all. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, meditate on Psalm 1:1-3, particularly verse 3: “...whatever he does shall prosper.”

message:
Horticulturists understand that you can’t judge a tree’s health by looking at one branch. A tree might have one branch loaded with fruit while the rest is diseased or dying. The tree isn’t truly healthy until every part thrives. Similarly, a person might excel at one thing—career, academics, athletics—while their relationships crumble or their character decays. That’s not success; that’s one thriving branch on a struggling tree.

Success from God’s perspective has nothing to do with a man’s position in life or how much he possesses. Jesus said, “...one’s life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses” (Luke 12:15). The Message version puts it this way: “...Life is not defined by what you have, even when you have a lot.” How true! Real success is found in Christ and in His Word. That’s why the Lord gave Joshua the recipe for success in our opening scripture: “meditating on the Word day and night!” That’s the infallible recipe for the God-kind of success.

Real success isn’t partial. It’s total. It shows in everything: school, work, friendships, family, and your walk with God. God doesn’t want you to be good only in some areas and struggle in others. He wants you to be excellent in all you do. That’s the life He’s set before you. If you’re born again, you’re already a success! The seed of success is in your spirit.

The secret is in the Word; it’s by meditating on the Word day and night, speaking the Word to yourself until it takes over your thought processes! If you’d do this, everything you do will prosper. You’ll be an excellent child, an excellent student, an excellent team member, and of course an excellent Christian! You’ll be an all-round success. Glory to God!

title: Higher Standards
excerpt: Marine biologists have observed that fish placed in polluted water gradually adapt to it. They don’t recognise the contamination because they’ve grown accustomed to swimming in it.
scripture: “Therefore “come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch what is unclean, and I will receive you.’”
subtitle: (Live Above The Indecent Standards of The World)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the power of your Word in my life. You’ve made me an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity, and I show myself in all respects to be a true model of righteousness and good works. I’m the light of the world, and my light shines ever so brightly, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Time for a thorough self-check! This week, review your online/ social media activities and do away with any material (pictures, videos, songs, comments, etc.) that’s inconsistent with your godly character.

message:
Marine biologists have observed that fish placed in polluted water gradually adapt to it. They don’t recognise the contamination because they’ve grown accustomed to swimming in it. Only when transferred to clean water do they realise the difference. Similarly, when you’ve been surrounded by certain behaviours long enough, they begin to feel normal, even when they’re slowly degrading the standards you once had.

As a Christian, you should never be swayed by the world’s standards. God’s Word teaches us moderation, not excess. There are things you just shouldn’t allow. As a Christian, you have a higher life with higher standards. There should, therefore, be some decency in your dressing, speech, and way of life. Read our opening scripture again; it says, “…Come out from among them and be separate…;” that means “Be different!” You have a different life, a different culture, and a different mindset; it’s called the mindset of the righteous.

You were sanctified by the Spirit, which means He separated and declared you holy and undefiled. Therefore, walk in righteousness. Don’t let those of the world drag you into ungodly behaviours; otherwise, you can’t win them for the Lord. Your standards have to be higher to do so. Copy the Master; think like Him; act like Him; talk like Him. There’s a decency that goes with the Spirit of God, and that decency must be evident in your life. Let everything about you edify others and bring glory to the Lord in every way and every day, for you’re the light in a dark and perverted world.

## Prayer

You’ve made me an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity, and I show myself in all respects to be a true model of righteousness and good works. I’m the light of the world, and my light shines ever so brightly, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: “My Day Is Blessed!”
excerpt: No successful farmer walks onto unplowed, unseeded ground and looks forward to a harvest.
scripture: “And God blessed (spoke good of) the seventh day, set it apart as His own, and hallowed it, because on it God rested from all His work which He had created and done.”
subtitle: (Learn To Bless Your Day Every Day)
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank you, for I receive all the favours and benefits you’ve ordained for me today. The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places, and the land is subdued before me, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Say these words aloud, “My day is blessed! I walk in the supernatural and manifest the righteousness of God today. I walk worthy of the Lord this day, pleasing Him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of Him! Hallelujah!”

message:
No successful farmer walks onto unplowed, unseeded ground and looks forward to a harvest. Long before planting season, they prepare the soil, enrich it, and speak with confidence about what the land will produce. They understand that the condition of the ground before planting largely determines what comes up later. Your morning declarations are like preparing the soil of your day; you’re getting the ground ready to produce what you intend to grow.

In Christ, every day for you should be a day of joy, blessings, thanksgiving, and rejoicing. That means you should look forward to having a great day, every day! This is God’s will for your life. Our opening verse shows us just how we can walk in this reality; it says, “And God blessed (spoke good of) the seventh day….” This is a profound revelation of God’s truth! You ought to bless your day. This is possible because you’re created in the image and likeness of God, to live and function like Him. So, you ought to take a cue from the Lord and do what He does.

Psalm 68:19 says, “Blessed be the Lord, who daily loads us with benefits….” There are blessings and benefits for you every day; expect them and speak them forth! Don’t talk like unbelievers who say, “I’m having such a bad day.” Instead, take charge of your morning; bless your day and tell it exactly what to produce for you.

As you wake up, speak productivity and favour into your day. Declare that the Spirit of God is leading you to be at the right place at the right time. Declare that He’s opening up “main character” opportunities for you and giving you the wisdom to recognise and win all the way.

title: Be Excellent
excerpt: Andrew’s name was on the school’s Board of Honour again, just like every other term. It didn’t matter whether it was academics, sports, or leadership; everything he touched seemed to shine.
scripture: “Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the governors and satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king gave thought to setting him over the whole realm.”
subtitle: (Stand Out from the Crowd)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for giving me an excellent spirit and for sending the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of excellence, to live in me and produce excellence in me. I’ll excel in all my endeavours and do things right the first time because the Spirit of excellence is working in me mightily, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: In one task today—whether at work, school, or home—choose to go above and beyond what’s expected. Do it with such excellence that people will notice something different about you.

message:
Andrew’s name was on the school’s Board of Honour again, just like every other term. It didn’t matter whether it was academics, sports, or leadership; everything he touched seemed to shine. His projects were always well executed, his team was always motivated, and his results were always outstanding. Students often wondered what his secret was. But Andrew didn’t rely on “luck” or waiting for someone to push him. He simply recognised and expressed what was already within him: an excellent spirit.

Just like Daniel in the Bible, who “had an excellent spirit” and prospered in all he did, God has placed that same Spirit of excellence inside you. As read in our opening verse, Daniel was described as one who dealt excellently in his affairs because “an excellent spirit was in him.” Anointed men and women in the Old Testament had the Holy Spirit “come upon them,” but today, He lives in you! He’s the Spirit of excellence; hence, it’s His ministry to cause you to excel in everything you do. When you recognise this truth, walking in excellence will become a natural occurrence for you—you’ll excel in every endeavour.

For young people, excellence means more than just getting good grades or winning games. It’s showing up fully in everything you do, whether it’s school, your hobbies, sports, online projects, helping others, or your involvement in the house of God. To excel means to go beyond the ordinary, to stand out from the crowd, and to leave a mark wherever you are.

You don’t have to pray to God to make you excel, for excellence is in you. All you need do is recognise it and express it. Choose to excel; make the conscious effort to improve your mind by studying the right materials. Become studious; don’t loaf or laze around, for laziness isn’t a quality of an excellent spirit; go the extra mile! Reject mediocrity and mundanity from your life.

title: Too Late to Be Poor
excerpt: The moment you were born again, it became too late for you to be poor, for you were born into prosperity.
scripture: “Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.”
subtitle: (Walk In Prosperity… It’s Your Birthright)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for bringing me into the life of abundant prosperity, where I lack nothing and require no aid or support! I honour you for your wonderful blessings in my life, which flow out and touch others around me, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, whenever a thought of lack or poverty tries to dominate your mind, reject it immediately and declare, “I was born into prosperity. It’s too late for me to be poor. I’m blessed in the city and blessed in the field. Everything I do prospers!”

message:
The moment you were born again, it became too late for you to be poor, for you were born into prosperity. The Bible says, “For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich” (2 Corinthians 8:9). Now you know why it’s not possible for you to be poor anymore!

Moreover, the prosperity that comes from God isn’t only about money, riches and other material wealth. It’s about the totality of your well-being—spirit, soul and body. It’s about having the blessing of God on your life in such a way that you’re able to impart the same life to someone else. It’s the manifestation of God’s grace upon your life which causes everything that concerns you to succeed exceedingly.

You’re born to prosper. Begin to function in this truth. The Lord already made the sovereign declaration that whatsoever you do shall prosper; therefore, let that be your mindset. Refuse poverty and poverty mentality. Refuse thoughts that say “I can’t,” “I’ll never,” or “people like me don’t succeed.” Recognise that you have a limitless and inexhaustible inheritance in Christ. Glory to God!

## Prayer

title: God’s Number-One Job
excerpt: Soul winning is God’s number-one job.
scripture: “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.”
subtitle: (Take Soul Winning Very Seriously)
prayer: Dear Lord, thank you for the privilege of being a vital labourer in the end-time harvest. I can see that the fields are white with the harvest; therefore, I commit myself to pulling men and women out of darkness into the kingdom of light. By your Spirit, I’m guided to seize today’s opportunity to impact and win souls into the Kingdom, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Before the day ends, look for an opportunity to share the Gospel with someone. It could be a friend, a family member, or even a stranger. It doesn’t have to be a long sermon; just a simple testimony of what He’s done for you.

message:
Soul winning is God’s number-one job. It’s so important to Him that He sent Jesus, His only Son, into the world, not to be the president of a nation, a senator or an engineer, but a soul winner. No wonder the Lord Jesus Himself also took soul winning very seriously during His earthly ministry. Even when He was physically tired and needed rest, the opportunity to share the Gospel with the Samaritan woman was enough to make Him forget His hunger and tiredness. He said to His disciples,“... My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work” (John 4:34).

We need to realise as God’s people that we may not always have the opportunity to win souls, and that’s why Jesus said, “I must work the works of Him who sent Me while it is day; the night is coming when no one can work” (John 9:4). He knew He had a time limit in the earth; so He maximised it by being an effective soul winner. This is the same thing He expects from us; we ought to recognise that the responsibility of telling others about the Gospel of Christ’s salvation has been entrusted to us (2 Corinthians 5:18), and we must do the work of Him that sent us while it’s day.

You’re young, and that’s your advantage. You have energy, influence, and opportunities to reach your peers, friends, and even strangers with the Gospel. The responsibility God has given you is serious: to share His love now, while the time is right. Don’t wait for the “perfect moment” or think you’re too young. God can use your social media posts, your school friendships, your conversations, and even your small acts of kindness to bring someone to Christ. This is the day of salvation; this is the season of the end-time harvest.

Soul winning is God’s number-one job. It’s so important to Him that He sent Jesus, His only Son, into the world, not to be the president of a nation, a senator or an engineer, but a soul winner. No wonder the Lord Jesus Himself also took soul winning very seriously during His earthly ministry. Even when He was physically tired and needed rest, the opportunity to share the Gospel with the Samaritan woman was enough to make Him forget His hunger and tiredness. He said to His disciples,“... My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work” (John 4:34).

We need to realise as God’s people that we may not always have the opportunity to win souls, and that’s why Jesus said, “I must work the works of Him who sent Me while it is day; the night is coming when no one can work” (John 9:4). He knew He had a time limit in the earth; so He maximised it by being an effective soul winner. This is the same thing He expects from us; we ought to recognise that the responsibility of telling others about the Gospel of Christ’s salvation has been entrusted to us (2 Corinthians 5:18), and we must do the work of Him that sent us while it’s day.

You’re young, and that’s your advantage. You have energy, influence, and opportunities to reach your peers, friends, and even strangers with the Gospel. The responsibility God has given you is serious: to share His love now, while the time is right. Don’t wait for the “perfect moment” or think you’re too young. God can use your social media posts, your school friendships, your conversations, and even your small acts of kindness to bring someone to Christ. This is the day of salvation; this is the season of the end-time harvest.

## Prayer

Dear Lord, thank you for the privilege of being a vital labourer in the end-time harvest. I can see that the fields are white with the harvest; therefore, I commit myself to pulling men and women out of darkness into the kingdom of light. By your Spirit, I’m guided to seize today’s opportunity to impact and win souls into the Kingdom, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Before the day ends, look for an opportunity to share the Gospel with someone. It could be a friend, a family member, or even a stranger. It doesn’t have to be a long sermon; just a simple testimony of what He’s done for you.

## Further Study

1 Corinthians 9:16; 2 Corinthians 5:18-19

## Bible Reading Plans

**1-Year Bible Reading Plan:** 2 Thessalonians 3:1-18, Isaiah 48-49

**2-Year Bible Reading Plan:** John 6:30-40, 2 Kings 4

title: Your Inheritance Is Vast
excerpt: The world is full of treasures, yet many go through life without ever knowing those treasures belong to them.
scripture: “The earth is the Lord’s, and all its fullness, the world and those who dwell therein.”
subtitle: (The Riches Of This World Belong To You)
prayer: Father, I thank you for opening the eyes of my spirit to discover the treasures and inestimable riches that you’ve laid up for me in life. I declare that this is my set time to enjoy the treasures and hidden riches in secret places, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
The world is full of treasures, yet many go through life without ever knowing those treasures belong to them. It’s like having access to something valuable but living as if you’re broke because you don’t know what’s yours. As a child of God, you’re not just an observer; you’re an heir! Every resource, every hidden wealth, every unclaimed blessing on the earth is yours in Christ. God said through Isaiah, “I will give you the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places” (Isaiah 45:3).

The riches of this world belong to God, and as His child, everything He owns is at your disposal. The Scripture reminds us, “And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise” (Galatians 3:29). Your inheritance is vast—both the treasures already revealed and the hidden riches waiting to be discovered. That includes ideas, opportunities, connections, and solutions others haven’t even thought of yet.

The Lord Jesus Himself demonstrated this. He instructed Peter to catch a fish, and inside its mouth was a coin to pay the temple tax. This shows that God’s provision is always accessible when we move in obedience and faith. Long before you were born, God deposited reserves of wealth and blessing for you: ”unsearchable riches” (Ephesians 3:8). These are inexhaustible treasures, waiting for you to access them with the wisdom and revelation of the Holy Spirit.

The Bible says all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ (Colossians 2:3). Thus, as you constantly study the Word and fellowship with the Spirit, you’ll receive insight into reality; the Spirit of God will help you discover the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places. Glory to God forever!

title: Speak from the Word
excerpt: Faith isn’t about making empty confessions or merely repeating words.
scripture: “And since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, ’I believed and therefore I spoke,’ we also believe and therefore speak.”
subtitle: (The Basis Of Our Confession Is The Word)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for granting me an understanding of the true basis of faith. My words are full of power because they’re anchored in the finished works of Christ. As I declare your Word, the realities of my inheritance in Christ, my health, wealth, and victory are activated and manifested, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Take a scripture on any area of concern you have, meditate on it and declare it out loud.

message:
Faith isn’t about making empty confessions or merely repeating words. For example, saying “I’m fine, I’m fine, I’m fine” when you’re stressed about school, exams, or friendships doesn’t make things better. The scripture above says, “I believed, and therefore I spoke,” and in Romans 10:10, believing comes first, then speaking. What’s the basis of your “I’m fine”? Faith rests on what Christ has already done.

So, when you say, “I refuse to be sick,” it’s because God has already given you divine health. Even if you feel tired, anxious, or stressed, when someone asks, “How are you?” you can say, “I’m excellent,” because God’s life in you is stronger than sickness, fear, or weakness. The same goes for declaring, “I refuse to be poor,” because Christ has made you rich. 2 Corinthians 8:9 says, “For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich.” Being “rich in Christ” isn’t just about money; it’s about blessings, favour, and opportunities.

Our faith in who we are in Christ is the foundation of our confessions. It brings God’s Word into manifestation. We can also speak new realities into existence by God’s Word (Greek: “rhema”). Whether it’s courage for a test, peace in friendships, or creativity for a project, speaking God’s Word activates change. Affirming your health, success, and victory is acknowledging what Christ already made yours. Glory to God!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for granting me an understanding of the true basis of faith. My words are full of power because they’re anchored in the finished works of Christ. As I declare your Word, the realities of my inheritance in Christ, my health, wealth, and victory are activated and manifested, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: You Have Access to the Father
titleOriginal: YOU HAVE ACCESS TO THE FATHER
excerpt: The Old Testament folks always had to resort to the prophets and seers to enquire of the Lord.
scripture: “You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give you.”
subtitle: (It’s The Father’s Good Pleasure To Hear You)
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank you for the privilege and opportunity to fellowship with you in prayer and make my requests known unto you. I rejoice at your Word that lets me know that your ears are attentive to my requests and that it’s your good pleasure to grant my heart’s desires. Thank you for this wonderful blessing and privilege, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Don’t just mutter a timid prayer today; talk to the Father with boldness and confidence. Present your request clearly, in the Name of Jesus, and then thank Him that you’ve received the answer.

message:
The Old Testament folks always had to resort to the prophets and seers to enquire of the Lord. It wasn’t a common revelation amongst the people to talk directly to God in prayer and expect to receive an answer from Him. However, when Jesus came, He made it clear that it was the Father’s desire for us to boldly and confidently talk directly to the Father in prayer and receive answers: “And in that day you will ask Me nothing. Most assuredly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My Name He will give you. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full” (John 16:23-24).

The “day” that the Lord Jesus spoke of isn’t a twenty-four-hour day but a dispensation, a season, a set time in which you could make requests and receive answers to your prayers. Thanks be unto God! This is that set time! We’ve come into “that day” that Jesus was referring to. If you’re born again, you have the privilege of being able to pray and receive the answers to your prayers instantly: “...whatever things you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them” (Mark 11:24).

There’s no need to look for someone to pray to God for you; there’s no need to cry and keep reminding God of your troubles: just ask in faith and in the Name of Jesus, and your requests will be granted. Whether it’s about your grades, your future career, your friendships, or whatever, you can talk to Him directly. Always remember that it’s the Father’s delight to answer your prayers; it’s His good pleasure to give you the wonderful treasures of His kingdom (Luke 12:32). So, ask boldly. Believe confidently. Receive joyfully. Glory to God!

message:
As Jane dropped her backpack on the couch, she sighed deeply: “I don’t think this can ever change,” she muttered. “I’ve tried everything.”

Her older brother, Derek, looked up from his Bible: “Everything?” he asked with a smile. “Did you try God’s way?”

Jane frowned: “What do you mean? This is a hopeless situation!”

Derek shook his head gently: “Hopeless to whom? From man’s perspective, maybe. But with God, there’s no such thing as a hopeless situation.”

As a young person who’s born again, you’re not meant to react to life the way everyone else does. You’ve been called to function by divine principles. That means you don’t panic when things go wrong; you respond with faith. The life in you is the life of a victor. You were born to reign, even in your classroom, on your campus, in your workplace, and among your peers. When someone says, “There’s no way you can pass that,” or “You’ll never make it,” don’t be discouraged. Get excited! That’s your opportunity to put your faith to work. Pray. Declare God’s Word over your situation.

As Jane dropped her backpack on the couch, she sighed deeply: “I don’t think this can ever change,” she muttered. “I’ve tried everything.”

Her older brother, Derek, looked up from his Bible: “Everything?” he asked with a smile. “Did you try God’s way?”

Jane frowned: “What do you mean? This is a hopeless situation!”

Derek shook his head gently: “Hopeless to whom? From man’s perspective, maybe. But with God, there’s no such thing as a hopeless situation.”

As a young person who’s born again, you’re not meant to react to life the way everyone else does. You’ve been called to function by divine principles. That means you don’t panic when things go wrong; you respond with faith. The life in you is the life of a victor. You were born to reign, even in your classroom, on your campus, in your workplace, and among your peers. When someone says, “There’s no way you can pass that,” or “You’ll never make it,” don’t be discouraged. Get excited! That’s your opportunity to put your faith to work. Pray. Declare God’s Word over your situation.

Speak life instead of fear. Say, “The greater One lives in me. I’m an overcomer. I can do all things through Christ!” God loves to see you stand strong. The Bible says His wisdom is revealed through us. Every time you refuse to give up, every time you choose faith over fear, you’re showing the world—and even the spiritual realm—that the power of God is real and active in your life.

Remember, the inherent dynamic ability to turn hopeless situations around came into your life when you received the Holy Spirit. That confidence you need, that turnaround in your family or academics—it’s not out of reach. This is the set time to demonstrate the life of victory that God has brought you into. Praise God!

## Speak

I can never be disadvantaged in this life because the greater One lives in me, and He’s given me the inherent dynamic ability to change hopeless situations. I have the power and wisdom to turn every unfavourable situation around for my good, to the glory of the Father! Every challenging situation that I face is an opportunity for me to demonstrate my faith and manifest the glory of God. Hallelujah.

## Act

Look at the most challenging situation you’re facing right now. Instead of being discouraged, get excited! Say, “This is my opportunity to prove the Word of God. Greater is He that is in me! I speak change to this situation, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.”

title: The “Mimshach” Anointing
excerpt: When you study the Scriptures, you’ll discover a consistent pattern in the lives of Abraham’s physical descendants: no matter how humble their beginnings, they ended in dominion and…
scripture: “Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not spare; lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes. For you shall expand to the right and to the left...”
subtitle: (Inside of You Is The Seed Of Greatness)
prayer: Dear Lord, thank you for the Holy Spirit that causes me to grow, increase, and make progress in every area of my life. As I recognise and take advantage of the power of the Holy Spirit today, I’m making progress in my studies, developing my talents, growing in influence, and becoming all you’ve destined me to be, in the Name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, take a practical step to “enlarge your tent.” If you want to improve your grades, learn something new or develop a talent, take the next step. Sign up for a course, practise a skill, or start working towards a goal you’ve been putting off.

message:
When you study the Scriptures, you’ll discover a consistent pattern in the lives of Abraham’s physical descendants: no matter how humble their beginnings, they ended in dominion and expansion. Consider Isaac; the Bible says he “...waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great… and the Philistines envied him” (Genesis 26:13–14 Kjv). His life was a story of unstoppable increase.

If that was the testimony of the natural seed, how much more you who are the true seed of Abraham through Christ (Galatians 3:29)! The natural progression of your life is increase, advancement, and expansion in everything you do. Stagnation is inconsistent with your spiritual DNA. When you received the Holy Spirit, He’s supposed to do much more than make you speak in tongues and prophesy. He’ll cause everything you do to grow and expand. That anointing is the “mimshach” anointing, which in Hebrew means “expansion” or “to spread.” It causes everything you do to multiply and expand beyond your immediate sphere of contact.

God wants you to recognise that this grace is already at work in you. Maybe you’re in school, maybe you’re building a brand, coding an app, running a small business, creating content, or figuring out your next move; don’t despise small beginnings. That small channel can grow. That campus idea can become a company or even a conglomerate. So, start making plans for a greater and higher level at which you want to function. Glory to God!

## Prayer

Dear Lord, thank you for the Holy Spirit that causes me to grow, increase, and make progress in every area of my life. As I recognise and take advantage of the power of the Holy Spirit today, I’m making progress in my studies, developing my talents, growing in influence, and becoming all you’ve destined me to be, in the Name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.

title: Your Heavenly Father Is Big
excerpt: There are no laws in heaven or on earth against dreaming big. So, as a Christian, you’re at liberty to dream and dream big.
scripture: “Now Joseph had a dream, and he told it to his brothers; and they hated him even more.”
subtitle: (Dream Big)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: My mind is continually open to receiving new ideas. I refuse to see myself as small in life, for the God I serve is the limit-breaker! I see my greatness, my increase and my influence bursting forth on every side, in the Name of Jesus! Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Take a piece of paper and write down the biggest dream you can imagine for your life. Don’t limit yourself by your current circumstances. Make it so big that only God can accomplish it. Then, thank Him for making it happen.

message:
There are no laws in heaven or on earth against dreaming big. So, as a Christian, you’re at liberty to dream and dream big. Let your dream of success be big enough for God to get involved with it. That’s why I love the man Joseph in the Bible. As a young lad, his dreams were out of this world! He was basically a teenager talking about leadership and influence while still living under his father’s roof. Though his brothers hated him for all his extraordinary dreams of greatness, he kept on dreaming and telling them about his dreams.

A teenager with a big dream can attract God’s attention. That’s why even in prison, Joseph kept rising to the top. He eventually became the prime minister of Egypt and preserved both Egypt and several other nations from famine. It’s time for you to dream and dream big. It’s a decision you must make. Dream big about your academics, your creative gifts, your tech ideas, your ministry, your influence.

Stretch your vision. Refuse to put your mind to sleep; keep dreaming! See yourself doing big things. Have a different way of thinking. Your Heavenly Father is big, and His resources are limitless. Not only is He able to cause your visions of success to come to pass, but He’s also more willing and enthusiastic about your success than you could ever be. Glory to God!

## Speak

My mind is continually open to receiving new ideas. I refuse to see myself as small in life, for the God I serve is the limit-breaker! I see my greatness, my increase and my influence bursting forth on every side, in the Name of Jesus! Amen.

title: Commit to the Upward and Forward Life

excerpt: As a child of God, your journey is meant to be one of continual advancement. The Bible gives us the example of Isaac, a man who refused to settle for the easy or convenient path.
scripture: “Then Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year a hundredfold; and the Lord blessed him. The man began to prosper, and continued prospering until he became very prosperous.”
subtitle: (Refuse To Settle For Anything Less Than God’s Best)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for leading me from success to success. I declare by the power of the Spirit that I’m making progress and moving forward in life. My success and prosperity are appearing unto all men, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
As a child of God, your journey is meant to be one of continual advancement. The Bible gives us the example of Isaac, a man who refused to settle for the easy or convenient path. In a time of famine, his neighbours and friends fled to Egypt, seeking security and abundance. Yet, God instructed Isaac to remain in Gerar, the very land facing scarcity, and to sow there.

Isaac obeyed, and the results were extraordinary. The Scripture says, “The man got richer and richer by the day until he was very wealthy. He accumulated flocks and herds and many, many servants, so much so that the Philistines began to envy him” (Genesis 26:13-14 MSG). His obedience produced unmatched growth, proving that God’s direction always leads to progress, regardless of how circumstances may appear. Even when things look dry, competitive, or unfair around you, God can still make you thrive right there.

This is your call today: to listen to the Spirit of God. Where He directs you, go. What He commands you, do. When you align your steps with His guidance, your life, like Isaac’s, will be marked by unending growth and overflowing blessings. Famine, opposition, or scarcity can’t hinder God’s plan for your advancement: No tough exams, limited resources, or difficult background can hinder God’s plan for your advancement. None of these things can.

Let today be the day you commit to the upward and forward life. Refuse to settle for anything less than God’s best. Don’t shrink your dreams to fit your current situation. Obey, move in His direction, and watch as your life becomes a testimony of continual progress, prosperity, and divine favour. Your story is not one of lack; it’s a story of becoming very great.

body:
As Lisa and Jordan chatted after school, they came across an astonishing headline on Jordan’s tablet.

“Did you see this?” Lisa asked, her eyes widening. “A fifteen-year-old just graduated top of their class in mathematics in the UK!”

Jordan shook his head in disbelief: “Fifteen? That’s... unbelievable! How’s that even possible?”

Lisa smiled: “You know, it made me think... if God can do that, what can’t He do through us?”

“What if the kid didn’t believe in God?” you may ask. Well, in our opening scripture above, Jesus addressed a group of people and told them nothing shall be impossible to them. This group of people weren’t Christians at the time; no one could have been born again since Jesus hadn’t died and risen from the dead. Now, if people who didn’t have eternal life were being told by Jesus that they could use their faith for anything, what about you who are born again, having the life and nature of God in you?

It therefore means there’s no limit to how much you can achieve in life! You’ve been called to a life of unending success, triumph and prosperity. You have the supernatural ability to do exploits because you’re filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8). Failure, defeat and the down-life shouldn’t be part of your life. All you need is to be conscious of God’s ability in you. Notice that the Lord Jesus didn’t say, “And nothing shall be impossible unto God;” rather, He said, “Nothing shall be impossible unto you.”

Think about it: if nothing is impossible to you, it means you can do anything and be everything God has planned for you to be. So, when obstacles appear, don’t shrink back in fear or despair. It doesn’t matter the strength of your adversaries; refuse to cower or be intimidated. Remember, the power of God in you is greater than any problem before you. Go on and win today. Glory to God!

## Speak

I’m a winner in everything I do. There’s nothing I can’t handle because God’s own strength is working inside me. I’m done with focusing on what’s stopping me or letting obstacles get in my head; my path is set for success, victory, and big things. I can literally do all things through Christ, because He’s the one giving me the power to crush my goals.

## Act

Identify one “mountain” in your life—something that seems impossible; don’t just pray about it; speak to it. Say, “Mountain, be removed! I’m not limited by you. Nothing is impossible to me!”

subtitle: (Enjoy the Fullness of God’s Blessings)

message:
Imagine you had a wealthy relative you’d never met. You spent years writing letters, asking them to please send you some money, hoping one day they might answer. Then, one day, a lawyer showed up at your door and informed you that the relative had passed away years ago, and you were the sole heir to the entire fortune. You were already rich and didn’t know it. That’s the moment you start living in your inheritance!

Isn’t it amazing to know that the fullness of God’s blessings already belongs to you? Not “when I’m older,” not “after I’ve figured my life out.” Right now. Somebody said, “I’ve been praying to God to bless me.” But you see, that’s actually not the best way to think about it. God has already blessed you way beyond what you can imagine! He’s already given you ALL spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ Jesus, not just a few.

The Bible says you were called to inherit a blessing (1 Peter 3:9); you were born into God’s blessing because you’re part of Abraham’s family. God told Abraham, “I will make you a great nation; I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing” (Genesis 12:2). That promise wasn’t just for Abraham; it’s for you too (Galatians 3:16). So, not only are you blessed, you’re meant to be a blessing to others.

In your school, your friend group, your online space, you carry something valuable. Decide today to live like the person God created you to be. You’re full of His blessings. There’s nothing in this world or heaven that you need to beg for, because everything belongs to you (1 Corinthians 3:21). Your life should overflow with good things so that others who come in contact with you can partake of the goodness of God in your life. Praise God!

message:
A young man once asked me, “How come many scientists have invented a lot of things for the world to enjoy, and Christians haven’t done anything?” The young man asked an intelligent question, but the mistake he made was that he saw Christians as one group and scientists as another group; he never thought of the fact that many scientists are Christians.

There’s no telling what a Christian who has received the Holy Spirit can achieve. He has the greatest Teacher living inside him, and there’s absolutely no subject in life He’s deficient in. As one who’s filled with the Holy Spirit, you have knowledge of witty inventions, for the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of wisdom. Therefore, you’ve got to blaze new trails and chart new frontiers in different fields of human endeavour.

The Holy Spirit living in you is your unparalleled advantage to be a trailblazer. He can grant you insights into fields that haven’t even been discovered yet! You can be the first to discover the cure for cancer, HIV/AIDS, and other medically incurable ailments. The world is looking for problem-solvers who’ll make new discoveries that’ll permanently solve the many social, political, and economic ills that are plaguing the world today. Don’t let your imagination go to sleep. Put the wisdom of God that’s functioning in you to work, and become a creator. Become an inventor. It’s time to break new grounds.

title: There’s Abundance of Grace
excerpt: Imagine standing at the edge of a river overflowing its banks, the waters rushing with abundance. You can either satisfy your thirst right there, or remain thirsty.
scripture: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.”
subtitle: (Take A Hold Of God’s Grace)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for your grace, which you’ve lavishly poured out upon me. Thank you for the gift of righteousness that gives me the boldness in your presence and causes me to reign in life as a king, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, consciously take hold of God’s abundant grace. Declare that you reign in life and act with this consciousness throughout the day.

message:
Imagine standing at the edge of a river overflowing its banks, the waters rushing with abundance. You can either satisfy your thirst right there, or remain thirsty. This is the picture of God’s grace in your life: not a trickle, but an overflowing abundance waiting for you to receive it fully. According to our opening verse above, the Apostle Paul didn’t say, “…they which receive grace,” but he emphasised, “...they which receive abundance of grace”. Abundance brings to mind a cup running over, a blessing so full it can’t be contained.

This overflowing grace is what equips you to reign in life—to walk in victory, power, and divine authority. But notice the word “receive.” It’s from the Greek “lambano,” meaning to take, seize, or make yours. It’s not a passive act. Grace doesn’t automatically manifest in your life without engagement. Just as the woman with the issue of blood reached out in faith and received healing from Jesus by touching His garment (Mark 5:29), you too must actively reach out and take hold of God’s grace. Those who don’t believe or act receive nothing.

This is your set time to reign in life. God has lavishly poured out His grace on you (Titus 2:11). Whatever you need—be it tuition fees, finances or resources to start a project—it’s already available. The question is: will you seize it? Remember, God has ordained you to reign as a king in life. This is your season to manifest His glory, walk in victory, and rise above every challenge.

## Prayer

Dear Father, I thank you for your grace, which you’ve lavishly poured out upon me. Thank you for the gift of righteousness that gives me the boldness in your presence and causes me to reign in life as a king, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: Your Set Time to Rejoice
excerpt: In sports, coaches often teach athletes to smile or celebrate after a mistake or during physical exhaustion.
scripture: “Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say, rejoice!”
subtitle: (The Joy Of The Lord Is Your Strength)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I declare that the joy of the Lord is my strength, and that joy saturates my spirit and bursts forth in refreshing streams of rejoicing. I rejoice always in the Lord my God, who has filled my heart with gladness and my mouth with songs of rejoicing.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, set aside five minutes for a laughing session. Find a quiet place; meditate on all the good things God has done for you, and just start laughing. Laugh at the devil. Laugh at the challenges.

message:
In sports, coaches often teach athletes to smile or celebrate after a mistake or during physical exhaustion. This isn’t because the situation is funny, but because the physical act of celebrating can help interrupt the cycle of panic and fatigue. It gives them the strength to finish the race. There is a profound spiritual truth here: celebrating before the victory appears is actually a source of supernatural strength.

You may say, “What if the circumstances of my life aren’t such that should give room for rejoicing? What if school feels overwhelming? What if my friends misunderstand me, my grades drop, or things at home feel tense? How am I supposed to rejoice then?” That’s precisely the time to rejoice! Yes, your joy is independent of circumstances; it’s rooted in your spirit. It’s a supernatural delight that persists even when the storms rage. When faith is challenged, that’s the perfect moment to celebrate. The Bible says, “...with joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation” (Isaiah 12:3).

“Salvation” is an all-encompassing word; it refers to soundness, preservation, divine health, success, prosperity, and every blessing that the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus Christ consummated for the Christian. In other words, God wants you to know that you must keep your joy afloat to experience the wonderful blessings of salvation. So, even when exams are tough, peer pressure is loud, or the future feels unclear, you can still stand strong inside. Learn to maintain a joyful spirit even in the midst of daunting and trying circumstances, for the joy of the Lord is your strength(Nehemiah 8:10). Glory to God!

## Speak

I declare that the joy of the Lord is my strength, and that joy saturates my spirit and bursts forth in refreshing streams of rejoicing. I rejoice always in the Lord my God, who has filled my heart with gladness and my mouth with songs of rejoicing.
body:
In sports, coaches often teach athletes to smile or celebrate after a mistake or during physical exhaustion. This isn’t because the situation is funny, but because the physical act of celebrating can help interrupt the cycle of panic and fatigue. It gives them the strength to finish the race. There is a profound spiritual truth here: celebrating before the victory appears is actually a source of supernatural strength.

You may say, “What if the circumstances of my life aren’t such that should give room for rejoicing? What if school feels overwhelming? What if my friends misunderstand me, my grades drop, or things at home feel tense? How am I supposed to rejoice then?” That’s precisely the time to rejoice! Yes, your joy is independent of circumstances; it’s rooted in your spirit. It’s a supernatural delight that persists even when the storms rage. When faith is challenged, that’s the perfect moment to celebrate. The Bible says, “...with joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation” (Isaiah 12:3).

“Salvation” is an all-encompassing word; it refers to soundness, preservation, divine health, success, prosperity, and every blessing that the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus Christ consummated for the Christian. In other words, God wants you to know that you must keep your joy afloat to experience the wonderful blessings of salvation. So, even when exams are tough, peer pressure is loud, or the future feels unclear, you can still stand strong inside. Learn to maintain a joyful spirit even in the midst of daunting and trying circumstances, for the joy of the Lord is your strength(Nehemiah 8:10). Glory to God!

## Speak

I declare that the joy of the Lord is my strength, and that joy saturates my spirit and bursts forth in refreshing streams of rejoicing. I rejoice always in the Lord my God, who has filled my heart with gladness and my mouth with songs of rejoicing.

## Act

Today, set aside five minutes for a laughing session. Find a quiet place; meditate on all the good things God has done for you, and just start laughing. Laugh at the devil. Laugh at the challenges.

## Further Study

1 Thessalonians 5:16; Philippians 3:1

We’re in a day where there’s increased angelic activity upon the earth because the second coming of the Master is at hand. His work of salvation must be carried out with more urgency and fervency than ever before.

title: Become Visionary
excerpt: Imagine a world where everyone asked, “How can I make a difference today?” What a beautiful place it would be!
scripture: “Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”
subtitle: (Make A Difference In The World)
prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, I thank you for giving me the inspiration, motivation and ability to conceive and execute divine ideas that’ll make the world a better place. I recognise that this is my season and set time to make a difference in the world; therefore, by the power of the Spirit, I’m impacting the world with the investment of my personality! Thank you for making me a blesser and a giver, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Look around your immediate environment: your home, your school, your neighbourhood; identify one problem, big or small, and take a step towards solving it. Offer help, share an idea, or lend a hand.

message:
Imagine a world where everyone asked, “How can I make a difference today?” What a beautiful place it would be! Often, we think success is about what we can gain, but true success is measured by what we give. It’s about leaving the world better than we found it. The world needs visionaries: young people who will step out from the crowd, find a need, and reach out to meet that need. That’s one of the principles of success—when you’re challenged to make things better than the way you met them.

Instead of being the one asking for help and waiting for others to give to you, you should become the helper! Become the one to meet other people’s needs. Be the blesser and the giver, for that’s your calling. The Bible shows us that Joseph stood out in his day and saved the entire nation of Egypt from starvation during a time of famine (Genesis 41:55). Think about your school, your group of friends, or your community; maybe someone is being bullied, struggling with school, or just needs a friend; you don’t have to solve the world’s problems first; you can start small.

This is your set time to make a difference in your world. The world ought to be a better place because you came. And you know what? It begins with being passionate about a God-idea and having the courage to implement that idea once you receive it from God. It doesn’t matter how small the idea may seem; once you have it, run with it. Before long, God will expand your vision and increase your inspiration! He’ll grant you the motivation and the ability to conceive and execute more ideas that’ll impact the world and make it a better place. Wake up to that calling today. Praise God!

title: Not “Sickable”
excerpt: God’s greatest wish is for you to prosper and live in health.
scripture: “Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.”
subtitle: (Walk In Divine Health)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I’m a new creation in Christ Jesus, born in Zion, where sickness doesn’t have a foothold. The life of God inundates every fibre of my being, making me impregnable to sickness and disease. From the crown of my head to the soles of my feet, eternal life gains the ascendancy! I walk in divine health every day because my body is the temple of the Holy Ghost. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Act
extras.text: If any symptom tries to hold you down, don’t confess it. Instead, place your hand on that part of your body and say, “My body is the temple of the Holy Ghost. I command you to line up with the Word. I walk in divine health.”

message:
God’s greatest wish is for you to prosper and live in health. Now, notice in the scripture above, that God didn’t say, “Beloved, I wish above all things that you may prosper and be healed....” Rather, He said, “…that you may prosper and be in health.” He’s talking about you living in divine health, not just getting healed. Healing is good; it’s the children’s bread, but walking in divine health is even better. When you’re living in divine health, you don’t need healing because you just don’t get sick.

To some, this sounds impossible because they think everyone gets sick eventually. But that’s not how life in Christ works. His death, burial, and resurrection made it possible for us to live sickness-free. As you grow in Christ, don’t settle for getting healed; live in health every day. This is the life of the new creation in Christ Jesus; old things (including sickness) have passed away!

This is why the Bible says, “...The inhabitant will not say, “I am sick...’” (Isaiah 33:24). The city the prophet talks about is Zion, the city of the living God, and you became part of Zion the moment you were born again (Hebrews 12:22-23). The reason the inhabitants of Zion don’t say they’re sick isn’t that they’re careful with their words; it’s because they literally don’t get sick. They’re not “sickable”! Eternal life inside them destroys sickness, repels disease, and cancels infirmity.

So, erase “sickness talk” from your vocabulary. Someone might ask, “But what if I feel sick, can’t I just say how I feel?” The answer is no; say what God says, not what you feel. We live by faith, not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7). Symptoms aren’t proof that you’re sick. When you keep speaking faith-filled words, your body becomes resistant to every form of disease. Walking in divine health is your birthright, and as a teenager, you can enjoy and walk in it now. Glory to God!

title: “Laughing Sessions”
excerpt: Psychologists have identified a common trait in people who thrive despite difficult circumstances.
scripture: “He who sits in the heavens shall laugh; the Lord shall hold them in derision.”
subtitle: (Laugh Your Way To Victory)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I’m laughing my way through life, from victory to victory and from glory to glory! I laugh at the devil and challenging circumstances because I know I can never be disadvantaged. I’m soaring high on the wings of the Spirit. My mouth is filled today with laughter and my tongue with the songs of triumph, in Jesus’ mighty Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Have a laughing session today.

message:
Psychologists have identified a common trait in people who thrive despite difficult circumstances. It’s called “cognitive reframing”—the ability to find humour or perspective in hard situations. They aren’t pretending problems don’t exist; they’ve simply learnt that how you interpret an event shapes how that event affects you.

The Bible reveals an even more powerful truth: when you see your circumstances through the eyes of God’s Word, you can respond with joy instead of fear. That’s why Proverbs 17:22 declares that “A merry heart does good, like medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones.” Why wouldn’t you laugh when you know that you’re more than a conqueror? Why shouldn’t you laugh when you know that all things work together for your good?

Refuse to allow circumstances dictate your happiness. It doesn’t matter what comes against you in life; learn to laugh your way to victory. Unsatisfactory grades, drama with friends, online pressure, family issues—none of these get to decide your joy. The opening scripture shows us that God laughs at the ranting of His enemies. Like your Heavenly Father, learn to laugh the enemy to scorn when he starts throwing his tantrums at you. When tough times come, that’s the time to laugh, for there’s absolutely nothing the enemy could do to harm you.

No wonder the Apostle James admonished that you “… count it all joy when you fall into various trials” (James 1:2). If you’ve been facing trying times, I recommend to you “Laughing sessions.” Sit all by yourself and meditate on the victorious life Christ has brought you into, and begin to laugh! At first, you might even look ridiculous to yourself, but keep at it. It won’t be long before you’ll find yourself declaring the Word of God that’ll change everything. Glory, Hallelujah!

title: Only Believe
excerpt: A man came to Jesus one day to ask the Master to heal his demon-possessed son. The man said to Jesus, “If You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us” (Mark 9:22b).
scripture: “And when He had come into the house, the blind men came to Him. And Jesus said to them, ‘Do you believe that I am able to do this?’ They said to Him, ‘Yes, Lord.’“
subtitle: (Cast Yourself On His Word)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for giving me a heart that can believe. My hope and my faith rest completely in your Word, because it’s the only sure foundation. I believe that everything your Word has said concerning me is true, dependable, and sure, and I cast myself wholly upon your Word, knowing that my future is secure in you, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Take a moment to speak in tongues and make faith-filled confessions of the Word concerning a particular matter in your heart.

message:
A man came to Jesus one day to ask the Master to heal his demon-possessed son. The man said to Jesus, “If You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us” (Mark 9:22b). The Master replied, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes” (Mark 9:23). Finally, the man blurted out, “Lord, I believe; help my unbelief” (Mark 9:24)! He was trying to put the responsibility for his believing on Jesus, which shouldn’t be. The Lord, nonetheless, compassionately healed the boy.

Many people are like that man today. They think that if they’re unbelieving, it’s up to God to help them believe, but it’s not so. The Bible says, “…with the heart one believes unto righteousness...” (Romans 10:10). You believe with your heart. This means that believing is a choice, which is entirely up to you; it’s your responsibility to believe. God isn’t the one to make you believe His Word. You’re the one to choose to believe His Word, and when you do, you’ll see His glory in your life (John 11:40).

God is looking for someone who can believe! Every time He locates such a person, He does mighty things in his life. Abraham believed God and received a son in his old age. Moses believed God and led more than six million Jews through the midst of the Red Sea. He’s looking for those who can stake their lives on His Word.

Make a choice today to believe; cast yourself on His Word, trusting that everything the Lord has said is true. Your dreams—whether it’s getting into the right school, acquiring a scholarship, or becoming who God has called you to be— are possible if only you can believe. Praise God!
