title: It’s More Blessed to Give
excerpt: The Lord Jesus made it clear that it’s not how much you receive and amass that measures your value. Rather, you measure your value or worth by how much you give.
scripture: “And He said to them, ‘Take heed and beware of covetousness, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses.’“
subtitle: (Make Up Your Mind To Be A Giver)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for granting me the grace and wisdom to be a consistent giver. I declare that I’m a big-time giver and financier of the Gospel. I thank you for always multiplying my seeds sown and increasing my ability to give even more, in Jesus’ Name. Amen!

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, choose one thing you value—your time, your money, your talent, or something you own—and intentionally give it as a seed.

message:
The Lord Jesus made it clear that it’s not how much you receive and amass that measures your value. Rather, you measure your value or worth by how much you give. No wonder the Apostle Paul, reiterating the words of the Master, declared that “...it is more blessed to give than to receive” (Acts 20:35). As far as God is concerned, the one who gives is greater than the one who receives. Thus, it’s not how much you have in your bank account that determines your worth; rather, it’s how much you give.

The only way to conquer anything, be it money or some other material possession, is by giving it. That means it’s not about how many sneakers you own, how much allowance you get, or how many gadgets you have; if you can’t give it, you don’t really have control over it; it has control over you. If you ever find that you’re unable to give something you possess, it means you haven’t conquered that thing yet. But when you’re able to exercise your faith and give it, you’ve conquered that level, and immediately, God promotes you to a higher level of giving.

Learn to be a giver. Nothing of this world should have a hold over you to the point that you can’t give it. The Lord Jesus said, “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be put into your bosom. For with the same measure that you use, it will be measured back to you” (Luke 6:38). That means the giver has a promise; a guarantee that he’ll only move upward and forward in life. But for the receiver, there’s no promise.

Therefore, make up your mind to be a giver. Decide now—even as a teenager—that you’ll be known as someone who gives generously, not just someone who always wants more. As you learn to release, God will multiply your seeds sown and increase your ability, such that you’ll keep getting greater and greater.

message:
“Do you ever feel like you’re just… ordinary?” Khloe asked, frowning.

“Ordinary? Not at all,” replied Johnny. “God has put special abilities in you that no one else can express the way only you can.”

Khloe looked puzzled: “Special abilities? Me? I’ve never really thought of myself that way.”

“That’s exactly why you need to hear this,” Johnny said with a smile. “No one was ever like you; no one is like you, and no one will ever be like you. You’re the only one of you that God has. So, be the best of you.”

The Living Bible translation renders our opening scripture this way: “However, Christ has given each of us special abilities; whatever He wants us to have out of His rich storehouse of gifts.” I like that term, “special abilities,” for it lets us know that there’s not a single one of God’s children that’s lacking in ability. You may never have thought about the fact that God has given you special abilities, but let it dawn on you today that there are special abilities in you which came into your life when you were born again and received the Holy Spirit.

The Living Bible translation renders our opening scripture this way: “However, Christ has given each of us special abilities; whatever He wants us to have out of His rich storehouse of gifts.” I like that term, “special abilities,” for it lets us know that there’s not a single one of God’s children that’s lacking in ability. You may never have thought about the fact that God has given you special abilities, but let it dawn on you today that there are special abilities in you which came into your life when you were born again and received the Holy Spirit.

The Bible says, “But you shall receive power (ability, efficiency, and might) when the Holy Spirit has come upon you” (Acts 1:8 AMP). What you need do is recognise and agree with what the Word says; tell yourself, “God has given me special abilities, and I’m putting these abilities to work in my life.”

Remember that God doesn’t have a duplicate of you; He’s deposited in you gifts and abilities that set you apart and make you unique. What a wonderful blessing! You can express the beauty of God from your spirit in a way that no one else can. So, next time you feel like you’re just “another face in the crowd” at school or on social media, remember: God made you with a one-of-a-kind mix of abilities that no one else has. Stop comparing your story to someone else’s story!

Never look at yourself and think there’s nothing special about you. God has given you special abilities, and it’s up to you to let them show and make an impact in the Kingdom of God.

## Prayer

I thank you, Father, for depositing within my spirit special abilities according to the measure of the gift of Christ. No task or endeavour is beyond me, for I have in me the grace and supernatural ability I require for every task, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:

Today, the world—living and non-living—is crying out for freedom. People struggle with sickness, poverty, and failures; even resources are misused.

The sons of God are the world’s only hope. The Scripture says all creation is waiting for the manifestation of the “sons” of God—the mature followers of Christ who know how to stand strong and make a difference, even as teens! These mature sons know how to overcome sickness, lack, and obstacles, and bring hope to others.

Make up your mind not to remain in the babyhood stage of Christianity. Grow to maturity because the world is waiting for you! God wants to deliver great things to His mature sons and daughters, for He knows they can handle responsibilities.

Take your Christian growth very seriously. It’s only in the position of maturity in Christ that you can take your place as the “huios” (mature son) of God and bring deliverance, healing, salvation, and joy to a hurting world.

message:
Dr David Yonggi Cho once told a story about how, as a young preacher, he tried to spice up his sermons with philosophy to show the people how learned he was. After the service, he met an elderly man who happened to be a Professor of philosophy. All the while he thought he impressed the congregation, the elderly man wasn’t impressed. He advised the young preacher to stop trying to impress anyone with his “elementary” philosophy. Pastor Cho, though unhappy about the rebuke, made up his mind to specialise in the Bible.

That’s what I made up my mind a long time ago to do, and I encourage you to do the same. Even if you’re amazing at sports, gaming, music, or school, make sure you’re also a “Word Specialist.” Get to know God by studying the Word, and let it be your go-to guide no matter where you are. Memorise the Scriptures.

To experience true and lasting success in life, the Word of God is what you need: “This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success” (Joshua 1:8). God’s Word will make you an all-round success, including your academics.

It doesn’t matter how smart you are in school or how talented you are at anything else; what really matters is becoming an expert in God’s Word. Keep learning it, living it, and letting it guide your choices. That’s how you’ll manifest success in life.

message:
Filters are designed to allow only the good parts of a solution or mixture pass through, while the undesirable parts are caught and held back. That’s the same principle the Spirit of God shows us in our opening scripture. Your mind is the door to your spirit, and whatever thoughts or words you allow through will shape your spirit. That’s why you need to screen and filter what enters your heart.

Every day, we hear and see all kinds of information, positive and negative. You need a spiritual filter: guard your heart and refuse to process anything that doesn’t line up with God’s Word. For example, if someone says, “Life is impossible for teens like us,” or you hear bad news about the economy, don’t let those words define you. Remind yourself: “God has great plans for me, and I walk in His blessings.”

Use the Word of God as your filter to stop wrong thoughts from taking root in your heart. Whatever life you’re living now comes from your thoughts and words. The Bible says, “And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind….” (Romans 12:2). Transformation starts with your thought patterns. Reject fear, lack, or negativity. Instead, focus on success in school, relationships, talents, and joy that comes from God’s Word.

Choose thoughts of victory, health, prosperity, happiness, and fulfilment—whatever aligns with God’s Word. Every time you scroll, watch a video, or listen to someone, ask: “Does this encourage God’s truth or plant fear?” Let His Word guide what you accept. Keep vigilant watch over your heart because what you allow in will shape who you become.

excerpt: Imagine a master artist who spends a years creating a breathtaking masterpiece. If a speck of dust falls on the canvas, does the artist destroy the painting? No!
scripture: “And we have known and believed the love that God has for us. God is love...”
subtitle: (He’s Not Looking To Condemn You)
prayer: Dear Father, I rejoice for the great love wherewith you’ve loved me, and I’m grateful for your grace and tender mercies that encompass me each day. Through your Spirit, I’m able to comprehend the magnitude of your love, and to take advantage of it each day in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
Imagine a master artist who spends a years creating a breathtaking masterpiece. If a speck of dust falls on the canvas, does the artist destroy the painting? No! He gently brushes it away because the flaw never outweighs the value of what he made.

Rest in God’s love. Quit all struggles and take advantage of God’s unfeigned and unconditional love for you. Even if life feels messy, maybe you’ve messed up or feel far from God, He’s still saying, “Rest in my love!” All you need do is repent and receive forgiveness. Once you do that, He’s quick to forgive you because it’s His nature to forgive.

The father of the prodigal son killed the best calf to celebrate his son’s return (Luke 15:21-23), showing God as an ever-forgiving and loving Father. He rejoices when His straying child returns. If you’ve been ignoring God or feeling distant, it’s time to come back. He’s waiting with open arms, not anger. He already took the hit for you through Jesus. All He wants is for you to rest in His love.

Let nothing separate you from God’s love, not even your mistakes. When you receive forgiveness, God receives you and sets you back on the right path. Confidence in God’s love grows as you spend time with Him—talking, studying the Word, acknowledging His work in your life. The more you know Him, the more joy and peace you’ll feel, even in chaos. His love follows you everywhere. So, rest in His love today. He doesn’t look to punish you; He wants to embrace you.

message:
When God arises in a person’s life, all enemies are scattered, and all that hate Him flee in terror! But how does God arise in your life? Is it just by praying, “O God, arise; defeat my enemies”? What you do matters. Firstly, notice the words “Let God arise”; that’s another way of saying, “Allow God to arise.” It’s your choice to let Him move in your life. Since God and His Word are one: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1), giving His Word first place in your life lets Him arise.

God doesn’t need to part the heavens to work in you; He already lives inside you. As you meditate on His Word and speak in tongues, His Word stirs in your spirit. That’s God arising in you! Then speak that Word as a prophecy. No enemy can resist it. When life throws challenges—like school stress, peer pressure, or feeling left out—don’t just feel stuck. Stir God’s Word in your spirit and speak it out. Say, “I’ve got the power of God in me! I’m stronger than any challenge! I’m set up for success, happiness, and peace!” Doing this makes fear, doubt, and negativity back off.

Keep declaring: “I have the life of God in me! I can never be poor! Prosperity, health, and goodness are my birthright!” As you do, poverty, sickness, lack, and failure will flee. Your faith in God through His Word will rise like a giant and defeat every enemy in your life.

title: Freedom’s True Purpose
excerpt: When you were born again, you were born into a life of absolute liberty in Christ. You became free to live, free to serve God, free to reign and free to love.
scripture: “For you, brethren, have been called to liberty; only do not use liberty as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.”
subtitle: (Serving, Not Indulging)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the liberty you’ve given me in Christ Jesus, to be everything that you desire for me to be and to have everything you desire for me to have. I declare that I’m free to serve you, love you, and reign in life as a king. I ask that you help me, through your Word, to take full advantage of my liberty in Christ, while I do only those things that bring glory to you and edify the Church, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Do something today to help at home or for your friends, without being asked, and without complaining.

message:
When you were born again, you were born into a life of absolute liberty in Christ. You became free to live, free to serve God, free to reign and free to love. However, as Christians, the Bible admonishes that we use our liberty in Christ rightly. Under the Old Testament, they could read the commandments to know what to do and what not to do, but the new creation man wasn’t given any law to obey: “knowing this: that the law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and for sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers” (1 Timothy 1:9).

According to the Bible, it’s difficult to impute sin where there’s no law (Romans 4:15). Some young Christians are in a dilemma because they’ve been brought into a life without a list of religious rules. So, they might think, “I’m free; so I can do whatever I want and get away with it.” The Bible says, ”as free, yet not using liberty as a cloak for vice, but as bondservants of God” (1 Peter 2:16).

The life you live as a child of God should be to the praise and glory of God in all things. Though it’s absolutely clear that God has called you to a free life, only make sure that you don’t use this freedom as an excuse to do whatever you want to do and destroy your freedom. Rather, use your freedom to serve one another in love; that’s how freedom grows (Galatians 5:13).

Use your liberty in Christ rightly by doing only those things that please the Father; and the way to please the Father is to walk by faith, which, by extension, is to walk according to the provisions of God’s Word. Yes, God isn’t imposing rules and regulations on us like a strict principal with a rulebook; He’s given us His Word as a guide. But be sure to use your liberty to the praise and glory of His Name.

title: Faith Is a Verb
excerpt: Faith, the Bible says, is the substance of what you hoped for, and the title-deed of unseen realities.
scripture: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”
subtitle: (Act Like You’ve Already Received)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: My faith is producing results; I don’t waver or stagger at the Word of God through unbelief. I believe that God is who He says He is, and that I have what He says I have, and I can do what He says I can do. My faith is the victory that overcomes the world. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Take one physical step today that proves you believe your prayer is already answered. If you’ve prayed for a new opportunity, clear your schedule for it or prepare the “outfit” you’ll wear for that success.

message:
Faith, the Bible says, is the substance of what you hoped for, and the title-deed of unseen realities. In other words, faith means that the things you were hoping for are now your present-hour possession. This is where the demonstration of faith comes to play. If it’s true that what you hoped for is now yours, then you ought to act that way. For example, you might have prayed to God for something concerning yourself, believing He’d do it.

If you truly believe that God heard your prayer, then you shouldn’t come back tomorrow and pray about the same thing again. You should now begin to act like someone who has received from God: that’s how to put your faith to work. That’s what Marcus’ Dad is saying in the opening conversation.

When Peter and John met the crippled man at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, Peter said to the man, “Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6). Peter then grabbed the man by the hand, and lifted him. The Bible says, “So he, leaping up, stood and walked and entered the temple with them—walking, leaping, and praising God” (Acts 3:8).

The man didn’t try to test whether he could stand up; he jumped up! That’s a demonstration of faith. He believed he’d been healed, and he immediately acted that way, and he began to walk instantly. Understand that faith is active and not passive; faith acts now because it’s taken possession. That’s why the Bible says, ”… faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead” (James 2:17). That means faith without corresponding actions is dead. The faith that works is when you believe that what God says are yours are yours, and then you act accordingly.

Someone offers you a choice: they could deposit a million dollars into your bank account right now, OR they could give you the wisdom to know how to create, manage, and multiply wealth for your entire life. Which would you pick? The Million Dollars or Wisdom?

Are you still thinking which one to go for? The principal thing you need for success in life is divine wisdom. Yes. David knew this, and he admonished his son Solomon on the importance of pricing wisdom over riches. He said, “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding” (Proverbs 4:7). He had known from his walk with God that wisdom was the key thing in life, and he passed that on to his son Solomon. It was no surprise, therefore, that when God asked Solomon what he wanted Him to do for him (1 Kings 3:5), Solomon said, “Therefore give to Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people, that I may discern between good and evil...” (1 Kings 3:9). In other words, he asked for wisdom.

The Lord’s response to Solomon’s request was remarkable, He said, ”Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked long life for yourself, nor have asked riches for yourself, nor have asked the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice, behold, I have done according to your words; see, I have given you a wise and understanding heart... And I have also given you what you have not asked: both riches and honor, so that there shall not be anyone like you among the kings all your days” (1 Kings 3:11-13). For choosing wisdom, rather than riches, Solomon became the wealthiest man who lived until Jesus. Why? Because wisdom will deliver riches to you!

As you imbibe God’s Word into you, not only will you find yourself dealing wisely in the affairs of life (like choosing the right friends, handling pressure at school, or making good decisions), but wealth and riches beyond your comprehension will be delivered into your hands! You wouldn’t have to ask or pray for them. Don’t pursue money, fame or material possessions. Go for wisdom!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for filling my heart with your wisdom. As I study and meditate on your Word, your wisdom saturates my heart, causing me to deal wisely in the affairs of life. I declare that I’m increasing in my expression of divine wisdom; that wisdom is in my heart and in my mouth always, in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

## Act

Before making any choice today, no matter how small, stop and ask: “What would wisdom do here?” Then act accordingly.

Proverbs 16:16; Proverbs 23:23

message:

He didn’t say, “I have a light for the world,” or “I know of a special light somewhere for the world.” He said, “I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life”. Period.

John described Him as “...the true Light which gives light to every man coming into the world” (John 1:9). There are other lights in the world, but Jesus is the true light! As long as you’ve received Him into your heart and follow Him, you’ll never again walk in darkness. Why is that? It’s because the true light now shines from within you.

Now, what’s light? Light is that which describes; in other words, it shows you what exists. If you entered a pitch-darkroom with no flicker of light, even though that room may be beautifully adorned with state-of-the-art décor, furniture, and electronic gadgets, it would be impossible for you to see and appreciate their beauty. That’s because there’s no light describing or showing you the things present in that room.

In the same way, young people who don’t have Jesus in their lives can’t know what true success, fulfilment, peace and prosperity are. Such people grope in darkness, and in utter hopelessness—journeying aimlessly, with a ticket to nowhere. Restless will they be until they find their rest in Christ Jesus, who is the True Light that lights every man. He’ll light your life with success, peace, health, joy, and prosperity. Glory to God!

scripture: “And do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation; but be filled with the Spirit.”

message:
Reading our opening verse above in the Amplified Classic makes it clearer; it says, “And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery; but ever be filled and stimulated with the [Holy] Spirit.” The fact that you’ve received the Holy Spirit doesn’t mean you’re always filled with the Spirit. To be filled with the Spirit doesn’t mean you’ve lost your mind, as some people think! It means you’re functioning under the control and influence of the Holy Spirit twenty-four hours every day. That’s how God wants you to live.

Note that you don’t get filled with the Spirit simply because you said, “I’m now filled with the Spirit.” There are things you do that fill you with the Spirit, and they’re listed in the nineteenth verse: “speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Ephesians 5:19). This is how to be filled with the Spirit.

“Psalms” are spiritual poems sung or spoken to God in worship. “Hymns” are songs of thanksgiving and praise directed to God or about God. “Spiritual songs” are prophetic songs that come to you from the realm of the Spirit. Such songs are filled with the Word of God, and sometimes they may come to you in other tongues. Then he says to “Make melody in your heart to the Lord.” The melody might be you humming a tune to God while you walk to class or wait for the bus, but you’re getting so blessed as you sing to the Lord in your own heart!

Never leave home or embark on any endeavour without being filled with the Spirit. A good way to get yourself in the flow of the Spirit before a big day at school, preaching the Gospel, or a sports game is to start by speaking in other tongues as you get ready. Before long, the words and songs of the Spirit will well up in you. You can’t be filled with the Spirit and experience sickness, failure, or lack. Your spirit will continually be energised for victory and success every day.

subtitle: (You Can Access Knowledge Of Any Topic)
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for opening unto me the boundless storehouse of knowledge and wisdom in Christ. extras.label: Act
extras.text: Before studying or doing homework, pray in tongues for 60 seconds, then ask: “Precious Holy Spirit, thank you for showing me what I need to know.”

message:
The Bible says all of the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ, and we know that Christ in the context of the scripture above doesn’t refer to Jesus alone: “so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another” (Romans 12:5). In other words, Christ refers to the Church for which Jesus is the Head, and we’re His body. Thus, if all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid in Christ, that means nothing ought to be beyond your scope of knowledge as a child of God.

Let me give you a practical example: You might have lost something, like your earphones or a textbook, and you’ve turned your room upside down looking for it; you’ve exhausted every logical thought. But do you know that your spirit doesn’t forget? If you activate your spirit by speaking in tongues, your spirit will begin to function like a GPS! Before long, your spirit sends that signal to your mind, and you know where that thing is. Someone may ask, “Does this really work?” Emphatically, yes! The reason some of God’s people still function below their call is ignorance; they haven’t tapped into the reservoir of knowledge God has made available to them. No child of God should be in the dark about anything. Should you need insight for a school project, wisdom for a relationship, or clarity for a decision, through the agency of the Holy Spirit, you can access knowledge of any topic in the world.

Begin to practise how to relate with God’s treasure-house of knowledge through the Spirit. The next time you’re tempted to say, “I don’t know thus and thus,” stop yourself and say, “In the Name of Jesus, I have access to the treasures of wisdom and knowledge!” Then, begin to speak in tongues and let the Holy Spirit bring that knowledge home to your spirit and then to your mind, for you have access to all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Glory to God!

message:
As a child of God, you must be very definite about your commitment to Christ. The Lord Jesus made it abundantly clear that there can be no middle ground when it comes to expressing your allegiance to Him; it’s got to be all or nothing. He meant it when He said, “…whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father who is in heaven.”

Some people deny Jesus sometimes without knowing it. For example, at school, someone might mockingly ask, “Wait, are you seriously one of those “church kids’?” and to protect your social image, you might laugh it off or give a vague answer like, “I just go sometimes.” You may not know it, but you just missed a big opportunity to identify with Jesus. You ought to have boldly declared, “Yes! I follow Jesus!” Some young people hide their Bibles in their backpacks when they’re at school or with friends, so people won’t ask questions; that’s wrong. The most honourable, sublime and worthy personality you could ever be identified with is the Lord Jesus. Be proud of your association with Him and those for whom He died. Never tuck your head in shame when those who are unlearned in the things of God make derogatory remarks about Christians and what they believe. Be proud of your identity as a born-again, Spirit-filled, tongue-talking child of God.

Nothing in this world is worth clinging to at the expense of your commitment to Christ. There’s no greater honour than to belong to the Lord Jesus Christ! Stand up tall for him everywhere you are and let others know that you’re a Christian. When you do, He too will speak on your behalf.

message:
The Bible says, “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:4), meaning that there are several gifts that God imparts to His children through the agency of the Holy Spirit. But from our opening Scripture, we can decipher that the gift of prophecy ranks above all the other gifts of the Spirit that you should desire. God wants you to operate the gift of prophecy.

The gift of prophecy isn’t just for apostles, prophets, evangelists or pastors; it’s for the Church! Every Christian ought to prophesy. To prophesy is to speak forth the Word of God in power, whether by foretelling future events, or as a rhema-word to cause a change in the now! The Bible says, “But he who prophesies speaks edification and exhortation and comfort to men. He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church” (1 Corinthians 14:3-4). When you declare the mind of God in prophecy, others are edified, strengthened and comforted.

Thus, with the gift of prophecy in operation in your life, you can never be in darkness as to what steps to take in life. Whether it’s choosing which subjects to focus on, navigating friendships, or making plans for your future, prophecy can guide you. Moses, in the Old Testament, understood the power and importance of prophecy and wished that all of God’s children were prophets (Numbers 11:29). But thanks be unto God; now that we’re born again and have received the Holy Spirit, we’ve received the divine enablement and inspiration to prophesy. Hallelujah!

Consequently, whether you’re praying on your own or in the company of other Christians, you can prophesy. As the Word of God wells up in you under that influence of the Holy Spirit, open your mouth and speak forth those words in prophecy. Begin to desire the gift of prophecy. The Bible says the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man (not some but all) to profit withal (1 Corinthians 12:7). This means you, too, can prophesy, and you can begin right now!

message:
Some people are more concerned about keeping their body fit, instead of paying the most attention to exercising their spirit unto godliness. The spirit is the real man; no wonder we’re admonished in the Scripture to exercise ourselves rather unto godliness (1 Timothy 4:7).

God doesn’t want you to have a super-built body and be flabby spiritually; therefore, you must exercise your spirit! You must engage in spiritual exercise, which, unlike physical exercise, has a promise both for this life and for the life to come. So, the question then is: how do you exercise yourself spiritually? It’s simply by engaging in spiritual activities, such as going to church regularly, praying in tongues consistently, studying God’s Word and sharing it with others.

Some young people only show up to church when they feel like it or when their friends are going, and that’s not right. The church is where you’re taught God’s Word that builds your spirit and helps you navigate teenage life! It’s the place where you can connect with others your age who are also trying to grow spiritually. Keep exercising yourself unto godliness by doing those things that enhance your walk in the divine life. As you do, not only will your faith get stronger as you find yourself being built up in your knowledge of God, you’ll also deal wisely in the affairs of life. Praise God!

## Prayer

Dear Father, I thank you for showing me how to exercise and energise my spirit! I’m mightily helped to channel my energies and focus on building my spirit consistently. And as I do, I make tremendous progress in my life, and the work of the ministry is prospering in my hands, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.

You must engage in spiritual exercise, which, unlike physical exercise, has a promise both for this life and for the life to come. So, the question then is: how do you exercise yourself spiritually? It’s simply by engaging in spiritual activities, such as going to church regularly, praying in tongues consistently, studying God’s Word and sharing it with others.

Some young people only show up to church when they feel like it or when their friends are going, and that’s not right. The church is where you’re taught God’s Word that builds your spirit and helps you navigate teenage life! It’s the place where you can connect with others your age who are also trying to grow spiritually. Keep exercising yourself unto godliness by doing those things that enhance your walk in the divine life. As you do, not only will your faith get stronger as you find yourself being built up in your knowledge of God, you’ll also deal wisely in the affairs of life. Praise God!

Dear Father, I thank you for showing me how to exercise and energise my spirit! I’m mightily helped to channel my energies and focus on building my spirit consistently. And as I do, I make tremendous progress in my life, and the work of the ministry is prospering in my hands, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.

subtitle: (The Two Most Powerful Words)
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for teaching me the importance of expressing gratitude. I’ll never neglect to say, “Thank you” for the favours and kindness shown to me. message:
The words “Thank you” are two of the most powerful words you can ever say. They’re words that convey heartfelt appreciation and gratefulness, which, when rightly expressed, leave in the hearts of the recipient an indelible impression of your sincere gratitude. Sadly, some people find it difficult to say “Thank you” even when the occasion warrants it. As a Christian, it matters that you express gratitude and manifest a grateful spirit at all times.

Did you ever go out somewhere and an usher showed you to a seat in church or at the theatre, and you sat down without saying, “Thank you”? Did a cab driver drive you safely to your destination, and you alighted without saying “Thank you”? Have you ever been in school and a classmate shared their notes with you before a test, and you just collected them and walked off? All of these are simple, everyday situations we experience, and sometimes we don’t realise we ought to be thankful for these little things.

God expects you to have an attitude of gratitude; therefore, you should always be quick to say “Thank you.” When people do things for you, be it a favour or even something they’re obliged to do, always remember to thank them for it. Train yourself to lavishly express gratitude. Let that joyful atmosphere of thanksgiving always fill your home! There’s so much in life to be grateful for; so, practise being thankful.

Every day, before you think of your long list of prayer requests, thank God for all that He’s already done! When you learn to express gratitude to God, and profusely thank people for what they do for you, you’ll be amazed at the favour, joy and promotion you’ll experience in your life.

Liam: “I don’t know… I just feel like if I try to pray over this test, it won’t make a difference.”

Ava: “Why not? God’s Word says He’ll guide your steps. Faith isn’t guessing or hoping; it’s trusting His Word.”

Liam: “But what if it doesn’t work?”

Ava: “Then it was not faith, because faith ALWAYS WORKS.

Faith isn’t a leap in the dark as some people think, but a leap on the Word of God. Understanding this simple truth will position you rightly to live triumphantly every day and help you judge whether you’re actually functioning in faith or not. Those who think faith is a mysterious leap in the dark are always apprehensive and reluctant to take the step that’d have led them to victory. They’re always hesitating over stuff like exams, school projects, or standing up for what’s right: “What if I fail the test?” “What if I try to help my friend and it doesn’t work out?” “What if I speak the Word and nothing changes?” That shouldn’t be you.

Faith is the confident assurance that, based on God’s Word, things favourably expected will come to pass. Faith doesn’t ask “what if?” Rather, faith knows. In other words, faith knows that if hands are laid on the sick, they’ll recover, since that’s what the Word says! Faith knows that if there’s a need, then there’ll definitely be a corresponding supply based on Philippians 4:19: “And my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.” Hallelujah!

If you see faith as a leap into the unknown, you’ll always have many reasons for not doing the things you ought to do. You’ll always find yourself considering, reconsidering and hesitating. Faith depends on the Word of God as the basis and assurance for action. Faith hears and jumps, but fear hears the same thing and considers other factors. Remember, in the eyes of natural men, the Word of God is “unreasonable”; it makes no sense. That’s because God’s Word isn’t meant for the head but for the human spirit. Learn to respond to God’s Word from your spirit, and your faith will always prevail.

message:
Physicists have discovered a strange phenomenon called quantum entanglement, where two particles become so deeply connected that they behave as one system, even when separated by vast distances.

Our opening scripture above alludes to this concept, albeit at a much more advanced, spiritual level. It shows us that it isn’t just our spirits that are joined to the Body of Christ; even our very bodies are part of Him! Notice the Apostle Paul didn’t say, “Your body is a member of Christ,” which would have led us to believe he was speaking in a generic sense; he said, “…your bodies are members of Christ,” meaning your own body—yes, the one you use every day—is part of Him.

No wonder the Bible says “we are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones” (Ephesians 5:30). This means the life of Christ is flowing through you in real ways, even when you’re doing homework, hanging out with friends, or playing sports. Christ literally lives in you! He dwells in your spirit and expresses Himself through your physical body. This is why sickness, disease, and weakness ought not to thrive in your physical body. When you’re conscious of this truth that Christ lives in you, it’ll be impossible for you to experience any infirmity!

The reason many have suffered so much trouble in their health is their lack of knowledge. According to the provisions of the Gospel, it ought not to be possible for any child of God to be sick or suffer affliction of any kind. Your body isn’t ordinary; it’s Christ’s expression point on earth; Christ rules and functions in your physical body. Meditate on this truth and let it gain the ascendancy in your spirit. Live with the daily consciousness that your body is a member of Christ. As you do, sin, sickness, and disease will be completely banished from your life.

Lena: “But what if you don’t have to take the longest route just to find your way?”

Emma: “So… you’re saying there’s a better way?”

Lena: “Yeah. God’s Word. It guides you before the mistake ever happens.”

Many young people assume they must make mistakes first before learning important lessons, but God’s Word was given so you don’t have to learn the hard way. It’s the instruction manual for living. That’s why the Bible says, “All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness” (2 Timothy 3:16). There’s no better way to be a success in life than to follow the Word of God and do what it says. You don’t need to ruin your future choices, friendships, or purpose before learning wisdom. God already provided it in His Word.

You don’t have to fail a semester to learn the value of diligence, or lose a good friend to learn the importance of loyalty. Learning God’s Word and putting it to work will save you from regrettable experiences. David said, “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” (Psalm 119:105). That means the Word of God illuminates the paths of your life; it gives you direction and the “know-how” to succeed in life.

You don’t have to live by “trial and error”; stick with the Word, and everything about your life will work out beautifully. Yielding to the Word of God and living by it will make you a wonder to others around you. They’d begin to ask how come life is so easy for you! The answer is simple: the Word of God has become the pilot of your life. Praise God!

## Speak

Dear Lord, your Word is a lamp unto my feet and a light unto my path! It’s the compass by which I navigate through life, driving me in the path of righteousness, success, and prosperity. My heart will forever trust in your Word to do what it says, as it pilots me to greatness and good success in life, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
Many young people hear adults say, “God works in mysterious ways,” and start thinking God is unpredictable or hard to understand, like someone who changes rules without warning. But God isn’t that way; He’s not mysterious at all. Jesus showed us clearly what the Father is really like.

Jesus proved that God isn’t mysterious when He said, “He who has seen Me has seen the Father.” In other words, if you want to know what the Father is like, just look at Jesus. The Bible describes Jesus as the brightness of God’s glory, and the express image of His person (Hebrews 1:3), and Jesus wasn’t mysterious at all!

To be mysterious is to be strange and unpredictable, and Jesus wasn’t that way. He was, and still is, the perfect representation of the Father’s personality. He’s the Word of God made flesh. Thus, if you want to know more about the Father, then dig into the Word of God! Instead of guessing what God is like based on random opinions, social media quotes, or what someone angrily says during a crisis, study the Word daily, and you’ll become better acquainted with the Father’s personality. As you receive His Word into your Spirit and meditate on it, His character will be revealed to you and through you.

Make up your mind to know the Lord; He’s a loving, caring, thoughtful, patient, and merciful Father! A loving person can never be mysterious. Contrary to the perception of many, God isn’t the one responsible for the things that cause grief, turmoil, and panic in the world; those are the acts of the devil. According to the Bible, only good and perfect things come from God (James 1:17).

He doesn’t want anyone in the dark regarding His personality; that’s why He gave us His Word and sent the Holy Spirit to show us who He is. Praise God!

title: The Power of a Filtered Mouth
titleOriginal: THE POWER OF A FILTERED MOUTH
excerpt: In the realm of the spirit, words are extremely important. Many young people speak negatively about themselves without realising it—about their intelligence, future, family, or abilities.
scripture: “But I say to you that for every idle word men may speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
subtitle: (Build Your Life with Your Words)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for teaching me about the power of my words. Through your Word, and by your Spirit, I’m culturing my tongue to speak only faith-filled words! No unwholesome communication is allowed to proceed from my mouth. I speak only life-giving words that are consistent with your plans and purposes for my life, and I declare that my future is secure, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Record a 1-minute voice note of yourself making faith declarations about your life. Listen back to it twice today.

message:
In the realm of the spirit, words are extremely important. Many young people speak negatively about themselves without realising it—about their intelligence, future, family, or abilities. That’s why the Lord Jesus said, “…by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.” Interpreting the Master’s words literally means that a man will go to heaven or hell because of what he said or didn’t say. But beyond that, your life is the character of your words. If a man’s words are confusing, his life will be confusing. In the same way, if a man’s words are wholesome, his life will be wholesome.

This is why you must watch what you say. Some folks are positive with their “mouth-work” at times, and negative at other times; that’s the reason they experience so many ups and downs in their lives. Having made a wrong confession, they’d say: “I didn’t really mean what I said,” or “I was only joking when I said that.” Well, in the realm of the spirit, you have what you say, whether or not you meant it. In Mark 11:23, Jesus didn’t say, “…you shall have what you mean;” He said, ”…you shall have what you say.”

If you must make any joke, let it be positive and don’t joke against the Word. Avoid making self-deprecating jokes or “venting” about how you’re “dead” or “finished” after a long day. Don’t make careless statements, for they’ll produce results for you. That’s why you must say only what you mean, and mean whatever you say.

Remember, God holds you accountable for the things you say. So, build your life with your words. Your life can’t be different from the words you speak. Therefore, make it a conscious exercise to store God’s Word in your heart, for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks (Matthew 12:34). As God’s Word dwells richly in your heart, you’ll develop and speak faith-filled words. Praise God!

title: The Unconditional Love Mandate
excerpt: The Bible says, “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life” (John 3:16).
scripture: “In this is love, not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.”
subtitle: (See People Through God’s Eyes)
prayer: Dear Father, just as you’ve loved me with an everlasting love, I extend that love to everyone I meet today and show them the compassion of Christ. Thank you for filling my heart with your love and granting me the ability to take no record of any wrong, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, say one sincere, kind word to each person you interact with. Choose patience in every conversation and do at least one helpful act without expecting anything in return.

message:
The Bible says, “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life” (John 3:16). Isn’t it remarkable that the Bible doesn’t say “For God so loved Christians that He gave His only begotten son….” Rather, it says “For God so loved the world,” and that doesn’t refer to the plants, trees, and other physical features in the world, but to the world of men—sinners! What could God have seen in these sinners who didn’t even want Him that would compel Him to offer the ultimate sacrifice—the death of His Son—to save them?

This lets me know that God loves everybody, irrespective of who they are and what they’ve done. In His eyes, everyone is beautiful; there’s a value in man that makes God love him unconditionally. That love causes Him to look beyond your shortcomings. The Bible says “…that is, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses to them...” (2 Corinthians 5:19).

God’s love for man is both unconditional and irrevocable. In Ephesians 5:1, we’re admonished to be imitators of God as beloved children. This includes how you treat classmates, siblings, teammates, and even people who offend you. There’s a beauty in others that God expects you to see, irrespective of what you see and how you may feel about them.

When you train yourself to relate with everyone around you in this manner, anger, malice, and bitterness will never be a part of your life! There wouldn’t be anything that someone could do that would make you want to hurt or hate them. Rather, you’d respond to people with the love of God. Let God’s love burn in you, such that you’ll always see the good in others. Let there be absolutely nobody that you can’t love, for everyone is lovable. I love everybody because I see them with the eyes of the Father. Remember, everyone is lovable, for they’re all worth the blood of God’s own Son.

title: Grace Is upon You
excerpt: A seed, buried in the soil, may seem hidden and powerless, yet with the right conditions, it bursts forth, breaking through the ground toward the sunlight.
scripture: “For exaltation comes neither from the east nor from the west nor from the south. But God is the Judge: He puts down one, and exalts another.”
subtitle: (This Is Your Set Time For Promotion)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for the power of promotion that is at work in me, which causes me to rise higher and higher everyday in every area of my life. I experience only the “upward and forward” movement in my life, heaping success upon success, in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: As you go to work or school, don’t just expect the same old routine. Expect divine favour. Expect to be noticed for your excellence.

message:
A seed, buried in the soil, may seem hidden and powerless, yet with the right conditions, it bursts forth, breaking through the ground toward the sunlight. Just as the seed is designed to grow and reach higher, God has designed your life for continual elevation. Stagnation isn’t in His plan for you.

Promotion, the Bible says, doesn’t come from the east, west, or south, but from God. The Lord delights in promoting His children; that is, taking them from one level to a higher level in every aspect of their lives. He detests stagnation and retrogression; that’s why He wants you to continually progress and move forward in life. The Bible says, “...the path of the just is like the shining sun, that shines ever brighter unto the perfect day” (Proverbs 4:18). The remarkable thing about God’s promotion is that it defies human logic and amazes the natural mind.

As a young person, it’s important to understand that God’s grace is the power behind every step of advancement in your life. Even when circumstances seem challenging, whether in school, relationships, or personal goals, His grace is active, preparing you for higher levels of success.

Consider Joseph in the Bible. He was sold into slavery by his brothers, falsely accused by Potiphar’s wife, and imprisoned. Yet, the grace of God moved him from prison to becoming the Prime Minister of Egypt (Genesis 41:39- 40). God can transform even difficult situations, which might seem disadvantageous, into the very avenues of your advancement because you’re His chosen child. Praise God!

message:
Job was a man who had lived in great affluence because he was richly blessed of God. But imagine the terrible words he uttered when he got into trouble! This is just like some folks; when they face even a small problem—like failing a test or dealing with family drama— they forget so quickly all the good things God has done for them. Not only do they wallow in self-pity, but they also want everyone to feel sorry for them.

If you read the whole chapter, it’s full of lamentation and self-pity. This is the result of fear and a lack of understanding of the nature of God. Job wished to die. He had given up. But the Lord was merciful and restored him. We must learn not to give up in times of adversity.

The man of faith is the man with a righteous heart that’s fixed on God and trusting in Him. He doesn’t accept defeat and refuses to give in. He doesn’t give consideration to anything aside God’s Word. He lives a consistent and persistent life of confession of the Word. People without faith complain about everything and focus on the negatives. Job opened his mouth and cursed his day. Christians, full of faith, however, open their mouths to encourage themselves and others, speaking God’s Word even when things seem tough.

Faith that possesses doesn’t speak carelessly. Therefore, no matter what the case may be, let the life you live be the life of faith. When school, friendships, or personal challenges try to knock you down, refuse to cower or give up; keep speaking God’s Word over your life, because faith always wins. Glory to God!

message:
Have you ever felt like life is totally unfair? Like, no matter what you do, things just keep going wrong? Maybe friends have let you down, school is tough, or your dreams feel so far away. That’s what we’re discussing today.

If you ever find yourself in a difficult situation where things look bleak, don’t despair; rather, rejoice, because that seemingly negative situation is part of the grand process for your promotion. Joseph’s brothers sold him as a slave in Egypt (Genesis 37:28), but from prison, Joseph rose to become the Prime Minister of Egypt. No wonder the Bible says, “count it all joy when you fall into various trials” (James 1:2), because the result is certain: they’ll turn out for your good!

Think about this: everything around you—your friends, your school, even social media—can somehow work in your favour when you trust God. Just like the stars in their courses fought for Deborah against her enemies (Judges 5:20), the things in your world can line up to help you win. Even in moments that feel totally out of your control, God has your back. Remember Joshua commanding the sun and moon to stand still (Joshua 10:12-14)? God made creation work for Joshua’s advantage. In the same way, God is setting things up in your life, even the stuff that seems random or frustrating, to make sure you win.

God has ordained your life, so no challenge can truly overwhelm you. When trials and pressures come, face them with the mindset of someone who already has the advantage. Praise God!

message:
Christianity isn’t a religion; it’s the pulsating life of God in a human person. When you become a Christian, it means eternal life has been imparted to your spirit. You become God’s dwelling place. So, now that you’re born again, God has fully tabernacled in you! You’ve become His living headquarters. He looks through your eyes and walks with your legs. You’re a God-carrying vessel.

Talking about Jesus, the Bible says “...in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily; and you are complete in Him...” (Colossians 2:9-10). Notice the tenth verse says “And you are complete in Him....” In other words, all of divinity resides in you. You’ve become God’s operating centre! You’re loaded with the maximum load of God. That’s what it means to be “complete in Him,” as rendered in the original Greek text. Nothing else needs to be done in you to make you as divine as God is divine, because He already lives in you in His fullness.

This is why sickness, diseases, and infirmities shouldn’t be part of your life. You have in you the genes of your heavenly Father. You’re as divine as God is divine. Basically, God’s power isn’t just for church or Sunday; it’s running through you all the time, even when you’re at school or hanging out with friends. You’re sufficient in His sufficiency (2 Corinthians 3:5); in other words, His abilities are at work in you. No wonder the Bible declares that you’re a partaker of His divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). Glory to God!

prayer: Dear heavenly Father, I thank you for making me your heir. Thank you for my royal lineage! You’ve made me a king and a priest; therefore, I refuse to live a beggarly and ordinary life, for I was born to reign and effect changes in the realm of the spirit through my words, and your Word in my mouth is producing abundant results, in Jesus’ Name. message:
The kings of the earth employ painstaking efforts to raise and culture their children, because they’re royalty. Their kids don’t walk, talk, dress or behave like everyone else. The expectations are even greater when the child in question is the heir-apparent. That’s why Solomon said, “I was my father’s son, tender and the only one in the sight of my mother. He also taught me, and said to me: “Let your heart retain my words; keep my commands, and live’” (Proverbs 4:3-4).

Solomon certainly wasn’t David’s only child, yet he said, “I was my father’s son” because he was the one groomed for the throne. There was a special training David needed to bequeath to him, which the other sons didn’t get. As God’s children, we’re His heirs: ”and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ...” (Romans 8:17). You’re a joint-heir with Jesus Christ!

You’re not an ordinary person; you’re a prince of power with God. Your heavenly Father owns the whole world and has placed you in charge of His possessions. No wonder the Bible says all things are yours (1 Corinthians 3:21). What an honour to be an heir of God! You’ve been called to reign in life as a king. Make up your mind to walk, talk and live as a king that you are.

Refuse to use beggarly language; the children of kings don’t talk cheap; they exercise authority. In your prayers, don’t beg. Relate with God as a son. He loves you and knows you’re His heir, who has a right to His inexhaustible inheritance. Glory to God!

titleOriginal: WALK IN THE LIGHT OF THE WORD
excerpt: The Word of God is light (Psalm 119:105), and the Scripture tells us to walk in the light as God is in the light.
scripture: “But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin.”
subtitle: (Allow The Word Of God Guide You)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: Dear Father, your Word is a lamp unto my feet and a light unto my path. I walk in the reality of your Word today, and as I do, I’m guided in the path of prosperity, victory and excellence! There’s no darkness or uncertainties on my path because I walk in the light of your Word, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, before you make any major decision or react to any situation, pause and ask yourself: “What does God’s Word say about this?”

message:
The Word of God is light (Psalm 119:105), and the Scripture tells us to walk in the light as God is in the light. In other words, we’re to walk under the same light in which God dwells and functions. This means we’re to walk in the light of God’s Word. The people of the world can’t understand that light since they’re not born into that realm of life. But we can walk in the light and have fellowship with God, because we’re born of the Word (1 Peter 1:23).

Walking in the light as God is in the light means your judgments and opinions are based on the light of God’s Word. So, instead of forming your opinions from social media trends, peer pressure, or what everyone else thinks is “cool,” you choose to see things the way God sees them. Under that light, you don’t see poverty, sickness, disease, death, failure or impossibilities. When you agree with what the Word says about you, and then confess it and act that way, you’re walking in God’s light. God has given you His Word to light up your path, so there wouldn’t be darkness or uncertainties as you journey through life.

The Bible lets us know that when you walk in the light, the blood of Jesus Christ automatically cleanses you from all sin. The world around us is full of sin, and even the very air we breathe is defiled, and God knows it. Then oftentimes, we do things that are wrong without knowing, but thanks be unto God! He says when you walk in the light, you won’t need to keep asking yourself, “What sin have I committed today?” The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses you automatically!

Learn to walk in the light as He’s in the light. That way, you’ll never be weighed down by the burden or yoke of sin; rather, you’ll be free to serve God and run the faith race without hindrances.

message:
The Lord Jesus performed several miracles while He was here on earth; He healed the sick, raised the dead, multiplied food, and turned water into wine—His life was an unending stream of the miraculous. As He prepared to leave the earth, He declared that those who believe in Him would do even greater works than He did. That means He’s made you a miracle worker just like Him, even as a teenager in your school, on your team, or in your neighbourhood! He said, “Most assuredly, I say to you, he who believes in Me, the works that I do he will do also; and greater works than these he will do, because I go to My Father.”

When Peter and John met the crippled man at the gate of the temple, Peter said, “Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6). Then Peter grabbed the man’s hand and lifted him up and he walked! Peter didn’t pray to God to heal the man; Peter performed the miracle in the Name of Jesus! That’s the kind of life He’s called you to live. Remember the words of the Master: “… you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you” (Acts 1:8). “Power” there is the dynamic ability to cause changes.

The question, therefore, is: Have you received the Holy Ghost? If you have, then you’re a miracle worker like Jesus, for it was the Holy Ghost in Him that made Him do those works. Is someone at school hurting? Go ahead and lay your hands on that one and demand a recovery in the Name of Jesus. Whether it’s someone being bullied or you’re facing pressure from exams or family issues, declare the change you want to see in the Name of Jesus. You have no reason to feel disadvantaged or helpless anymore, because there’s a miracle-working ability in you now! Glory to God forevermore!

message:
There’s a touching story about a wealthy man who lived like a pauper, unaware that a vast inheritance had already been credited to his name. message:

Success in life isn’t dependent on the number of degrees you bagged in college; it’s in the amount of God’s Word you know and put to work. No demon will listen to you because of your education, nor will sickness, disease, or poverty bow to anything else except the Word of God.

Just as every father desires to see his child progress academically, it’s your heavenly Father’s desire that you grow up spiritually. Sadly, some Christians are still in the realm of childishness meaning there’s still so much in the Word of God to learn. Life is spiritual, and the Word of God is also spiritual (John 6:63). I know some people love reading, so someone can read the Bible from Genesis to Revelation and still not gain anything at all. excerpt: To delight yourself in the Lord means to be excited about God. It means taking joy in serving Him and doing what pleases Him.
scripture: “Delight yourself also in the Lord, and He shall give you the desires of your heart.”
subtitle: (Delight Yourself in the Lord)
prayer: Dear Father, my heart is full of love and tender appreciation of you. I love you, and I’m excited to express that love every day of my life. My desire in life is to bring honour and glory to your name, and I’m empowered to fulfil your purpose, Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: This week, come early for a church service and make yourself available to serve. If you’re not yet in a unit, join one or volunteer for a team, and gladly take up a role that advances God’s work.

message:
To delight yourself in the Lord means to be excited about God. It means taking joy in serving Him and doing what pleases Him. That was David; he said, “I was glad when they said to me, ‘Let us go into the house of the Lord’“(Psalm 122:1). He loved being in God’s presence and pleased God so much that God called him a “...man after My own heart” (Acts 13:22).

To be “excited” means “to be stirred by strong emotion.” That means when you think about God, your heart lights up, like when your favourite song plays or you nail something you worked hard on. You want to do anything to make Him happy! That’s delighting yourself in the Lord.

The Bible says, “Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord; and I will cause you to ride on the high hills of the earth...” (Isaiah 58:14). Those who delight in God experience life differently, like playing on easy mode while the rest of the world struggles. Every day feels vibrant, full of purpose, and even the miraculous.

Those who aren’t excited about Him, even if saved, often have a dull experience of life. But when you delight yourself in the Lord, the Bible says, “...He shall give you the desires of your heart.” God places good desires in your heart and fulfils them, so your prayers focus more on others and worship than just asking for yourself.

Get excited about God and all that matters to Him, and watch your life overflow with His goodness and miracles!

excerpt: Stefan always thought he didn’t have enough faith as a Christian. He figured his was less than Christine’s, who always had miracles and supernatural events happening in her life.
scripture: “For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.”
subtitle: (No Amount Of Faith Is Insignificant)

extras.label: Act

message:
Stefan always thought he didn’t have enough faith as a Christian. He figured his was less than Christine’s, who always had miracles and supernatural events happening in her life. This was Stefan’s thinking till the day he heard Romans 12:3 preached in church. He suddenly realised he had all the faith he required for an awesome life and, in fact, could grow his faith.

This same amount of faith is what you’ve received as God’s child. Notice Paul didn’t say in our opening scripture: “…a measure of faith”; rather, he used the definite article “the.” This shows that there’s only one measure of faith, and He gave it to you when you were born again.

You might ask, “If I already got the faith I require, why did Jesus then say in Mark 11:22: “Have faith in God’”? Or as the marginal reference in some versions puts it, “Have the faith of God.” As a new creation, you’re born of God’s Word, with faith in your spirit. Faith came to you as a seed when you received the Gospel, and it’s the same size given to every one of us.

What you’re supposed to do is to use it and grow it. You increase your faith by hearing the Word (Romans 10:17) and make it stronger by acting on the Word. Glory to God!

title: Beyond Your Paycheque
excerpt: Most rivers don’t create their own water; they simply carry water from a larger source, such as rainfall, glaciers, or lakes. When the source dries up, the river eventually disappears.
scripture: “And my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.”
subtitle: (Look to God, Not Your Job, as Your Source)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: Heavenly Father, I rejoice for I know I can forever rely on you to supply my every financial and material need because you’re my source. I experience promotion and prosperity. Thank you for bringing me to my place of inheritance in Christ Jesus, where I prosper financially, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Never say, “Oh God, I need money!” Instead, say, “I’m rich; I have all the money I need because God has made all favour and earthly blessings come to me in abundance.”

message:
Most rivers don’t create their own water; they simply carry water from a larger source, such as rainfall, glaciers, or lakes. When the source dries up, the river eventually disappears. What many people call their “supply” is often only a channel. The most important thing therefore isn’t the channel, but the source of it.

Now, the way some people live, you would think Paul meant, “My God shall supply all your needs according to how much you’re paid at your place of work.” Even if your “job” is chores, a part-time gig, or allowance, God is still your ultimate source. Your job ceased to be the source of income for you the day you were born again. Now God supplies all your needs according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:19).

If you look at the Sun you will not see the shadows; in the same way, when you put your trust in God, you will stop chasing shadows. Stop stressing about allowance, online fame, or what your friends have—you have a bigger source. Stop seeing your job or your business as your source of income, for God is your source.

The forces of nature will try to make you believe your job is your source, but refuse it completely. The Bible didn’t say “Work, that you may have money.” Rather, it tells us that the reason God wants you to work is so that you “may have to give to him who has need” (Ephesians 4:28). Even small acts, like helping a friend, volunteering, or sharing your lunch, are ways God blesses others through you. Your job is a channel to bless others, and in doing so, you are rewarded. Giving is God’s established medium to prosper you financially—never forget it.

Therefore, it doesn’t matter how much you’re paid at your job or business, never take it as your source of income. Do your schoolwork, sports practice, or any responsibility with excellence and avoid laziness, and God will promote you. Do your job with excellence and shun mediocrity, and the Lord will promote you.

Now, the way some people live, you would think Paul meant, “My God shall supply all your needs according to how much you’re paid at your place of work.” Even if your “job” is chores, a part-time gig, or allowance, God is still your ultimate source. Your job ceased to be the source of income for you the day you were born again. Now God supplies all your needs according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:19).

If you look at the Sun you will not see the shadows; in the same way, when you put your trust in God, you will stop chasing shadows. Stop stressing about allowance, online fame, or what your friends have—you have a bigger source. Stop seeing your job or your business as your source of income, for God is your source.

The forces of nature will try to make you believe your job is your source, but refuse it completely. The Bible didn’t say “Work, that you may have money.” Rather, it tells us that the reason God wants you to work is so that you “may have to give to him who has need” (Ephesians 4:28). Even small acts, like helping a friend, volunteering, or sharing your lunch, are ways God blesses others through you. Your job is a channel to bless others, and in doing so, you are rewarded. Giving is God’s established medium to prosper you financially—never forget it.

Therefore, it doesn’t matter how much you’re paid at your job or business, never take it as your source of income. Do your schoolwork, sports practice, or any responsibility with excellence and avoid laziness, and God will promote you. Do your job with excellence and shun mediocrity, and the Lord will promote you.

## Speak

Heavenly Father, I rejoice for I know I can forever rely on you to supply my every financial and material need because you’re my source. I experience promotion and prosperity. Thank you for bringing me to my place of inheritance in Christ Jesus, where I prosper financially, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Never say, “Oh God, I need money!” Instead, say, “I’m rich; I have all the money I need because God has made all favour and earthly blessings come to me in abundance.”

message:
Some runners start a race strong but falter before the finish line. Others stumble at the first sign of resistance. But the one who finishes strong is remembered— not for how fast they ran at the start, but for how they ran when the pressure was greatest.

There’s a race of life, and everyone is involved in that race, whether or not they know it. When Paul said, “I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus,” the idea most folks get is that of someone inching his way slowly through a press to reach the goal. The Greek word translated “press” is “dioko”, and it means “to run swiftly as in a race so as to win a prize.”

Not only is it important for you to know that you have a race to run, it is even more important for you to know “how” to run your race. You must run fast, because the time is short and the adversary will do everything to frustrate you from getting the prize. This is why Paul said “I run swiftly toward the mark for the prize.”

What’s that prize? It’s not just talking about heaven; the man wanted to fulfill God’s purpose and calling for his life and finish it completely! No wonder at the end of his life, he could boldly declare, “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Finally, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness...” (2 Timothy 4:7-8).

Like the Apostle Paul, run your race with purpose. Think about your school goals, your friendships, or your talents; what has God put in your life that only you can develop? What is that thing God has called you to do? Commit your whole being to it. Let your heart’s cry be to fulfil God’s purpose and plans for your life. Even small steps count—showing kindness, doing your homework with excellence, standing up for what’s right— they’re all part of your race! Run your race to win, so that at the end, you too can boldly declare, “I have finished my course, I have kept the faith,” and then receive the Master’s crown.

title: Let Love Lead
excerpt: Across the world, disagreements between people, groups and nations often grow into hostility. History shows how quickly differences can turn individuals into enemies.
scripture: “You have heard that it was said, “You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you.”
subtitle: (Meditate On The Love Of God)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: Dear heavenly Father, I have set my eyes on you and your Word alone. As I meditate on your goodness and your love, my heart is completely overwhelmed by your love for me. By your Spirit, I demonstrate this love to others every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, choose one person who’s a bit “difficult” to connect with; pray for them, bless them in your heart, and do one kind act toward them.

message:
Across the world, disagreements between people, groups and nations often grow into hostility. History shows how quickly differences can turn individuals into enemies. Many societies even justify loving those who support you and rejecting those who oppose you. Yet the Lord Jesus profoundly challenges this thinking.

The society tells you to love your friends and hate your enemies. On the contrary, the Lord Jesus is teaching you in the portion of the scripture you’ve just read to love both your friends and enemies. It’s important to note that He was addressing men who weren’t born again; people who still thought of their enemies as flesh and blood. Sadly, some young people still think this way, and sometimes pray against their classmates or peers, saying, “Oh Lord! Fight against my enemies, destroy them....”

You can’t be God-conscious until you’re conscious of God’s love. This is why you must always take out time to meditate on the love of God. Think about His grace, kindness and how He chose you to be His child, despite your imperfections.

Always remember that if you were the only one on earth, the Lord Jesus would still have given His life for you. Just as the man in Matthew 13:44 sold everything he had to buy a field because of the treasure in it, you’re the treasure Jesus saw that He willingly gave His life for. When you let the love of God dominate you as you meditate on His Word, you’ll cease to be enemy-conscious.

message:
Sylvester always thought, “I believe the Word, but why aren’t things working out right for me?” He was hoping that God would set him free someday; he was clueless to the truth that Jesus had already made him free. Even though he’d heard about it sometime ago, he wasn’t in faith.

You see, faith is different from believing: Faith declares the Word to be real and true now, and acts accordingly. The contrary circumstances will not change by themselves, or change just because you believe. “Believing” the Word is not enough; your believing must translate to faith.

For your situation to change or to maintain a life of continuous progress and triumph, it’s got to be by your faith.

It’s like the title deed to a property. You don’t have to be in the property to know it’s yours; faith is the title deed. Take a hold of God’s Word and affirm your healing and health, prosperity, success, and victory in Christ Jesus! The second part of Romans 10:10 says, “…with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.”

title: It’s Here Now
excerpt: In 2009, an unknown Scottish woman stepped onto a talent show stage and stunned the audience with an extraordinary voice.
scripture: “Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon”
subtitle: (Receive the Promotion that Comes from God)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for your wisdom functioning in me. That wisdom is the power of promotion in my life this year, and by it, I’m rising to greater heights at work, at school, in ministry by the Spirit, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Expect promotion today; declare: “This is my set time for favour and elevation!” Then watch for doors, opportunities or recognition.

message:
In 2009, an unknown Scottish woman stepped onto a talent show stage and stunned the audience with an extraordinary voice. Within minutes, someone many had overlooked became a global sensation overnight. Moments like that remind us how quickly a person can move from obscurity to the spotlight when the right opportunity appears.

Promotion doesn’t come from the east or west, but from God alone. He’s the only one who can supernaturally promote you in a way that’ll baffle your detractors. The promotion that comes from God is the kind of promotion that defies human logic and leaves people wondering how it happened. The Bible tells us how Joseph was sold into Egypt as a slave by his brothers. To further compound his ordeal, while serving in Potiphar’s house, he was falsely accused and imprisoned. Things looked bleak until the Pharaoh had a dream which no one but Joseph could interpret.

After Joseph interpreted the dream and proffered his advice on how to contain the coming famine, the king said, “Inasmuch as God has shown you all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you. You shall be over my house, and all my people shall be ruled according to your word; only in regard to the throne will I be greater than you” (Genesis 41:39-40). Glory to God! Joseph went from prisoner to Prime Minister of a superpower nation in one day! That’s supernatural promotion---the promotion that comes from God.

A few verses before the opening Scripture, the king had been angry with all his wise men and threatened to kill them all. Yet, a little while later, Daniel was promoted! He received both the knowledge and the interpretation of the king’s dream and saved his life and the lives of many others. God used a situation that should have led to his destruction as a means of promotion for him!

Get ready to receive inexplicable promotions in school, in leadership roles, and in responsibilities people may think you’re “too young” for. This is your season to get promoted to higher levels
