Both environments exist on the same planet, yet the life in one cannot live by the conditions of the other. Similarly, human life can be understood as operating within two distinct spiritual realms.

There are two spiritual realms of life and death existing side by side, and everyone is in either one of them. excerpt: Every ecosystem on earth depends on order. When the seasons run their normal course, crops grow well, rivers flow steadily, and animals can find the food they need to survive.
scripture: “Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world or life or death, or things present or things to come—all are yours. And you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.”
subtitle: (Enjoy What God Has Given You)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I’m an obedient child of God. I’ve obeyed the Gospel, and I do the Word. Because I’m willing and obedient to the Word, I eat the good of the land, and I walk in health and prosperity. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Name one thing you desire, whether small or big, and declare: “All things are mine; I receive God’s best in this.”

message:
Every ecosystem on earth depends on order. When the seasons run their normal course, crops grow well, rivers flow steadily, and animals can find the food they need to survive. But when that order is disrupted, even strong systems begin to struggle. In the same way, life often produces its best results when we live according to the order established by God.

Everything God created was good and especially made for your comfort and provision. That’s why the Word says all things are yours to enjoy! But sadly, some young Christians believe they have to suffer and settle for the lesser things in life. They’ve been taught that it’s wrong to look good, and it’s better to be poor on earth and go to heaven than to be rich on earth and go to hell. Being rich and looking good have nothing to do with going to hell or heaven—including enjoying your youth responsibly.

The Bible says in 2 Corinthians 8:9, “For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich.” Jesus suffered that we might not suffer; He became poor that we might become rich; He brought us out that He might take us in. He tells us in Isaiah 1:19,“If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land...” This means your life becomes enjoyable when you decide to walk in obedience to the will of God.

Obedience is an act of submission to the leadership of God. When you obey God’s command, you come under His authority. As such, He’s empowered to act on your behalf. But when you disobey, you break His hedge of protection around you, and you give the enemy the chance to strike.

Start from where you are and respond to God’s Word today. Be conscious that indeed all things are yours and that He’s given you all things that pertain to life and godliness. Walk in obedience so you will enjoy all He has given to you and made available for you. How much you enjoy life depends on you. Start today!

title: Present Yourself to the Word
excerpt: Imagine a friend gave you their brand-new gaming console to borrow for the weekend. You’d treat it with respect, right? You wouldn’t spill drinks on it or drive it into a wall.
scripture: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.”
subtitle: (Your Body Is A Gift Of Trust Given To You By God)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: Dear Father, my body is your temple and your dwelling-place. I yield every fibre of my body to your Word, as a living sacrifice, that I might bring glory to your Name. No sickness shall reign in my body, and sin shall not lord it over me, because I belong to you. Thank you for this great privilege, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.

message:
Imagine a friend gave you their brand-new gaming console to borrow for the weekend. You’d treat it with respect, right? You wouldn’t spill drinks on it or drive it into a wall. You’d want to take care of it because it’s a gift you’re responsible for. Well, God has given you a gift too: your body. And He actually lives in it.

The Bible says, ”Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own? For you were bought at a price; therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s” (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Your body is actually a gift of trust given to you by God to function here on earth, and He expects you to use it wisely, because every one of us will account for what we did with our bodies. This is the reason the Lord tells you to present your body as a living sacrifice.

To present your body as a living sacrifice means that you present your body to the Word of God. In other words, you cause your body to do only those things that the Word of God says you should do. You make your body function in such a way that brings glory to the Word of God. For example, the Bible says you should put to death the illegal transactions of the body (Romans 8:13); so, when your body starts feeling tired, lazy, or tries to get sick right before a big game or exam, you say, “Body, you’re the temple of the Holy Ghost; we’re not accommodating sickness or weakness here; I’m alive!”

Again, the Word of God says that “sin shall not have dominion over you” (Romans 6:14), and so you let God’s Word and righteousness reign in you. When you present your body to the Word of God, life will take on a whole new meaning; sickness and infirmity, depression and sorrow will be a thing of the past! The glory of God will be mightily manifested from your spirit, through your body, to the outside world.

excerpt: You know how in video games you usually have an avatar? That character running around, jumping, and exploring is just the skin you control. The real you is the player holding the controller.
scripture: “rather let it be the hidden person of the heart, with the incorruptible beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in the sight of God.”
subtitle: (Recognise That You’re A Spirit Being)
prayer: Dear Father, I pray that you would grant me, according to the riches of your glory, to be strengthened with might by your Spirit in my inner man, and that Christ may continually dwell in my spirit by faith, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, take a minute to talk to your spirit—the real you. Say out loud, “You’re the real me. You’re strong, you’re filled with God’s light, and you’re in charge.” Then, feed your spirit with the Word and pray in the Spirit.

message:
You know how in video games you usually have an avatar? That character running around, jumping, and exploring is just the skin you control. The real you is the player holding the controller. In the same way, your body is like your earth-suit, your avatar. But the real you? That’s the spirit man living inside.

The one Peter calls the “hidden person of the heart” is the same one the Apostle Paul calls the “inward man” (2 Corinthians 4:16). The inward man is the human spirit, the one who can’t be seen with the optical eyes. The “outward man” is the body with its five senses. The real “you” is the inward man, not the outward man. When you speak, it’s the inward man that talks through your mouth.

You’re a spirit being, not a physical body. The body that you see is your house, not the real you (2 Corinthians 5:1). A lot of people get this backwards. They spend all their time and energy worrying about what their “avatar” looks like—their clothes, their skin, their hair—and they forget to upgrade the person inside. It’s important to recognise that you’re a spirit being, because the man inside is the one that God deals with and relates to, not the physical body. This is the reason the Bible says, “The spirit of a man is the lamp of the Lord, searching all the inner depths of his heart” (Proverbs 20:27).

The Lord relates with your spirit in leading and guiding you, not your mind or your body. The character you exhibit outside is a direct reflection of the state of your spirit, so God contacts you through your spirit. As you walk in this consciousness, you’ll live beyond physical circumstances; your body will comply with the inward man, and your life will be supernatural every day.

excerpt: Modern aircraft can track their position within metres using satellites thousands of kilometres above the earth.
scripture: “However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.”
subtitle: (The Holy Spirit Guides You In The Path Of Life)
prayer: Precious Holy Spirit, I thank you for your ministry in my life. I thank you for opening my eyes to see the sure paths you’ve prepared for me to walk in. extras.text: Before you make a decision today—from friendships to study choices or your future—pause and say, “Holy Spirit, how would you want me to go about this?” He’ll guide you.

message:
Modern aircraft can track their position within metres using satellites thousands of kilometres above the earth. Without that guidance, even the most powerful plane could easily lose its way. In the same way, life without direction leaves many people uncertain about the future.

As one who is born again, never find yourself anxious about the future, especially when it comes to school, career choices, or your purpose in life. The Lord Jesus said, “When the Holy Spirit, who is truth, comes, he shall guide you into all truth...He will tell you about the future” (John 16:13 TLB). The man without the Holy Spirit is the one who should be uncertain about his future, for he’s like an aeroplane without a pilot, or a ship without a captain, lost at sea, bobbing up and down in the water. Such a person is walking in darkness, without a sense of direction.

But if you’re born again, you can be certain that your future is a bright and prosperous one. You don’t have to panic about “what’s next” or compare your journey with others. Life doesn’t have to be mysterious anymore because the Holy Spirit has come to guide you and bring the future into your present. The Psalmist said, “You will show me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy; at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore” (Psalm 16:11).

By yourself, you can’t know the path of life that brings success, joy, victory and prosperity, but the Holy Spirit has come to lead you into that path. He knows how to take you through life’s journey and make you a success, for He sees the end from the beginning. Recognise Him as the One called to guide you in life, and He will show you visions of the future. Let go of the “trial and error” life and let the Holy Spirit have His way in you. You don’t have to “guess” your life; He helps you choose wisely. He has come to show you the higher life, where your future is a settled fact!

excerpt: In law, the principle of vicarious liability allows one party to be held legally responsible for the debts of another, effectively clearing the original debtor of all charges once the…
scripture: “Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise Him; He has put Him to grief. When You make His soul an offering for sin...”
subtitle: (Live Free From Condemnation)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for sending Jesus to die in my place, thereby paying the full penalty for my sins. I rejoice, knowing that His sacrifice for sin was the ultimate sacrifice by which I now stand justified in your presence. Thank you for ushering me into this new life of righteousness, where I now reign and rule with Christ forever, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: End the month by declaring: “Jesus paid it all; I’m forever free!”

message:
In law, the principle of vicarious liability allows one party to be held legally responsible for the debts of another, effectively clearing the original debtor of all charges once the penalty is paid. When this happens, the case is permanently settled, and the original defendant can no longer be tried for that offence. This illustrates how one act of substitution can result in total acquittal, permanently erasing a record of guilt.

This is precisely what the Lord Jesus did for us. He was condemned in our place, and He paid the full penalty for our sins. He was crucified on the Cross, and He went to hell for our sake. In other words, in the mind of God, we’ve been justified; that means declared “not guilty.” God is no longer going to judge or hold us accountable for our sins; He already judged Jesus on account of our sins. The Bible says, ”But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities...” (Isaiah 53:5). So, if you ever wondered if you have to keep carrying guilt, the answer is no. Jesus already carried it.

The sins of the whole world were laid on Jesus; that means no sinner in the world should take responsibility for their sins because Jesus paid for everybody. That’s the message of the gospel! The Bible says”that is, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses to them...” (2 Corinthians 5:19). Notice it says God was in Christ, reconciling ‘the world’ (not Christians), but ‘the world of sinners’ unto Himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them. This means He’s not holding their sins against them.

Now, that’s for the sinner. What about you that are born again? God is not ‘low-key’ mad at you! He’s not wielding a big stick over your head to strike you anytime you do something wrong; the Lord Jesus has taken responsibility and paid the full penalty for your sins, both past, present and future. You’re free to live with your head held high! Glory be to God!

message:
Did you know that praying in the Name of Jesus is like having ‘VIP Access’ to the most important person in the world? The Lord Jesus didn’t just give us a phone number; He gave us His own Name as the password!

One of the wonderful blessings of the new creation life is our privilege to talk directly to God in prayer and receive answers. Jesus said, “And in that day you will ask Me nothing. Most assuredly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My name He will give you. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full” (John 16:23-24). So, Leo’s fear that his prayers stop at the ceiling isn’t true. In Jesus’ Name, your prayers go straight to the Father. Hallelujah!

You have the right to pray directly to the Father in the Name of Jesus and receive answers to your prayers. Sadly, some folks don’t have confidence in their own prayers, so they look to others to pray for them. They feel like they’re ‘too young’ or not ‘holy enough’ for God to listen. But if you’re born again, that shouldn’t be your story for the Bible declares in 1 Peter 3:12: “For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are open to their prayers...”

Thus, you’re guaranteed to receive answers to your prayers—Jesus has chosen you and ordained you to receive answers to prayers. This should make your prayer times exciting moments with the Lord, for you know that every time you pray, you’ll surely receive answers. Therefore, the next time you kneel or lift your hands to pray, remember the words of Jesus---”but I have chosen you, and ordained you... that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.” God isn’t holding back from you, so never doubt His willingness to respond to your requests. He loves to hear your voice in prayer and delights in answering your prayers.

Most assuredly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My name He will give you. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full” (John 16:23-24). So, Leo’s fear that his prayers stop at the ceiling isn’t true. In Jesus’ Name, your prayers go straight to the Father. Hallelujah!

You have the right to pray directly to the Father in the Name of Jesus and receive answers to your prayers. Sadly, some folks don’t have confidence in their own prayers, so they look to others to pray for them. They feel like they’re ‘too young’ or not ‘holy enough’ for God to listen. But if you’re born again, that shouldn’t be your story for the Bible declares in 1 Peter 3:12: “For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are open to their prayers...”

Thus, you’re guaranteed to receive answers to your prayers—Jesus has chosen you and ordained you to receive answers to prayers. This should make your prayer times exciting moments with the Lord, for you know that every time you pray, you’ll surely receive answers. Therefore, the next time you kneel or lift your hands to pray, remember the words of Jesus---”but I have chosen you, and ordained you... that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.” God isn’t holding back from you, so never doubt His willingness to respond to your requests. He loves to hear your voice in prayer and delights in answering your prayers.

## Prayer

Precious heavenly Father, thank you for the wonderful blessing of praying in the Name of Jesus and the confidence of knowing that your ears are open to hear and answer my prayers always. I rejoice to know that you’ve ordained me to receive answers to my prayers; thus, I see the results of my prayers in my life and in the lives of my loved ones, in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

message:
Tyler: “How did Jesus do all those miracles?” Mary: “It’s because the Holy Spirit came on Him and anointed Him. And guess what? The same Holy Spirit is in you now.”

The word “Christ” is from the Greek word”Christos,” which refers to the Messiah or the anointed One, and His anointing. So contrary to what some folks believe, “Christ” isn’t Jesus’ surname; rather, it refers to the anointing that makes Him who He is. That anointing empowered Him supernaturally for His earthly ministry.

Remember, though He was Himself God, He ministered as the Son of man while He was on earth. But the anointing came into His life when the Holy Spirit came upon Him at the River Jordan (John 1:32-33), and that was when He became “the Christ.” He didn’t perform a single miracle until the anointing of the Holy Spirit came upon Him and made Him “the Christ.” That anointing gave Him the ability to do the mighty works He did.

Acts 10:38 says, “…how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with Him.” And just like Mary told Tyler, that same anointing came into you when you received salvation. The Holy Spirit lives in you. That means you’re not ordinary. You’ve been divinely enabled. So, when you face exams, peer pressure, insecurity, or tough situations, remember you carry supernatural ability on the inside. Glory to God!

message:
The Bible says that in Jesus dwells the fullness of the Godhead in bodily form, meaning anyone who wants to know what God looks like should look at Jesus. No wonder He said to Philip, “he who has seen Me has seen the Father.” Jesus is the express image of the Father’s Person; He is the effulgence of His glory. The Bible says it pleased the Father that in Him (Jesus) should all fullness dwell (Colossians 1:19).

No wonder He said in John 10:30, ”I and My Father are one.” When He said this, the Jews picked up stones and wanted to stone Him. Why? They said, ”...for blasphemy, and because You, being a Man, make Yourself God.” The Jews understood the import of what Jesus meant when he said, “I and My Father are one,” but they considered His words blasphemous because they didn’t know who Jesus was. Jesus is one with the Father; He is the complete embodiment of Deity.

So, if you’ve ever wondered whether God is distant or difficult, study Jesus. Watch how He treated people. Study the Word. When you see Jesus, you won’t need to look for the Father and the Holy Spirit. Jesus is the perfect image and replica of the Godhead. He’s the expression of God’s glory, and by inheritance, not only has He obtained a more excellent name in all of heaven and earth, but the Father has crowned Him with all glory, honour and majesty. He’s the Monarch of the universe, and He’s also your best friend. He’s the express image of the Father’s person.

message:
Mia: “Why can’t I just do what I want? It’s my life!” Jake: “Actually, it’s not. Jesus bought you with something far more expensive than money. You belong to Him now—your body, your choices, and your essence all belong to Him.”

The Bible says, ”you were not redeemed with corruptible things, like silver or gold... but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot” (1 Peter 1:18- 19). If you’re born again, you don’t own yourself. God paid a high price for you, the blood of His Son Jesus. Therefore, as the Bible says, you ought to glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are His. You ought to serve Him diligently and with wholehearted devotion by submitting yourself to His Lordship. You ought to consecrate yourself to Him.

Some people act like they’re the boss of their lives, scrolling, hanging out, or doing whatever feels right, but if you follow Jesus, He’s the CEO of your life, even in your school, friendships, and online world. Your choices, opinions and lifestyle must conform to God’s will as expressed in His Word. Understand that God knows how to take care of what belongs to Him. Since He owns you, it’s His responsibility to protect, keep, bless, help, promote and provide for you. But it’s your responsibility to serve, reverence, and commit your entire being to Him.

When you confessed Jesus as Lord of your life, He became the Lord of your spirit, your soul and your body. You don’t belong to yourself, your friends, or even your followers on social media; you belong to Jesus. You can only do what He wants you to do and go where He wants you to go. The Lord Jesus demands your complete allegiance and unwavering commitment to His will. You’re only permitted to pursue His plans and purposes for your life, for you no longer have a life of your own! He is your life (Colossians 3:4); you’re His property; He bought you with a price.

extras.label: Act

message:
One day, God, through an angel, spoke to a woman called Mary and said, ”...behold, you will conceive in your womb and bring forth a Son, and shall call His name Jesus” (Luke 1:31). When God speaks, His Word is the life of whatever He says. In other words, His Word is the life-carrying faculty of God. His Word has the life of the message that it carries; it becomes whatever it says. If the Word is a message of healing, for example, it’ll carry healing in it. No wonder Jesus likened the Word of God to seed (Luke 8:11). Every seed reproduces after its kind; what you sow is what you reap.

In the same way, when you read your Bible, you’re not just studying for a religious test or checking a box for your morning routine; you’re receiving “living code” that can reprogramme your mindset, your habits, your confidence, and even your future. The Word that God spoke to Mary literally manifested as Jesus; this is why Jesus is the Son of God. He wasn’t born from a human process; He was born from the Word that God spoke. You can’t separate God from His Word. So, the life inside baby Jesus was the life of the Word, and the life of the Word is the life of the Speaker— Almighty God.

Until Jesus was born, nobody ever knew or saw Him. The angels never saw anyone in heaven called Jesus. They only knew the Word. That’s why John said, “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God (John 1:1), then in the fourteenth verse, he said, “and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.” Jesus was the Word of God tabernacled in human flesh. Every move He made was the Word in action, and that was why He was such a wonder. The Word became flesh and dwelt amongst us, and we beheld His glory.

## Speak

Lord Jesus, you’re the living Word of God, full of grace and truth! I worship and adore you for who you are. You’re the Word of life, the living bread from heaven that gives life to every man in the world.

message:
Before we were born again, the Bible says we were”aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world” (Ephesians 2:12). That was a real state of hopelessness indeed. But then the Bible says, “But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ” (Ephesians 2:13). Before the redemptive sacrifice of Jesus on our behalf, we couldn’t approach God because we didn’t even know Him; however, by His death on the cross, Jesus paid the price for our redemption and brought us into peace and union with the Father. He is our Peace.

No wonder the Bible declares, “Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:1). What this implies is that through Christ Jesus, you’ve been set at one with God; you’ve come home in God! His death brokered a peace accord between you and God, bringing about a “ceasefire” as it were. Thus, there’s no need anymore for you to live in apprehension that one day God may recall your wrongs and punish you, no! Jesus has already taken your punishment! The Bible says, the punishment that brought us peace was laid on Jesus on the cross: ”But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement for our peace was upon Him...” (Isaiah 53:5).

This is what makes us bold to face life as champions. We’ve been awakened to the Fatherhood of God. We have unhindered and uninterrupted access to the Father twenty-four hours a day! Refuse to allow the devil deceive you and make you believe that God has a grudge against you—especially after a bad day, a mistake with friends, or failing a test. Jesus already settled every issue on your behalf and established peace between you and the Father: “For He Himself is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of separation” (Ephesians 2:14).

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank You for sending Jesus
body:
Before we were born again, the Bible says we were”aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world” (Ephesians 2:12). That was a real state of hopelessness indeed. But then the Bible says, “But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ” (Ephesians 2:13). Before the redemptive sacrifice of Jesus on our behalf, we couldn’t approach God because we didn’t even know Him; however, by His death on the cross, Jesus paid the price for our redemption and brought us into peace and union with the Father. He is our Peace.

No wonder the Bible declares, “Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:1). What this implies is that through Christ Jesus, you’ve been set at one with God; you’ve come home in God! His death brokered a peace accord between you and God, bringing about a “ceasefire” as it were. Thus, there’s no need anymore for you to live in apprehension that one day God may recall your wrongs and punish you, no! Jesus has already taken your punishment! The Bible says, the punishment that brought us peace was laid on Jesus on the cross: ”But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement for our peace was upon Him...” (Isaiah 53:5).

This is what makes us bold to face life as champions. We’ve been awakened to the Fatherhood of God. We have unhindered and uninterrupted access to the Father twenty-four hours a day! Refuse to allow the devil deceive you and make you believe that God has a grudge against you—especially after a bad day, a mistake with friends, or failing a test. Jesus already settled every issue on your behalf and established peace between you and the Father: “For He Himself is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of separation” (Ephesians 2:14).

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank You for sending Jesus to die for my sins and raising Him from the dead for my right standing with You. I rejoice, having been justified by the blood of Jesus and brought into peaceful friendship with You, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Take five quiet minutes to rest in God’s love. Thank Him that you’re free from condemnation, and let His peace fill your heart.

Colossians 1:20-22; Ephesians 2:13-19

message:
Our opening scripture lets us know that Jesus is the embodiment of all wisdom and knowledge. In other words, not only is He the creator of all things, but He also knows all things. There’s absolutely no topic or subject that He’s deficient in. He knows everything about God, heaven, angels, man and the devil. He also knows everything about your school subjects, your career path, coding, content creation, science projects, music production, business ideas and things beyond your imagination. He can teach you about them better than any professor.

He’s the fountain of all knowledge and can teach you anything. He can give you a word of knowledge, and that knowledge will be what you need to change your world for the better. The world is looking for solutions, and God wants to give His kids the solutions—even students like you. He can give you a word of knowledge about your career. He can give you the medical solution to cancer, HIV/AIDS and other medically incurable ailments. All you need is a word of knowledge from Him, which is only a part or a little piece of everything He knows.

You can receive a word of knowledge from the Lord about your health, job, business, family, academics and finances from time to time. What you need is to recognise that Jesus is knowledge personified, and then trust Him to enrich you in everything, including all utterance and in all knowledge (1 Corinthians 1:5).

message:
Our opening scripture is a sovereign declaration of Deity: at the mention of the Name of Jesus, every knee is compelled to bow. The King James uses the word “things” but the Weymouth translation says, ”...every knee should bow, of beings in Heaven, of those on the earth, and of those in the underworld.” The Name of Jesus has power over all things, and over all beings, whether they be in heaven, on earth, or in hell.

The Reverend Kenneth E. Hagin told the story of how, as a young boy, he died and went to hell. When he got to the gates of hell, a beastly-looking creature took a hold of him to lead him into hell. Suddenly, he said, he heard a voice from far above him. He didn’t understand what the voice said, but he recalled that when the voice spoke, all of hell shook and that evil being let him go. He didn’t know who it was that spoke then, but he found out later it was none other than the Lord Jesus.

Jesus has power and authority over everything that exists. That’s why Peter could say to a man who was physically disabled from birth, “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6), and the man leaped and walked. The Name of Jesus is higher than the name of any sickness or any label people try to put on you! As long as that sickness or problem has a name, it’s subject to the Name of Jesus.

Learn to call the Name of Jesus with confidence and with revelation. It’s not a magic word; it’s a Name vested with all the power of the universe. If you’re facing a challenging situation right now—social pressure, family issues, or physical symptoms—use the Name of Jesus to effect a change.

message:
In the Old Testament, God promised to make the children of Israel a kingdom of priests if they obeyed the covenant and kept His Word (Exodus 19:5-6). Their becoming a kingdom of priests was pre-conditioned on their obedience to God’s voice. However, in the New Testament, the Bible says Jesus has made us kings and priests unto God: ”and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father; to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen” (Revelation 1:6). This isn’t a promise or something that’ll happen in the sweet by and by; it’s a present hour reality.

That means this isn’t something you grow into when you’re older or “more spiritual.” It is who you are right now, even as a teenager. Jesus has made us kings and priests unto God. But the question to ask then is, to what intent did He make us kings and priests? Revelations 5:10 gives us the answer— He made us kings and priests to reign and rule in the earth. The Message Translation says, “He has made us Priest-kings to rule over the earth.” That means you’re not a victim of your circumstances, your school environment, or your background. You’re a master in life. You have authority over the devil and the negative forces of the world.

Kings make decrees, not entreaties. That’s why the Bible says, “Where the word of a king is, there is power” (Ecclesiastes 8:4). This means you don’t have to beg God to do things He’s already authorised you to handle. When you pray, issue commands as a king. Stop saying, “Oh God, please help me not to be scared,” and start saying, “I command fear to leave, in Jesus’ Name!” Having the consciousness that you’re a king will eradicate all beggarly prayers from your life.

title: The Exclusivity of Salvation
excerpt: In the ancient judicial systems of the Mediterranean, a “key” was often the unique symbol of authority given to an official to open the only available gate to a city or a treasury; without…
scripture: “Let it be known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by Him this man stands here before you whole. This is the “stone which was rejected by you builders, which has become the chief cornerstone.’ Nor is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.”
subtitle: (Only The Name Of Jesus Can Save)
prayer: Dear Lord, I reaffirm my conviction that the Name of Jesus is the only name under heaven, given among men by which we must be saved. My heart is stirred with your fire and your power to preach the Gospel in the demonstration of the Spirit and of power, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Pray for one friend who doesn’t know Jesus. Then look for a natural moment to share the Gospel. Be bold.

message:
In the ancient judicial systems of the Mediterranean, a “key” was often the unique symbol of authority given to an official to open the only available gate to a city or a treasury; without this specific key, all other attempts to gain entry were futile. Similarly, salvation isn’t a vast marketplace of multiple paths but a singular, divine provision where Jesus Christ stands as the only access point to the Father.

The Lord Jesus minced no words when it came to salvation; He said: ”I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me” (John 14:6). He never suggested that salvation could come from any other means or through anyone else but by Him.

In a world full of opinions, group chats, and endless takes online, it can feel awkward to say there’s only one way. But Jesus didn’t leave it open-ended. As a teenager, you must be absolutely convinced that there’s no salvation in any other name except the Name of Jesus. In a world that tells you “everything is fine as long as you’re nice,” you need the conviction that Jesus is the only Saviour.

When it dawns on your spirit that Jesus is the only Name given under heaven by which men shall be saved, you’ll preach the Gospel with conviction. When the sinner confesses with his mouth, not his sins, but the Lordship of Jesus, and believes in his heart that God has raised Him from the dead, he’s immediately passed from death unto life.

Understand that salvation isn’t in any other name aside the Name of Jesus. So, when you preach the Gospel, don’t preach apologetically. Don’t be shy about it on your timeline or in person. The whole world needs to know that Christ Jesus is the only Name given to men by which they must be saved.

excerpt: After Jesus rose from the dead, He appeared to His disciples. But one of them, Thomas, wasn’t there.
scripture: “For in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.”
subtitle: (He’s The Complete Embodiment Of Deity)
prayer: Precious Lord Jesus, You’re my Lord and my God! You’re my life, the One I live for and live unto. I worship You for who you are; you’re my everything and the reason for my existence. Thank you for revealing yourself to me today. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, set aside a few minutes for pure worship. Put your phone on “Do Not Disturb,” and just focus on who Jesus is. Let your heart adore Him for His majesty and His deity.

message:
After Jesus rose from the dead, He appeared to His disciples. But one of them, Thomas, wasn’t there. When the Lord appeared to the disciples on another occasion, Thomas was present and the Lord said to Him, ”Reach your finger here, and look at My hands; and reach your hand here, and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing” (John 20:27). With trembling hands, Thomas reached out his hand, felt the holes in the Master’s hands and the hole in His side. Awed at this, Thomas could say nothing else but, ”My Lord and my God!” (John 20:28)!

Peter had called Him, “the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16), but Thomas saw Him in a new light. Notice that when Thomas addressed Him as God, Jesus didn’t say, “No, Thomas, don’t call me God; you’re going too far.” He accepted it because Thomas spoke reality. Jesus is Himself God. The Bible says, ”In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1).

At some point, your faith can’t just be what your parents believe, what your pastor says, or what you hear in church. It has to become real to you. You’ve got to come to that point in your life where you recognise that Jesus is Himself God. The Bible tells us that the fullness of the Godhead bodily dwells in Jesus Christ. When you see Jesus, you wouldn’t need to look out for the Holy Spirit or the Father; He is the complete embodiment of Deity.

No wonder Colossians 1:16-19 says, ”For by Him all things were created that are in heaven and that are on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things were created through Him and for Him. And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist... For it pleased the Father that in Him all the fullness should dwell.” This is not just theology for adults; this is about the risen Christ you believe in, the One who lives in your heart and walks with you every day, even at school or with your friends. Glory to God!

title: No Groping in the Dark
excerpt: John described Jesus as”...the true Light which gives light to every man coming into the world” (John 1:9). There are other lights in the world, but Jesus is the true light!
scripture: “Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, ‘I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.’“
subtitle: (In You Dwells The Light Of Life)
prayer: Dear Jesus, you’re the true light that lights every man that comes into this world; therefore, I recognise you as the only true light that guides me in the path of success, victory and greatness! As I hearken diligently to your Word and practise what it says, my whole life is flooded with light; I’m directed in the path of progress and prosperity. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, look for an opportunity to be a light to someone. It could be a word of encouragement, sharing a scripture, or sharing a copy of the Rhapsody of Realities TeeVo.

message:
John described Jesus as”...the true Light which gives light to every man coming into the world” (John 1:9). There are other lights in the world, but Jesus is the true light! As long as you’ve received Him into your heart and follow Him, you’ll never again walk in darkness. Why is that? It’s because the true light now shines from within you.

Light is that which describes; in other words, it shows you what exists. If you entered a pitch dark room, with no flicker of light, even though that room may be beautifully adorned with state-of-the-art décor, furniture and electronic gadgets, it would be impossible for you to see and appreciate their beauty. That’s because there’s no light describing or showing you the things present in that room.

In the same way, when a man doesn’t have Jesus in his life, he can’t know what true success, fulfilment, peace and prosperity are. Such a fellow gropes in darkness and in utter hopelessness—journeying aimlessly, with a ticket to nowhere. Restless will he be until he finds his rest in Christ Jesus, Who is the True Light that lights every man that comes into this world. He’ll light your life with success, peace, health, joy and prosperity.

That means you don’t have to guess your way through school, friendships, or your future. The Light lives in you. You’re not confused, lost, or stuck. You have divine direction. Recognise Jesus today as the light of your life; recognise Him as the only true light that can guide you in the right path; hearken diligently to His Word, for His Word is light (Psalm 119:105).

title: You’ve Got Zoe!
excerpt: I feel so ordinary—same struggles, same drama, same me,” Asher groaned. “You’re not ordinary. The moment you gave your life to Jesus, God’s own life—Zoe—began to flow through you.
scripture: “And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.”
subtitle: (The God-Life is in You)
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank you for sending Jesus to die for me, therefore, making it possible for me to receive eternal life! I declare that this life is working in every fibre of my being, repelling sickness, disease, infirmity, death, poverty and everything inconsistent with the provisions of the divine life, in the Name of Jesus. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Place your hand on your chest and declare: “Zoe—the life of God—is pumping through my veins right now.”

message:
“I feel so ordinary—same struggles, same drama, same me,” Asher groaned.

“You’re not ordinary. The moment you gave your life to Jesus, God’s own life—Zoe—began to flow through you. That’s not ordinary human life; that’s divine, indestructible life. You’re carrying God’s DNA now!” Grace encouraged.

When Jesus came into this world, He came to do much more than merely die for our sins. He identified His mission in John 10:10: ”...I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.” His death was actually a means to an end: to give us “life in its fullest.” That life is eternal life. Eternal life is not life that goes on endlessly; it’s the life of God. The Greek word is “Zoe,” the essence and quality of divinity! It is the quality of life that God possesses.

The Bible says, ”He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God” (1 John 5:12-13). So, eternal life isn’t something you’re going to have in the sweet by and by; it’s not a promise but a present-hour reality. It’s the possession of the one who has received Jesus.

This new life is the life of God. It’s the very nature of God. Your human life was supplanted with the life and nature of God, the very minute you received Jesus as Lord and Saviour of your life. That life in you makes you indestructible and supernatural. This means you’re not just an ordinary teenager trying to survive school and social pressure. You carry the God-life. You carry divine wisdom, strength, creativity, and boldness inside you. Glory to God!

title: Not Trying to Win
excerpt: Alot of folks know that Jesus defeated Satan through His death on the cross, but not many know exactly how the Master did it.
scripture: “And having disarmed principalities and powers, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them in it.”
subtitle: (We’re On A Victory Parade In Christ)
prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, I thank you for rendering the devil powerless and giving me the victory and authority to keep him that way. I see how helplessly and completely defeated he is. As I resist him steadfast in the faith, I know for sure that he flees away in terror. Thank you for giving me permanent victory over the devil and the cohorts of hell. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: When fear or intimidation tries to creep in today, you should laugh and say: “Ha! You’re already defeated. I already won in Christ.”

message:
Alot of folks know that Jesus defeated Satan through His death on the cross, but not many know exactly how the Master did it. When Jesus died, He didn’t ascend to heaven that same day; He had been made sin for us (2 Corinthians 5:21) and so had to go to hell on behalf of all men. When He got to hell, there was an actual combat between Jesus and the forces of darkness. The Bible says, ”the hostile princes and rulers He shook off from Himself, and boldly displayed them as His conquests...” (Colossians 2:15, WNT).

In hell, all the demons grappled with Jesus; they tried to make Him bow to Satan, but Jesus declined and threw them off Him: He then defeated Satan and rendered him powerless. The Bible tells us that Jesus went over to the side of Hades where Abraham’s bosom was, opened the prison doors, and led out all the righteous men that were in there, including Abraham, David, Solomon and many others (Ephesians 4:8).

It doesn’t matter to us whatever hierarchy of demons exists; they’re all powerless. Jesus has defeated their overall boss, and that victory is yours! Remember, the Bible doesn’t say, ”Resist demons, and they’ll flee from you”; it says”Resist the devil, and he will flee from you” (James 4:7). The boss of all demons himself flees from you, terrified when you resist him in the Name of Jesus, much less his little demons.

So, when fear tries to creep in before an exam, when peer pressure hits, or when negative thoughts whisper that you’re not enough, remind yourself: the devil is already defeated. You’re not trying to win. You already won in Christ.

title: The Anchor of Your Life
excerpt: I know I’m smart, but I keep making silly errors on my tests,” Zoe complained.
scripture: “Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste”
subtitle: (Let Christ Be Your Rock And Firm Foundation)
prayer: Dear Father, you’ve taken me out of the miry clay and planted my feet firmly upon the rock, Christ Jesus. Now I know that I’ll remain unshakable even when the storms of life billow against me, for I’ve been securely planted on the true foundation—Christ Jesus the Rock. Thus, no situation can overwhelm me in this life because I’m not just a hearer but a doer of your Word. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Stand tall and declare your identity aloud: “I’m born of God, victorious in Christ!” Do it 3 times.

message:
“I know I’m smart, but I keep making silly errors on my tests,” Zoe complained.

Bryan nodded: “Maybe that’s because you’re building on and trusting in your intelligence and not in Christ.”

The Prophet Isaiah, in the scripture above, spoke prophetically about the “stone” which the Lord God would lay in Zion, and I want you to observe the way this “stone” is described. First, he refers to it as “a tried stone,” secondly, he calls it “a precious corner stone,” and then thirdly, he refers to it as “a sure foundation.” Being a “tried stone” means it’s been tested and proven; then, as “a precious corner stone” it means it’s the most important stone in the building; while as a “sure foundation” it means you can stake your life on it.

That’s who Jesus is; He’s the only true foundation upon which you should build your life. That’s why He said in Luke 6:47-49: ”Whoever comes to Me, and hears My sayings and does them, I will show you whom he is like: He is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. And when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently against that house, and could not shake it, for it was founded on the rock. But he who heard and did nothing is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream beat vehemently; and immediately it fell. And the ruin of that house was great.”

It matters the foundation upon which your life is built. The Bible says, “For no other foundation can anyone lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ” (1 Corinthians 3:11). In school, when exams feel overwhelming; online, when trends and opinions keep changing; with friends, when loyalty is tested; or on the field or stage when everyone is watching—when you build on Christ, you won’t collapse when pressure comes. In the face of adversity, you’ll be unshakable because on Christ the Solid Rock you stand.

message:
After His resurrection, the Lord Jesus instructed His disciples to meet Him on a certain mountain in Galilee. There, He declared to them that all authority in heaven and in earth had been given unto Him. That means men, angels, demons, things in heaven, earth and under the earth are subject to Jesus and must obey His voice. However, Jesus is presently in heaven, and He doesn’t exercise His authority from there. The way He exercises his authority today is through us—His Church, which is His Body.

That’s why He said to us, “Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations....” The Master delegated His authority to us to function in His Name and make disciples of the nations of the earth on His behalf. In His Name, you have the power to cast out devils, tame the forces of nature, and mobilise angels to work for your good. When you’re conscious of this reality, you’ll win, no matter what comes against you.

Think of it like being given the master key to every door in the school—you can walk through any obstacle and succeed. Jesus gave you the power of attorney (the right, influence, and legal power) to act in His place! Whatever you declare in His name, He’s back of it; therefore, be bold to use the Name of Jesus to effect changes in your school atmosphere, your family life, or any toxic situation you might face.

Let it dawn on your spirit that Jesus has given you His authority. The enemy and his forces may try to intimidate you, but when you command them in the Name of Jesus, they’ve got to obey! The power that created and sustains the universe is backing you. Use your authority in Christ Jesus to effect a change.

subtitle: (Trust the Scriptwriter of Your Life)

I rejoice at the assurance from your Word that there’s nothing for me to fear since you’re the author and perfecter of my success. message:
While exiled on the Island of Patmos, John the apostle was caught up into the realm of the Spirit and received revelations from the Lord. He said”I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, as of a trumpet, saying, ‘I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last,’ and, “What you see, write in a book and send it to the seven churches which are in Asia: to Ephesus, to Smyrna, to Pergamos, to Thyatira, to Sardis, to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea” (Revelation 1:10-11).

The Lord also said to him, ”...Do not be afraid; I am the First and the Last. I am He who lives, and was dead, and behold, I am alive forevermore. Amen...” (Revelation 1:17-18). The only one who fits that description is Jesus. He’s the One that died but is alive forevermore. He’s “Alpha and Omega”; the first, and the last; the beginning and the ending! This is the picture of the glorified Christ, and He says to you today, “Fear not; I am the first and the last.”

In other words, He’s telling you that in your journey of success, He’s with you. No wonder the Bible says in Hebrews 12:2, ”looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith....” He’s the author and perfecter of your faith. This means there’s nothing for you to fear as you journey through life. He’s right there with you every phase of your journey.

That means you don’t need to stress over your examination, your college applications, or your future career; He has seen the end already, and He said, “Fear not.” This ought to make life exciting and stress-free for you, knowing that you’re right in between the first and the last! You ought to go through life with confidence, for the King of the universe, who is the author and perfecter of all things, is with you.

message:
“I feel like the devil is winning. Everything keeps going wrong,” David moaned.

“No way! Jesus already beat him up so bad he’s got nothing left. He’s basically Mr Nothing now. You’re the one with the authority. Next time he tries to flex, just remind him who’s really in charge—you!” Rose fired back.

Satan is a defeated foe. The Lord Jesus despoiled him, stripped him of his armour, and openly triumphed over him. He left him with nothing (Colossians 2:15). Thus, you can also refer to Satan as “Mr Nothing!” He’s nothing, he’s got nothing, and he can do nothing! He’s not a factor; therefore, never be afraid of him, because you’re superior to him; he doesn’t count.

As a new creation, not only has Jesus given you power and authority to cast Satan out, He also made you superior to him and all his demons. When we became God’s children by being born again, we became one with God; we became one divine creation with our heavenly Father, having His very life. That life in us makes us the “uninfectable breed!” It makes us superior to Satan and impregnable to sickness, disease and infirmity.

The resurrection of Jesus made a champion of you. The Bible says you were raised together with and made to sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus (Ephesians 2:6). You’re seated with Christ, far above all principalities and powers. That means you’re superior to them! You occupy the place of authority in Christ, far above Satan and everything that’s connected to him. So, you don’t have to be afraid of nightmares, pressure from friends, or intimidation at school. Glory to God!

excerpt: The Lord Jesus initiated and established peace between God and man through His death on the cross; He reconciled humanity back to God.
scripture: “And you, who once were alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now He has reconciled in the body of His flesh through death, to present you holy, and blameless, and above reproach in His sight”
subtitle: (The Legal Reality of Being “Beyond Reproach”)
prayer: Thank you, Father, for the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus Christ, through which I’ve been presented holy, blameless and above reproach in your sight! Thank you for imparting to me your nature of righteousness, thereby granting me the right to stand before you without any guilt, condemnation or inferiority, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Make a list of your top three goals and consciously declare that you’re “above reproach” and qualified for success in each.

message:
The Lord Jesus initiated and established peace between God and man through His death on the cross; He reconciled humanity back to God. Man had become alienated from the life of God through Adam’s disobedience, but the Bible says Jesus has reconciled us with the Father in the body of His flesh through death, to present us holy, blameless and above reproach before the Father.

Notice that the scripture doesn’t say “He shall reconcile you in the body of His flesh through death” but that “He has reconciled you!” That’s not a promise; it’s a statement of fact. Jesus has already reconciled you with the Father. The latter part of the opening Scripture clearly reveals to us the reason for the reconciliation: ”...to present you holy, blameless, and above reproach in His sight.” In other words, the death of Jesus on the cross of Calvary was the perfect sacrifice that qualified you to stand in the presence of God without any inferiority, guilt or condemnation.

As far as God is concerned, you’re without blemish and free from all accusation; you’re holy, blameless and beyond reproach. That means God takes responsibility for your wrongs. He takes the blame for all your mistakes and errors. Even when you feel embarrassed about something you did at school or online, God still sees you as righteous in Christ. Men may blame you, scorn you for your errors and look at you as unholy, but God says you’re holy, flawless, perfect and impossible to fault in His sight! This is God’s testimony concerning you, and that’s the testimony that counts. No wonder He calls us “holy brethren” (Hebrews 3:1). Halleluyah!

title: Your Good Shepherd
excerpt: When Jesus said, ”I am the good shepherd; and I know My sheep, and am known by My own” (John 10:14), He wanted us to know His primary responsibility towards us, which is to nurture, guide…
scripture: “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
subtitle: (He Cares About Every Part Of Your Life)
prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, I recognise you as my Good Shepherd. I know I’ll never lack or be in want of any good thing, for you lay me down in the field of abundance. I rejoice, knowing that you’re with me, shielding and protecting me from all evil and guiding me to streams of peaceful waters. Your rod and staff comfort me. Surely, your kindness and love will always encompass me each day of my life, and I’ll live forever under your divine protection. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Set a five-minute timer to sit in silence, speak in tongues and receive guidance from the Holy Spirit on a specific decision you need to make today.

message:
When Jesus said, ”I am the good shepherd; and I know My sheep, and am known by My own” (John 10:14), He wanted us to know His primary responsibility towards us, which is to nurture, guide, protect and provide for us. “Shepherd” in Greek is “poimen,” which also means “Pastor.” Thus, Jesus described Himself as the “Good Pastor.” You need to know and relate to the Lord Jesus as your shepherd and bread-provider. That way, you won’t need to struggle through life trying to make things work on your own or feel like everything depends on you figuring it out.

Simply follow the leading of the Lord Jesus, your Good Shepherd, and He’ll guide you into everything you require for the good life. He’ll guide you in your classes, when you’re preparing for exams, when you’re choosing friends, when you’re dealing with peer pressure, and even when you’re trying to decide what to post, say, or respond to in a group chat. Your Good Shepherd loved you enough to die for you, and He lives in your heart today, guiding you by the Holy Spirit in the path of God’s destiny for your life.

Remember, Jesus loves you more than you love yourself; He loves you more than life itself, and He proved it by dying for you on the Cross. That’s the character of the good shepherd: he lays his life down for his sheep. Always be conscious of Christ’s irrevocable love for you. He is your Good Shepherd, and He cares about you.

When you feel misunderstood, left out, pressured to fit in, or worried about your future, He hasn’t stepped away. He’s right there, invested in every part of your story. He’s more willing and enthusiastic about your success, progress and prosperity than you could ever be. He went to the uttermost length to see to it that you turn out right in life.

message:
In the New Testament, God expects us to offer Him sacrifices but not on physical altars. From our opening scripture, we see that under the New Testament, Jesus is our Great High Priest, meaning He’s the one ordained by God to receive the sacrifices we have to offer: “Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name” (Hebrews 13:15).

Now, that’s another way of saying, “By Him therefore, let us offer the calves of our lips, giving thanks to His Name.” The expression “giving thanks to His Name” is akin to the Greek word “homologeo,” which means “to make confessions to His Name.” It means “to speak the same thing in consent”; in other words, to agree with and confess what God has said about you.

Every time you make the right confessions, God responds because your words are in agreement with His Word. When you declare, “I’m the righteousness of God in Christ” (2 Corinthians 5:21), or “I’m the best among my peers”, you’re speaking in consent with His Word, and it’s established.

Another scripture where the same Greek word (homologeo) was used is Hebrews 13:15, and it says, “Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.”

A better rendering reads: “…the fruit of our lips, making confessions to His Name.” Here, the Spirit of God, through the writer, is referring to confessions that are of praise—confessions that carry thanksgiving. Your confession must be based on what’s in the document, which is the Word of God. Hallelujah!

“Are you serious? You actually prayed before posting that?” Wesley asked, laughing.

“Yeah,” Zara shrugged. “If Jesus is really Lord of my life, He should care about my posts too, right?”

“Even your captions?”

“Especially my captions.”

Zara understood something many people miss. Calling Jesus “Lord” isn’t just something you say during an altar call. One major thing you need for a successful, vibrant, prosperous, and fulfilling year—even as a student navigating school, friendships, social media, and big dreams—is to be more conscious of the Lordship of Jesus. When you say “Jesus is Lord of my life,” you need to understand that it’s much more than a religious axiom. You’re not merely talking of someone who saved you from your sins and healed you from sickness. It means He’s boss over your life; He’s the One with supreme authority; He controls everything that has to do with your life.

Some have only been acquainted with Him as Saviour, but He’s more than a Saviour; He is Lord! That means Ruler and Master, one who has the preeminence, and to whom service and obedience are due. You must get to know Jesus and walk with Him every day as Lord in your family, academics, friendships, online interactions, future career plans, and everything that has to do with your life. In other words, let Him take preeminence.

Remember, He’s the only wise God, whose bidding you must do and whose leading alone you must follow. Recognise His Lordship today and submit to the supremacy of His will, counsel and wisdom.

## Speak

Lord Jesus, I recognize you as my Lord, Master and Ruler, the One with supreme authority and preeminence, to whom I owe allegiance. I believe with all my heart and declare with my mouth that you’re Lord over every circumstance and everything that has to do with my life. With the help of the Holy Spirit, I walk in the consciousness and revelation of your Lordship over my life every day! Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
Ever heard the saying, “Life is not a bed of roses”? Well, not the Christian life! It is, indeed, a bed of roses. Why else would the Psalmist say, “Because the Lord is my Shepherd, I have everything I need! He lets me rest in the meadow grass and leads me beside the quiet streams…” (Psalms 23:1-2 TLB). However, it’s a bed of roses that comes with tests and trials. Such challenging times are what our opening verse refers to as “the day of adversity.” Some believers dread such times and fervently pray to God to never to allow them go through them. However, to avoid situations that challenge your faith is to limit your spiritual growth and reduce your chances of promotion.

James 1:2 says, “My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into various trials.” Why would God admonish you to rejoice when tests and challenges come at you on all sides? It’s because He knows that victory is in your spirit. Having been born again, you’ve become an overcomer and more than a conqueror. Consequently, no situation that you face should overwhelm you.

There are things that make you tough as a Christian, and if you don’t welcome them, you’d remain at the same level of faith and maturity. Therefore, your adversaries are important in the toughening process, so never pray against them, no matter what troubles, problems and difficulties they bring your way. See challenges as spiritual training that builds your strength and confidence in God. Welcome them to strengthen your faith-muscles, and you’ll discover they’re the agents for your promotion.

I have known only one journey in life: upward and forward. I don’t have ups and downs. That doesn’t mean challenges don’t come, but I always win. No matter what you face in school, at home, or with friends, refuse to quit. So welcome challenges; welcome troubles because they’re the contrary winds that help to drive your roots deeper. And the more the wind blows against you, the higher you’ll fly. Hallelujah!

## Prayer

message:
Years ago, just right after I said to someone once, “Trust is not just given to you; you earn it,” the Spirit of God interrupted me and said, “No, son, you’re wrong. You don’t earn trust; trust is a gift.” I was surprised because, before that time, I thought trust was earned. But here was God saying no man could earn trust. The Lord then guided me through the Scriptures, and I saw things I didn’t realize and came to the conclusion that trust was indeed a gift as He had taught me.

No man in himself deserves to be trusted, no matter how trustworthy he seems, not even your closest friends. If you’re honest with yourself, you’ll discover that even you are not totally trustworthy. For example, there may have been times when you promised to pray for someone, help with homework, or show up for a friend, and you didn’t. What if that one’s life, for whom you were to pray, depended solely on your prayers at that time? But God, nevertheless, has chosen to trust you with the Gospel (2 Corinthians 5:18).

This is something that friends, classmates, teammates, co-workers, and spouses need to learn. In school, at home, and online, people don’t always “qualify” for your trust. You trust them because you love them and you expect the best of them. The man who can trust another is greater than the one he trusts, because trust helps him gain a level of faith to make provisions for the errors of others.

Those who can’t trust others are men of small minds. When you begin to see life the way God sees it, you’ll stop judging people only by their mistakes; you’ll start learning to trust people and not rate them according to who they are and what they do (2 Corinthians 5:16), but according to your expectation of them. Learning to trust doesn’t mean being careless; it means choosing love, forgiveness, and faith over fear.

## Prayer
body:
Years ago, just right after I said to someone once, “Trust is not just given to you; you earn it,” the Spirit of God interrupted me and said, “No, son, you’re wrong. You don’t earn trust; trust is a gift.” I was surprised because, before that time, I thought trust was earned. But here was God saying no man could earn trust. The Lord then guided me through the Scriptures, and I saw things I didn’t realize and came to the conclusion that trust was indeed a gift as He had taught me.

No man in himself deserves to be trusted, no matter how trustworthy he seems, not even your closest friends. If you’re honest with yourself, you’ll discover that even you are not totally trustworthy. For example, there may have been times when you promised to pray for someone, help with homework, or show up for a friend, and you didn’t. What if that one’s life, for whom you were to pray, depended solely on your prayers at that time? But God, nevertheless, has chosen to trust you with the Gospel (2 Corinthians 5:18).

You trust them because you love them and you expect the best of them. The man who can trust another is greater than the one he trusts, because trust helps him gain a level of faith to make provisions for the errors of others.

Those who can’t trust others are men of small minds. When you begin to see life the way God sees it, you’ll stop judging people only by their mistakes; you’ll start learning to trust people and not rate them according to who they are and what they do (2 Corinthians 5:16), but according to your expectation of them. Learning to trust doesn’t mean being careless; it means choosing love, forgiveness, and faith over fear.

## Prayer

Dear Father, I thank you for the grace to see people the way you see them. Thank you for your love that’s shed abroad in my heart by the Holy Spirit and for the ability to trust people and not rate them according to who they are and what they do, but according to your love and purpose for their lives, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

body:
“Mia sighed, ‘I’m really worried about my brother. He’s been sick for days, and I don’t know what to do.’

Daniel replied, ‘Have you tried praying for him? You know God can heal, even from a distance.’

Mia paused. ‘You mean… I can believe for him too?’

Daniel smiled. “Yes. That’s exactly what faith is about.’”

The Bible tells several inspiring stories of people who had faith for others to be healed. Even when they couldn’t bring their loved ones to Jesus physically, they got a miracle. This means that you can have faith for someone to receive their miracle.

A certain Centurion, whose dear servant was sick and ready to die, is one of such. When he heard of Jesus, he sent the elders of the Jews to beseech Him that He would come and heal his servant. Jesus agreed and followed them. But just before they got to the Centurion’s house, the Centurion sent a message to Jesus and said, “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof; therefore I did not even think myself worthy to come to You. But say the word, and my servant will be healed” (Luke 7:2–7).

When Jesus heard the words of the Centurion, He marvelled at his faith and turned to those that followed Him and said, “I have not found such great faith, not even in Israel!” By the time the messengers got back to the Centurion’s house, they found the hitherto sick servant perfectly healed and made whole (Luke 7:9–10). The faith of his master prevailed, and he (the servant) got a miracle!

So, the question is: What do you want? The Centurion was very clear about what he wanted for his servant, and he was convinced that the Master’s words were powerful enough to give him a miracle. The same applies to you today! Stand in the gap for others who are weak and helpless by asking the Father, in the Name of Jesus, for a miracle on their behalf, and believe with confidence that God hears you and responds.

## Prayer

I pray today for those who are sick and in hospitals, especially those amongst them who are preachers and ministers of the Gospel, that your healing power will mantle them, breaking the stronghold of sickness and disease off them, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
Society may place limits on you; your background, where you’re from, your school, your grades, your family situation, or your finances could place limits on you. But there’s a life without limits; that’s the life Jesus brought to us; it’s the transcendent life of glory where there are no limitations—A life unlimited by sickness, disease, failure, the devil, fear, discouragement, or low self-esteem!

Jesus proved it was possible to live this triumphant life when He walked the earth. He lived a life that was greater than anything that existed on the terrestrial plane. He refused to be limited by the circumstances of this world. He tamed nature. The Bible tells us how He defied the laws of nature by walking on water “in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went to them, walking on the sea” (Matthew 14:25), and hushing the sea to sleep “Then He arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace, be still!’ And the wind ceased and there was a great calm” (Mark 4:39).

Satan, death, nor the grave could limit Him. When He died, the Bible says through that death, He paralyzed him that has the power of death, that is, the devil “that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil” (Hebrews 2:14). Thereafter, He rose triumphantly from the grave. This is the life to which you’ve been called, where nothing can hinder or place limits on you. According to our opening scripture, you received this life when you were born again.

Now that you have this life in you, refuse to function according to your natural human abilities and take up God’s limitless power that’s been deposited in your spirit! Don’t think “I can’t do it,” “I’m not good enough,” or “I’m too young.” God gave you His ability so you won’t have to function with your own limited abilities but with His limitless and inexhaustible strength.

prayer: Dear Father, I thank you, in the Name of Jesus, for raising me and making me to sit together in heavenly places in Christ! message:
“Do you think God is building us mansions in heaven?” Jake asked.

“I used to,” Daniel replied. “But it’s actually something better.”

“Better than a mansion?!” Jake’s eyes widened. “How?”

Well, let’s see what the Lord Jesus really meant. In John 14:2–3 Jesus said, “In My Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to Myself; that where I am, there you may be also.” Many misinterpret this portion of Scripture to mean that when someone gives his life to Christ, God starts building a mansion for him (or her) in heaven. This sounds exciting, but that’s not what Jesus meant. In the verse above, Jesus wasn’t talking about heaven; He was referring to our place in Christ.

So, not only is Christ a Person, but He’s also a place. That’s what the Apostle Paul alludes to in our opening scripture. We are in Christ. We’ve been made to sit together with Him in heavenly places (Ephesians 2:6), which means the place Jesus prepared is not somewhere far away in the future, but where we already are in Him today. You came into Christ when you were born again; it’s a heavenly realm called Zion, the city of the living God. That’s the city of our habitation: “But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels” (Hebrews 12:22).

message:
King Nebuchadnezzar once had a dream that stressed him out big time. He called all his wise men together. “Tell me the dream AND the meaning, or you’re dead!” he yelled. The wise men froze—they had no idea what the king dreamed. They told him: “…There is not a man on earth who can show the king’s matter: …there is no king, lord, nor ruler, who asked such things of any magician, astrologer, or Chaldean. And it is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is none other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh” (Daniel 2:10–11).

The king got furious and ordered all the wise men, including Daniel and his friends, to be executed (Daniel 2:12–13). But Daniel stepped forward and asked for some time. He and his friends prayed that night. God revealed the dream and its meaning to Daniel, who in turn revealed it to the king. Nebuchadnezzar had to agree and proclaim that indeed Daniel had an excellent spirit.

With the Holy Spirit, you won’t have to feel lost about school choices, friendships, plans, or big decisions. The Bible says: “The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and our children forever…” (Deuteronomy 29:29). Think about it: The Holy Spirit can guide your thoughts, inspire your actions, and help you make choices that match God’s plan. Glory to God!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for the abiding presence of your Spirit who illuminates my mind with the Word and grants me quick understanding in all things, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
One question many Christians have asked is: “How do I know when the Holy Spirit is talking to me?” The first and most important thing is to receive the Holy Spirit into your heart. When you do, He doesn’t just visit. He lives in you and becomes your constant guide.

The Bible says, “He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit” (1 Corinthians 6:17), so you and the Holy Spirit are connected. Soon, you’ll notice His voice talking to you from your spirit. Romans 8:16 says the Spirit “bears witness with our spirit,” so your own spirit confirms that it’s Him speaking. He is the best Teacher, so first you receive Him, and then He will guide you to recognize His voice.

Another important thing to do in knowing the voice of the Spirit is to get really familiar with the Bible, because His words always line up with Scripture. He won’t tell you to do something that goes against God’s Word. John 16:13 says, “However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.” If you know the Word well, you’ll notice whenever the Holy Spirit talks to you, because His voice always agrees with Scripture. His voice and the Bible always match.

The Holy Spirit is the Master Communicator and knows the best way to grab your attention. The Bible gives the example of Moses and the burning bush. The bush was on fire, but it didn’t burn up. God just needed Moses to notice it. When Moses moved closer, God spoke—but only after He got Moses’ attention. After that, Moses didn’t need another burning bush to know God’s voice. The same is true for you: He can speak while you’re doing homework, texting a friend, or deciding what to do in a tough situation. He will teach you to hear Him clearly.
