body:
You’ve got to think about heaven; otherwise, everything you’re doing in the world is worthless. But we already belong in that city, which the old songwriter referred to as the “heavenly city bright”; it’s called Zion, the city of the great King. We’re citizens of that bright heavenly city. The night refers to the darkness, but we’re children of the day. Being born of God, you were born into the everlasting day; no more night in your life. Glory to God!

The Bible says, “…the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day” (Proverbs 4:18). The darkness is gone. The light has come. Darkness refers to everything sinister, evil, depraved, and of Satan. But light refers to God and all that’s good and the divine provisions of Christ in His Gospel. No wonder the Bible says, “Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness” (1 Thessalonians 5:5). excerpt: The greatest truth in all the world is this: Jesus Christ is alive! This is not a story from history or a doctrine preserved through time.
scripture: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.”
subtitle: (Jesus Christ Is Alive Today)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the consistency of your vision and the revelation of Jesus Christ alive today. The Church is marching forward, expanding and spreading the message of your love, power and grace through the nooks and crannies of the earth, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
The greatest truth in all the world is this: Jesus Christ is alive! This is not a story from history or a doctrine preserved through time. It’s the very pulse of our faith, the power of the Gospel, and the living reality of Christianity. The same Jesus who walked the streets of Galilee, who healed the sick and raised the dead, is still doing the same works through us—His Church—today.

When I began holding crusades many years ago, my passion was to present this living Christ to the people. Every handbill declared it boldly: “Presenting Jesus Christ Alive!” It wasn’t a slogan; it was a revelation. I knew that Jesus was not confined to the pages of Scripture or the memories of history—He was, and still is, the same yesterday, today, and forever!

In one of our early camp meetings, the Spirit of God gave us the theme: “Beyond the Written Pages.” How powerful! The Bible isn’t just a record of what God once did; it’s the revelation of what He’s still doing today through His Spirit. The Word has leapt off the pages and lives in us— hallelujah!

Christianity is not about following a historical figure; it’s the manifestation of the living Christ in and through you. This is our calling—to take this message to the nations, to let the world know: Jesus is alive and His life is in us!

So, wherever you are, whatever you do—present Him alive! Let His love, His power, and His glory flow through you. The world must know: Jesus Christ is alive today! Hallelujah!

excerpt: Not long ago, I watched a documentary about an ancient city surrounded by mighty walls and fortified gates.
scripture: “...and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.”
subtitle: (Dominate Your World)

message:
Not long ago, I watched a documentary about an ancient city surrounded by mighty walls and fortified gates. Those gates weren’t just entry points; they represented power, authority, and control. Whoever controlled the gate ruled the city. It reminds me of God’s declaration to Abraham after he offered Isaac to be sacrificed: “Thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.” What a profound promise!

Now, this wasn’t merely about physical territory—it was about dominion. In Bible days, the gate of a city was where leaders made decisions, where trade happened, and justice was executed. So when God said Abraham’s seed would possess the gate, He was declaring dominion in every sphere of influence—spiritually, economically, and politically. Glory to God!

And here’s what’s even more amazing: this promise wasn’t for Abraham alone. Galatians 3:16 reveals that “the seed” is Christ—and if you belong to Christ, then you’re Abraham’s seed and an heir according to the promise. That means you’re the one to possess the gates! You’re not at the mercy of circumstances or the systems of this world. You’ve been empowered to reign, to subdue, and to influence your world for Jesus Christ.

You can take charge in your school, online spaces, your family, or anywhere God places you. How? Through prayer, your words, and your attitude of faith. When things look dark, don’t stay quiet. Don’t allow evil to dominate your environment. Refuse to sit idly by. Speak the Word with authority and take charge in the Name of Jesus!

Exercise dominion in every area of your life and your world. You’re not here to barely survive—you’re here to reign! So, rise up and speak. Take charge through prayer, your faith-filled declarations, and action. Don’t watch evil dominate your environment; cast it out. Possess the “gates” through the authority in the Name of Jesus.

message:
The blessing of Abraham isn’t just a nice Bible story—it’s the very foundation of the Gospel! When the Lord said to Abraham, “I will bless you and make your name great… and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.” (Genesis 12:2–3 NKJV), He wasn’t just talking about material things. He was revealing His plan to pour out His love, grace, and kindness on all humanity through faith in Jesus Christ.

The Apostle Paul explains that this same blessing has come to us through Christ: “That the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith” (Galatians 3:14 NKJV). This means if you’re born again, you’re not trying to get blessed—you already are! You’re Abraham’s seed, the heir of God’s promises, and a carrier of divine favour.

When you received Christ, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise. That seal marks you as God’s own and guarantees your access to all the blessings and benefits of the Abrahamic covenant. So refuse to live small. You carry the same blessing that made Abraham great, the same power that caused Isaac to prosper in famine, and the same grace that distinguished Joseph in a foreign land. You’re an answer to the needs of your generation!

Never forget—you’re the evidence that God’s promise to Abraham is alive today. Live boldly, talk boldly, and bless your world with the life of God in you. You are the expression of the blessing! Hallelujah!

message:
Romans 6:10–11 (NIV) reveals your present reality in Christ. It says, “The death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God. In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.” This isn’t a promise—it’s a statement of fact! You’re dead to sin and alive to God. That’s your place, your position, and your identity in Christ.

The “old you” that was bound by wrong desires, guilt, and fear no longer exists; he was crucified with Christ. Now, you live in the newness of life—righteous, victorious, and full of glory. You’re not under the control of sin, failure, or fear; you reign in the power of divine life.

The Bible says, “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body” (Romans 6:12). That means you can say “no” to anything that doesn’t reflect who you are in Christ. You have authority over your thoughts, your words, and your actions. You’re not weak or helpless; you’re full of God’s strength and wisdom.

As a child of God, when you walk into a place, things change for the better! Your presence brings peace, joy, and excellence because you carry the life of God. The world is waiting to see that life expressed through you—at school, at home, and among your friends.

So square up! Think like someone who carries Jesus inside. Let this be your consciousness: you’re the manifestation of Christ’s righteousness. You function in His divine order and His divine power, bringing His glory everywhere.

title: It’s Your Identity
excerpt: In an art gallery, no painting is ever mistaken for the artist himself. Yet, every masterpiece carries the signature and essence of the one who created it.
scripture: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
subtitle: (You’re A Walking Garden Of Divine Fruits)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I bear the fruits of righteousness, and I walk in the glory of God, manifesting love, joy, peace and all the virtues of the recreated human spirit. My life is an expression of God’s divine nature, and I walk in the consciousness of who I am in Christ, radiating divine excellence.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Today, make a conscious effort to give expression to the fruits of your spirit.

message:
In an art gallery, no painting is ever mistaken for the artist himself. Yet, every masterpiece carries the signature and essence of the one who created it. When people behold the artwork, they immediately recognize its origin. In the same way, God designed you to carry His signature—to be identified by the fruit you bear.

The Lord Jesus declared in Luke 6:44 NKJV, “For every tree is known by its own fruit…” You don’t call a mango tree an apple tree; the tree is identified by the fruit it produces. This is true of your recreated human spirit. The moment you were born again, God filled you with His very essence, enabling you to produce divine fruits.

Let’s take a look at our opening scripture that talks about the fruits of the recreated human spirit. These aren’t just “nice personality traits”; they’re who you really are in Christ. Think of it like this: if the Spirit lives in you, then you’re a tree, and these are your natural fruits. The first fruit listed is love—that makes you a love-tree. Not the romantic kind of love, but a love that sees people the way God sees them.

Next is joy —so your name is Joy. You’re not waiting for circumstances to make you happy; joy flows out of your spirit like a river. And peace? That’s you too. You’re the calm in the middle of drama, pressure, or anxiety. You’re the one who doesn’t spiral when things go wrong—you radiate peace.

Patience, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance—all these are not qualities you’re struggling to acquire; they’re fruits you naturally bear. That’s who you are! So never say, “I’m not a patient person.” No, your spiritual DNA carries patience because the Spirit of God lives in you. And here’s something even more glorious: Ephesians 1:17 NKJV calls God “the Father of glory.” If He’s the Father of Glory, then what does that make you? You are Glory! You’re the outshining of God’s beauty, the visible expression of His excellence. When men see you, they see God’s masterpiece at work.

title: No Sickness Here!
excerpt: I once heard of a farmer who carefully fenced his vineyard, not to restrict the vines, but to protect them. Within those boundaries, the plants flourished and yielded abundantly.
scripture: “Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.”
subtitle: (The Word Guarantees Your Divine Health)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: Dear Father, I thank you for the gift of divine health, my inheritance in Christ Jesus. I’m healthy and strong, and I walk in the fullness of the divine life. Every fibre of my being is inundated with eternal life. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Speak words of health, wholeness and wellness over your body now.

message:
I once heard of a farmer who carefully fenced his vineyard, not to restrict the vines, but to protect them. Within those boundaries, the plants flourished and yielded abundantly. In much the same way, God has given us His Word as our “fence”—not to limit us, but to preserve us in divine health, strength, and victory.

Too many live at the mercy of sickness—hospital today, pharmacy tomorrow—tossed back and forth in a cycle of weakness This shouldn’t be your experience as a child of God. Don’t allow such in your life; refuse to let Satan toy with your body. The moment he notices you yield to minor symptoms, he attempts to escalate them. But praise God, you have the power to stop him!

Remember the words of the Master to Simon Peter: “Simon, Simon! Indeed, Satan has asked for you, that he may sift you as wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail” (Luke 22:31-32 NKJV). The Master didn’t pray that Peter wouldn’t be tested but that his faith would not fail. That’s the same with you today—your faith is the victory that overcomes the world!

Don’t settle for a life of recurring ailments. If you’ve been in and out of school because of health issues, you can decide today that “enough is enough.” Declare boldly: “I refuse to live in sickness and weakness. I have eternal life, and therefore I walk in divine health every day.”

While as a result of ignorance you might have tolerated sickness in the past, it should no longer have a place in your life now that you know the truth. Don’t ignore pain, hoping rest will solve it. No—release your faith through words. Your tongue is your instrument of victory! Use it to rebuke infirmity, command wholeness, and establish divine health in your body. Every time you speak God’s Word, you are setting your world in order. Speak life, speak strength, speak health! The Holy Spirit has empowered you to reign over sickness, disease, and every work of darkness.

message:
The Lord Jesus didn’t come to start a religion; He came to give us life—divine life! He gave up everything, even His own life, to make us sons of God. When you understand the depth of His sacrifice, it changes your entire perspective. You begin to live victoriously every day, knowing that His death, burial, and resurrection brought you an everlasting life—free from sin, sickness, poverty, and death.

The sacrifice of Jesus wasn’t a mere symbol; it was real, and so is the freedom it brought you. The Bible says, “Knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over Him.” (Romans 6:9 NKJV). Glory to God! Death has no dominion over you either because you’re in Him.

Through His resurrection, He imparted His very nature to you. You’re now alive unto God! You’re not just forgiven—you’re recreated in righteousness. This is why you can boldly declare, “I’ll never be sick in my life! I’ll never be broke in my life!” These are not empty words; they’re the realities of your new nature in Christ.

The Bible declares, “They which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:17). You’re not trying to “make it”; you’ve already made it in Christ! The old nature is gone; the new you is full of divine life.

So, live with this consciousness: you’re not a victim— you’re a victor! You’re not the defeated trying to win; you’re the one who already reigns in life through Christ Jesus. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Act

message:
The resurrection of Jesus is the foundation of our salvation. Without it, our faith would be in vain. But the Ascension—oh, the Ascension—reveals something even more glorious. It is the seal of His supreme authority, dominion, and eternal reign! He didn’t just come back from the dead; He ascended bodily into heaven, proving that He is greater than death, hell, and all creation.

Remember His words in John 6, when many were offended by His teaching. He asked them, “What and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before?” (John 6:62). And right before their eyes, those words became reality. It was too much for human language to capture!

Sadly, the Church has often overlooked the Ascension. Yet, it is the greatest event to have ever occurred on Earth. Elijah went up in a whirlwind with chariots of fire, but Jesus ascended physically.

This Easter, as we celebrate His resurrection, let us not forget the triumph of His ascension. He is not only risen; He is glorified! He reigns over all powers and principalities, and we’re seated with Him in heavenly places. Blessed be God!

message:
The Lord Jesus Christ is Himself the true God and eternal life. This is exactly who the Messiah was meant to be. For generations, the prophets proclaimed His coming. And when Jesus came, declaring Himself to be the Christ—God manifested in human form—many rejected Him, accusing Him of blasphemy. But He was right!

Titus 2:13-14 NKJV reveals Him as “our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave Himself for us, that He might redeem us from every lawless deed and purify for Himself His own special people, zealous for good works.” No other religious leader in history matches these credentials. They all lived, died, and remained in the grave. But Jesus Christ rose again! He ascended into heaven alive, and today He reigns forever.

Only His Name carries divine authority and power. In His Name, devils are cast out, the sick are healed, the blind see, the lame walk, and even the dead are raised. Through Him alone comes the remission of sins. Acts 13:38-39 NKJV declares, “through this Man is preached to you the forgiveness of sins; and by Him everyone who believes is justified from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

The testimony of Scripture is clear: eternal life is found only in Him. 1 John 5:11-12 NKJV says, “And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life.”

This is the Gospel: He gave His divine life so that you might have eternal life. And now that you’ve received Him, you’re no longer an ordinary human being. The God-life has supplanted the natural life within you. John 1:12-13 NKJV says, “But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.”

message:
In nature, some events are so rare that when they occur, they change the way we see the world forever. Think of an eclipse that suddenly turns day into night—so striking, beyond human power, that it forces everyone to pause in awe. Now imagine a moment when creation itself bowed to acknowledge the greatest sacrifice in history: the death of Jesus Christ.

The death of Jesus was no ordinary death. Falsely accused and nailed to the Cross, He was mocked by leaders, soldiers, and even the thieves crucified beside Him (Matthew 27:42–44). Yet, something supernatural unfolded. From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole earth. This was no eclipse—it was heaven’s declaration that the weight of the world’s sin was being placed upon Jesus.

At that moment, Jesus cried, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matthew 27:46 NKJV). He wasn’t afraid of physical death but of separation from the Father. The Holy One turned away as Jesus became sin for us (2 Corinthians 5:21). That was the true agony of the Cross—He bore the separation so we would never be separated from God again. With a loud voice He declared,“Father, “into Your hands I commit My spirit” (Luke 23:46 NKJV). He consciously

1212 gave up His life, fulfilling His own words: “I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again” (John 10:18 NKJV).

When Jesus yielded up the ghost, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, signifying the removal of the barrier between God and humanity, granting us access to the Father’s presence. Even the centurion overseeing the crucifixion, upon witnessing how Jesus died, declared, “... Truly this man was the Son of God” (Mark 15:39 NKJV). The manner of His death testified of His divinity. Jesus’ death was no ordinary death. It was the ultimate sacrifice that brought salvation to all mankind.

message:
When you look at the world today, it’s easy to think that those in government or positions of influence have ultimate control. They make laws, set systems, and dictate policies that shape nations. But, the Word of God lets us know that true authority is not in the hands of men, no matter how powerful they appear. All authority belongs to the Lord, and it’s enforced by Him through His Church!

In Daniel 4, King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream that revealed this eternal truth. He saw a great tree, majestic and flourishing but soon cut down at the command of an angelic being. The interpretation was clear: Nebuchadnezzar would be humbled until he acknowledged that “the heavens do rule” (Daniel 4:26). Indeed, pride blinded him, and he was stripped of all his glory until he confessed God’s sovereignty.

The Scripture goes further to explain that this decree was made by the watchers—heavenly beings assigned to ensure that God’s purposes are carried out on earth (Daniel 4:17). This has not changed. Those who falsely claim absolute authority over others, operating under the delusion that their influence gives them control over the nations, don’t realize that true authority lies with God and His heavenly Kingdom. The Most High rules in the affairs of men, and today, He carries out His will through His Church.

Indeed, pride blinded him, and he was stripped of all his glory until he confessed God’s sovereignty.

message:
Walking into a grand library filled with treasures of wisdom, yet spending all your time rearranging the chairs or dusting the tables, is a perfect picture of how many live today—busy, occupied, and exhausted, yet missing the true treasure. Life is not about how many activities fill your days but whether those activities are guided by God’s wisdom.

True success with the Lord is not measured by busyness or accomplishments but by the wisdom of God directing your path. And God’s Word is His wisdom. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom...” (Colossians 3:16 NKJV). This means giving priority to the Word, letting it dominate your thinking, guide your decisions, and shape your character.

Consider Martha and Mary when Jesus visited their home (Luke 10:38–42). Martha, though diligent and hardworking, was distracted by many tasks. Mary, on the other hand, chose the one thing that mattered most— sitting at the Master’s feet, hearing His Word. The Lord Jesus said Mary had chosen the good part that would never be taken from her. What a lesson! Martha’s service wasn’t wrong, but her priorities were misplaced.

Many young people today fall into the same trap— majoring on the minor, investing their time and strength in pursuits that don’t count for eternity. But the Lord calls us higher. His desire is that you focus on the Word, on fellowship with the Spirit, and on what truly matters.

Make God’s Word your greatest treasure. Train yourself to prize it above all else. As you study, meditate, and let it richly dwell in you, you’ll find yourself walking in wisdom that brings peace, direction, and divine success. You’ll move from glory to glory, victory to victory, and your life will be a testimony of the Lord’s excellence.

message:
A student preparing for final exams may dream of graduating with top honours. That’s vision. But unless they create a strategy—like setting a study timetable, joining group discussions, and practising past questions— the vision will never materialize. Vision inspires, but strategy executes. It’s important to understand the necessity of having a strategy. Many of God’s children, though able to visualize, lack the vital element of strategy.

Joshua 6 provides a remarkable example of how vision and strategy work together to produce divine results. God said to Joshua, “See, I have given into thine hand Jericho.” The battle had not yet begun, but God declared the victory. Joshua had to see it first—this is the power of vision, seeing what God has already given you and acting accordingly. However, vision alone is not enough. God gave Joshua the vision, but Joshua needed a strategy to take the city. The divine strategy was for him and the children of Israel to march around Jericho for seven days. Joshua had to follow the strategy to bring the vision to pass. In the same way, when God gives you a vision, He also gives you the strategy to accomplish it. Be sure to employ that strategy.

Life is a construction, not an accident. If life were an accident, it would be chaotic. Many people live in chaos because they have not structured their lives with purpose and vision. They drift from one event to another, relying on luck or chance. But a successful life or any successful endeavour is built on a solid foundation through vision, strategy, principles and means. It makes no difference what your endeavour is; function from where God has positioned you, and use the tools He has given you—vision, strategy, and faith—to build something extraordinary.

message:
Your labour in the Lord is not in vain; it is purposeful and eternal. God never promised that everything would be smooth or without challenges. He told us there would be difficulties, trials and adversaries. But in the midst of them all, He assured us of His presence and victory. Recall what we read in our opening scripture: He didn’t say there would be no tempest or fire. The promise is not the absence of challenges but the assurance of His presence and protection for you in the midst of adversities. It helps you understand the reason He says, “Count it all joy when you go through diverse tests” (James 1:2).

The Bible tells us in Daniel 3 about Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, three young men who stood firm in their faith despite fierce opposition. Their story is often remembered for the fiery furnace and their miraculous deliverance, but there’s more to it. Before they were thrown into the flames, they faced condemnation, rejection and false accusations. They endured hatred and opposition simply because they refused to compromise their faith. 2 Corinthians 4:17 says, “For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.” So, there are things you’ll have to face, go through, stand against and confront for you to live the godly life that the Lord has given you.

He assures us in Matthew 28:20 (NIV), “...And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.” Set your eyes on the future and on His glory. Refuse to be distracted by the temporary challenges. Be confident that no matter what, His Word will prevail in your life, and His glory will always be revealed in and through you.

extras.label: Speak

I’m triumphant over every adversity because I function in the authority and dominion of Christ, in whom I live and move and have my being. Amen.

message:
Think of electricity in a house. The wires are already carrying power, but if you don’t flip the switch, the light won’t come on. The power is present, but it needs to be activated. In the same way, the Holy Spirit in you brings the power of God into your life, but the power only works when you acknowledge and declare it. You have eternal life in you, and that life gives you power over sickness, disease and infirmities. You have power to cast out devils, heal sicknesses and cure diseases. You’ve been empowered to live in victory and unending prosperity.

This power in you is activated by acknowledgement and declaration. If you don’t acknowledge it, it can’t work. Sometimes, in a bid to sound humble, some people deny what they have. If, maybe, you said to them, “Oh, you really have power,” their typical response would be, “I don’t have any power; only Jesus has power.” But they’re wrong. The same Jesus said in Luke 10:19, “Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.”

Don’t deny what He gave you simply because you think you’re being humble. Acknowledge and affirm that Jesus gave you power to do the impossible—power over all things. Think about it: He gave us the Holy Spirit to live in us. What do you think He’s doing inside you? Who is the Holy Spirit? The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Trinity, who brings the power of God into your life. message:
The story of Cornelius in Acts 10 beautifully illustrates this truth. Cornelius was a Roman centurion, a Gentile and not part of the Jewish community. Yet, he was a devout man who feared God and was known for his generosity. He gave alms to the people and prayed continually. His giving and prayers did not go unnoticed; they ascended as a memorial before God. As a result of his generosity, God sent an angel to Cornelius with a divine instruction to send for Peter who would bring him the message of salvation. Think about it; an angel appeared to Cornelius because of his giving! God orchestrated an entire salvation plan for Cornelius, his family, and his household because of his generosity. As Peter preached about Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit fell upon everyone present. They began speaking in tongues and praising God. This moment was a pivotal point in the Early Church, highlighting the universal vision of the Gospel. God despises stinginess; it is contrary to His nature and reflects the nature of the devil.

So when God sees a giver, He sees something of Himself in that person and He’s drawn to that one in love. 2 Corinthians 9:7 AMPC says, “...God loves (He takes pleasure in, prizes above other things, and is unwilling to abandon or to do without) a cheerful (joyous, “prompt to do it”) giver [whose heart is in his giving].” Let this be your description and your experience of God’s love will be overwhelming.

## Speak

I’m a cheerful giver, and through my giving, I position myself in alignment with God’s divine purpose, experiencing His abundant grace. I function in supernatural blessings, favours and increase. Thank you Lord for making me a channel of blessings to my world, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
An artist’s signature on a masterpiece declares, “This is mine, authentic, and complete.” Likewise, when you received Christ, God placed His divine signature upon you—the seal of the Holy Spirit. What a reality! You’re God’s treasured possession, distinguished and set apart for glory.

The Scriptures declare, “…in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise” (Ephesians 1:13 NKJV). This seal isn’t merely a token of identity; it’s heaven’s declaration of ownership, protection, and inheritance. In ancient times, kings sealed decrees to confirm their authenticity and authority. God has done the same with you—placing His Spirit in you as proof that you’re fully His and backed by all of heaven’s resources.

When you received the Holy Spirit, you received the “earnest of our inheritance”—the guarantee of everything that belongs to Christ (Ephesians 1:14). Since God gave you His Spirit, He already gave you His best. There’s nothing greater He could withhold from you. Refuse to walk through life seeking acceptance or trying to qualify for blessings— you’re already accepted in the beloved, already qualified, already sealed!

The Holy Spirit in you is your access to divine wisdom, power, and fellowship with the Father. He’s your Helper, Teacher, Advocate, Strengthener, Intercessor, Standby, and Guide. Recognize His presence in your daily life. Talk with Him, listen to Him, and yield to His promptings. This seal also signifies divine protection. You’re untouchable, preserved, and empowered. Nothing in this world can override God’s mark upon your life. Walk boldly, knowing you’re distinguished for glory and excellence.

title: You Ought to Grow
excerpt: When a child is born, everything is done for them— feeding, carrying, cleaning, and protecting. The parents don’t expect the infant to walk or reason as an adult.
scripture: “But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.”
subtitle: (It’s God’s Desire That You Grow Up From Spiritual Infancy)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for your Word, which is my life and the light by which I see. I’m yielded to its power to transform and build me up in every area, delivering to me my inheritance in Christ. Your glory is revealed in my life, constantly transfiguring and renewing me more and more in knowledge into your image, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Become intentional about your growth. Get on the Pastor Chris Digital Library App, and put yourself on a routine of messages daily.

message:
When a child is born, everything is done for them— feeding, carrying, cleaning, and protecting. The parents don’t expect the infant to walk or reason as an adult. But as the child grows, responsibilities are gradually introduced. Imagine if a 15-year-old still expects to be spoon-fed like a toddler—it would be a tragedy! Growth demands change, and responsibility comes with maturity.

In the same way, when you first received Christ, your prayers were often answered quickly—even when they weren’t prayed correctly. That was God’s way of accommodating your spiritual infancy. Just as parents indulge little children while they’re learning, God gave you room to grow.

But as the Bible says, “For everyone who continues to feed on milk is obviously inexperienced and unskilled in the doctrine of righteousness (of conformity to the divine will in purpose, thought, and action), for he is a mere infant [not able to talk yet]!” (Hebrews 5:13 AMPC). The Lord expects you to move beyond milk to strong meat. This means your words, your thoughts, and even the way you pray now carry weight. You’re no longer to pray randomly or emotionally, but with accuracy and understanding.

For example, we don’t pray to Jesus in the Name of Jesus. Scripture teaches us to pray to the Father in the Name of Jesus. When you were born again, you already came to Him; you’re no longer “coming to Him” with every prayer— you now live in Him! These distinctions may not matter to babes in Christ, but they’re of great spiritual significance for the mature.

The Bible further declares, “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil” (Hebrews 5:14 KJV). As you apply the Word rightly, you’ll rise above the cycle of ups and downs. Instead, your life will move consistently—from faith to faith, grace to grace, and glory to glory. Hallelujah!

These distinctions may not matter to babes in Christ, but they’re of great spiritual significance for the mature.

The Bible further declares, “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil” (Hebrews 5:14 KJV). As you apply the Word rightly, you’ll rise above the cycle of ups and downs. Instead, your life will move consistently—from faith to faith, grace to grace, and glory to glory. Hallelujah!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for your Word, which is my life and the light by which I see. I’m yielded to its power to transform and build me up in every area, delivering to me my inheritance in Christ. Your glory is revealed in my life, constantly transfiguring and renewing me more and more in knowledge into your image, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
In these last days, many of God’s children have become more acquainted with spiritual gifts than ever before. Yet, one area often misunderstood is the gift of knowledge mentioned in 1 Corinthians 12. Contrary to popular thought, this is not about telling secrets of people’s lives—that’s prophecy. The Bible says, “...the secrets of his heart are revealed...” (1 Corinthians 14:25 NKJV) through prophecy.

The gift of knowledge, however, is far more expansive. The word “knowledge” here comes from the Greek “gnosis”, meaning scientific or intellectual knowledge. This gift allows the Spirit of God to supernaturally impart understanding about divine things, the cosmos, and even practical fields such as medicine, law, engineering, or artificial intelligence. How powerful this is!

Think about it: the One who created the heavens and the earth, the plants, animals, and minerals, can teach you about them supernaturally. He can reveal solutions the world is desperately searching for through you. That’s why you must become more conscious of His ministry in your life.

Christ, the embodiment of wisdom and knowledge, lives in you. The Holy Spirit, the Spirit of knowledge Himself, dwells in you. He’s able to transmit divine insight to your spirit, enabling you to walk in higher dimensions of creativity and excellence. Be mindful of His power and presence. As you yield yourself to Him, you’ll not only receive answers but also become the answer the world is waiting for.

message:
A fascinating truth about the eagle is that it never flaps its wings endlessly in flight. Instead, it soars, riding on the currents of the wind. Its strength is not in constant striving but in aligning with the unseen forces that carry it higher. That’s how God designed us to live—not by mere struggle on the outside, but by drawing strength from within, where His Spirit dwells.

Ecclesiastes 3:11 NKJV tells us something remarkable: “He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also, He has put eternity in their hearts...” What a glorious thought! The world is in your heart. Eternity is in your heart. Imagine that! No wonder Jesus said, “A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good things…” (Matthew 12:35 NKJV).

You carry divine treasures within you. Not only are the world and eternity in your heart, but the very Spirit of God resides there (1 Corinthians 3:16). That’s why the Christian life is lived from the inside out. Paul, writing by the Spirit, tells us, “…though our outward man is perishing, yet the inward man is being renewed day by day” (2 Corinthians 4:16 NKJV).

The forces that determine your success, health, and victory are not external—they’re in your inward man. Proverbs 4:23 exhorts us to guard our hearts diligently, for out of them flow the issues of life. When your spirit is trained to listen to God, you’ll always know what to do, where to go, and how to respond. Living from your spirit means speaking from your spirit. Declare the Word boldly, pray in tongues, and meditate on the Scriptures. Learn to pause and check within before making decisions. As you do, you’ll discover that your life aligns perfectly with God’s will.

Today, refuse to be driven by circumstances or emotions. Instead, be led by the Spirit within you. That’s the secret to consistent victory.

excerpt: In ancient cities, a watchman on the wall was vital. His duty was to stay alert, to guard, and to warn. If he forgot his role, the entire city was at risk.
scripture: “Beware that you do not forget the Lord your God by not keeping His commandments, His judgments, and His statutes which I command you today.”
subtitle: (You’re First And Foremost A Christian)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: What a joy to preach the glorious Gospel! message:
In ancient cities, a watchman on the wall was vital. His duty was to stay alert, to guard, and to warn. If he forgot his role, the entire city was at risk. Likewise, when we forget our spiritual priorities, we leave room for distractions and worldly influences to creep in.

The early Church spread with astonishing speed; in just three centuries, Christianity had permeated the known world. By 324 AD, persecution was abolished under Emperor Constantine, and within a few short years, Christianity became the official religion of the empire. Yet, in the midst of that success, urgency waned. The Church thought, “Everyone’s religious now; everything is fine.” But Jesus didn’t come to start a religion; He came to save men’s souls.

The children of Israel made the same mistake. God gave them rest and peace in the land He promised (Joshua 21:43-45). Yet, He warned them not to mingle with other nations or serve their gods (Joshua 23:7-8). Sadly, over time, they forgot and turned to idols. For young people today, the “distractions” may not be pagan idols but things like endless scrolling on social media, chasing popularity, gaming marathons, or relationships that weaken your fire for God. Before long, fellowship fades, church attendance drops, and soul winning gets pushed aside.

But hear this: you’re first and foremost a Christian! Your identity in Christ must be evident in all you do. Don’t let social media or the glitter of trends pull you away from your devotion to the Lord. Keep your fellowship strong, your priorities right, and your passion for soul winning alive. Let nothing distract you. Keep your eyes on the Master’s call, for that’s where true fulfilment lies.

message:
Asculptor once looked at a rough block of marble and declared, “I see an angel inside, and I must set it free.” With each deliberate strike of his chisel, the hidden beauty emerged. The words you speak are just like that sculptor’s tools—they shape reality, unlocking the treasures of God already present in your life.

Isn’t it amazing that the Lord Jesus said in John 20:21 NKJV, “…Peace to you! As the Father has sent Me, I also send you.” What a profound truth! He has commissioned you with the same authority with which the Father sent Him. The Father gave Jesus the Spirit without measure, and that same Spirit now dwells in you. That means heaven honours your words spoken in faith!

When you boldly affirm God’s Word, something extraordinary happens—heaven responds, angels act, and tangible results follow. Speaking God’s Word is not mere recitation; it’s declaring divine realities with the authority of the Spirit. Remember Genesis 1:3:“God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.” The Holy Spirit—the power of the Godhead—moved on those words and made them reality.

That same Spirit lives in you! The Lord Jesus said,“…the Father who dwells in Me does the works” (John 14:10 NKJV). Today, that Father—the Holy Spirit—dwells in you. When you speak healing, peace, or provision, the Spirit incubates on your words and brings them to pass.

So don’t speak fear, doubt, or the language of the world. Fill your heart with the Word of Christ richly (Colossians 3:16). Let your mouth become an instrument of creative power, shaping life and destiny with words of faith. Speak boldly today, for your words carry the very breadth of God!

message:
A fragrance has the power to change the atmosphere of a room. A single drop of perfume can alter the environment, leaving a lingering presence that can’t be ignored. That’s how your life is—you carry with you something far greater than a fragrance: the very essence of God’s blessing.

Galatians 3:29 NKJV declares, “And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” This isn’t just a scripture to admire; it’s your divine identity. The blessing of God is not simply what you have— it’s who you are. God didn’t only say to Abraham, “I will bless you”; He also declared, “You shall be a blessing.” That means Abraham became the embodiment of the blessing, and in Christ, you have inherited that same blessing.

You’re not chasing blessings; you’re the carrier of the blessing, and this blessing is not limited to material possessions. It’s a spiritual force that empowers everything you touch to prosper. It makes you fruitful, productive, and influential. Like Joseph, who prospered even in slavery and prison because the blessing was upon him (Genesis 39:2), you too are unstoppable. The blessing doesn’t recognise limitations—it manifests results regardless of circumstances.

You’re the seed of Abraham, called to be a blessing to your world. You’re not ordinary. The forces of heaven are at work in and through you. Be conscious of this truth. Declare it daily; walk in it. Let it reflect in your words, actions and expectations. You’re the expression of the blessing!

Your Spirit is at work in me, causing me not only to desire your divine will but also to carry it out. My life is a testimony of your grace, love and mercy, and I increase in knowledge and abound in wisdom as I fulfil your purpose for my life, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
In the heart of every gardener lies a simple joy: seeing a tiny seed blossom into a flourishing plant. The seed may appear small, insignificant even, but within it lies the potential for beauty, nourishment, and multiplication. In much the same way, God designed your life not to be barren or ordinary but to be consistently fruitful and productive.

As the seed of Abraham and a child of God, you’re divinely empowered to produce results. You weren’t created to merely pass through life unnoticed; you were chosen to make impact and to bear fruits that remain. Jesus declared in John 15:16 NKJV, “You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain….” Fruitfulness isn’t seasonal for the Christian—it’s your nature.

Whether in soul winning, your career, your relationships, or your service in God’s house, Christ in you guarantees success. Even when others fail, you succeed. message:
Some years ago, engineers tested a bridge built to withstand earthquakes. They shook it, strained it, and even tried to break it with simulated tremors. Yet, each time, it stood firm because it wasn’t designed to collapse—it was built to endure. That bridge reminds me of the Church of Jesus Christ. The storms of life may rage, opposition may rise, but the Church cannot be destroyed. Why? Because it is built by the Master Builder Himself—our Lord Jesus Christ.

He boldly declared, “…I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matthew 16:18 KJV). What He builds is eternal, powerful and glorious. And the beautiful thing is this—you’re not a spectator in this divine edifice. The Bible calls you “a living stone” (1 Peter 2:5), carefully chosen, shaped, and placed by God to reflect His glory. You’re not an accident. You’re part of something that cannot fail.

The Church doesn’t function by worldly systems; we operate by heavenly principles. We’re powered by the Holy Spirit and governed by the Word. That’s why adversity, persecution, or opposition only make us stronger. James said, “Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds” (James 1:2 NIV). Paul affirms in Romans 8:37 NKJV, “Yet in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.” There’s no amount of tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, peril or suffering that can prevail against us.

We are the undefeatable Church! Satan is under our feet. We reign in dominion, joint heirs with Christ, associates of the God-kind, and vessels of eternal excellence. The glory of God shines in and through us. So, rejoice today! You belong to a Kingdom and a Church that is unstoppable, unshakeable, and built to last—forever revealing the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

message:
Aworld-renowned artist once said, “The greatest tragedy is not in failing to paint a masterpiece, but in never discovering the canvas you were created to paint on.” How true this is of life! Many people drift through existence, chasing shadows and pursuing ambitions that were never theirs in the first place. Yet, as God’s child, you’re not called to guess your way through life. You were created to live in the very centre of God’s purpose—flourishing in His divine plan for you.

The Scriptures reveal that you were predestined to a glorious life in Christ: “For whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son” (Romans 8:29 NKJV). God designed you for alignment with His will, to express His glory, and to manifest His excellence in everything you do.

Ephesians 2:10 (AMPC) makes it clearer: “For we are God’s [own] handiwork (His workmanship), recreated in Christ Jesus…that we may do those good works which God predestined (planned beforehand) for us.” Isn’t that beautiful? There’s a life already mapped out for you—a life of victory, prosperity, health, righteousness, and impact. This is the “good life” that Christ purchased for you.

Like Epaphras, who laboured in prayer for the Colossians, the Spirit of God continually draws you to not only know but also to stand perfect and complete in the will of God. How? By meditating on the Word and fellowshipping with the Holy Spirit. As you do, your spirit is synchronised with God’s thoughts. Through the Word of God and the ministry of the Holy Spirit, you’re trained to know and walk in God’s divine provisions; your discernment sharpens, and your decisions reflect heaven’s interests and intent.

Even now, declare that you’re perfect and complete in all the will of God. This is your testimony! You’re not ordinary; you’re God’s workmanship, fashioned for excellence, designed to reign, and ordained to walk in the very paths He has prepared.

scripture: “And whatever you ask in My name, that I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.”
subtitle: (Use The Name Of Jesus To Reign Over Circumstances)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for giving me the power of attorney to use the Name of Jesus; I live and function in the authority of His Name which works and produces results for me everywhere. extras.label: Act

message:
I once witnessed a police officer who walked into a tense situation with nothing but his uniform and badge. Instantly, people calmed down. Why? It wasn’t about his size, his tone, or even his words. It was the authority behind that badge. Everyone recognised it. That’s exactly what the Name of Jesus is to you—it’s more than a word or phrase; it’s your badge of authority in this world and beyond.

The Name of Jesus represents everything He is and everything He accomplished through His death, burial, and resurrection. When you declare that Name, it’s as though Jesus Himself is speaking. Philippians 2:9-11 NKJV tells us, “…God also has highly exalted Him and given Him the name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.” Hallelujah!

This isn’t just a beautiful scripture; it’s our reality. The Lord Jesus gave us the legal right to use His Name. He said in Mark 16:17-18 NKJV, “And these signs will follow those who believe: In My name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues; they will take up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it will by no means hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.” The power is not in how loud you speak, but in the authority of the Name.

Peter understood this when he said to the lame man at the Gate called Beautiful, “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6 NKJV). Immediately, strength came to the man’s feet and anklebones, and he was healed instantly.

That’s the power of the Name in action. Use the Name of Jesus. Use it to reign over circumstances, keep yourself in divine health, and maintain the triumphant life God has given you. Colossians 3:17 NKJV says: “And whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus….”

message:
Notice how a child naturally imitates the language of their parents. They pick up the accent, the tone, and even the expressions without trying. Why? Because it’s their nature to echo what they hear at home. In the same way, when you received the life of God at the new birth, you received His righteousness—and with it, His vocabulary. Now, you don’t talk like the world. You speak the language of your Father: the language of victory, dominion, and faith!

The Bible says, “The righteousness which is of faith speaketh…” (Romans 10:6). Righteousness has a voice, and it declares what God has said. When you affirm, “I am the righteousness of God in Christ Jesus” (2 Corinthians 5:21), it’s not a mere positive confession. It’s truth released into your world! You’re saying what God has said. Hebrews 13:5- 6 NKJV declares, “…For He Himself has said… So we may boldly say….”

Your inheritance in Christ is activated by words. The Lord Jesus Himself said you shall have whatsoever you say (Mark 11:23). You can’t reign in life unless you talk as the royalty that you are. Your righteousness empowers your speech to produce divine results. Refuse to speak defeat, lack, or fear. Instead, let your words align with God’s Word: “I walk in divine health. I’m marvellously helped of the Lord. My life is upward and forward only!”

The righteousness of faith calls things that are not as though they were; it speaks reality, and the Word of God is the reality. When you speak the Word of God in faith, you align your life with heaven’s will. You silence doubt and confusion. You activate angels. You chart a course of divine success. So, speak boldly. Declare your health, peace, prosperity and victory. Express your righteousness through your words.

Your mouth is the tool for shaping circumstances and enforcing kingdom realities.

Faith doesn’t wait for visible results before speaking. Abraham was called “the father of many nations” even before Isaac was born. He declared what God said until it became his reality. Likewise, don’t wait for things to change before speaking differently. Don’t wait to feel blessed— declare, “I am blessed!” For the Word affirms, “He has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ” (Ephesians 1:3 NIV).

Keep declaring your health, your progress, your peace. Speak to your body, your finances, and every situation around you. The more you affirm the Word, the more heaven’s realities are established in your life. Remember, even salvation is activated by words (Romans 10:9–10).

Every time you speak in line with the Word, you give

1212 divine substance to the unseen. Refuse to stay silent. Keep prophesying your destiny: “My life is upward and forward! I am excellent and full of glory!” If you’ve been in and out of sicknesses, declare divine health and stick to the Word. Soon enough, your entire being will conform to your faith-filled declarations, keeping your body in health always.

Through the Holy Spirit, we know the things freely given to us by God, and we speak them forth (1 Corinthians 2:12– 13). Keep talking! Keep declaring your victory. Hallelujah!

## Speak

I declare that my words are full of power and life. I speak health, progress, peace, and prosperity into my world. My life is upward and forward only! I am excellent, radiant, and full of glory. I refuse to stay silent—I prophesy my destiny daily, and everything around me aligns with the Word of God. Through the Holy Spirit, I know the things freely given to me, and as I declare them, they’re established in my life. Hallelujah!

message:
A small flame in the middle of a vast, dark auditorium may seem insignificant at first glance. Yet, as your eyes adjust, you realise something profound: that one flame is enough to conquer the shadows. It changes the atmosphere, shifting the focus from darkness to light. Beloved, that is exactly how the Spirit of God describes you.

Jesus declared, “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden” (Matthew 5:14 NKJV). You’re not an accident in this world. You were born with divine intent—to radiate God’s glory, inspire hope, and manifest His goodness. Your presence in any environment should bring illumination, direction, and life.

Think of Jesus Himself. His public ministry was brief— just over three years—but the impact is eternal. What was His secret? Acts 10:38 NKJV reveals it: “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power….” That same anointing is upon you today through the indwelling Spirit. You’re not ordinary; you’re God’s answer to your generation.

The Apostle Paul reminds us, “For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind” (2 Timothy 1:7 NKJV). Fear, timidity, or failure cannot define you because the Spirit within you produces boldness, wisdom, and excellence. In fact, the Bible declares in 1 John 2:20 KJV, “But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things.” That means you have divine insight, supernatural ability, and the wisdom to influence your world.

Therefore, never see yourself as ordinary. Carry this consciousness everywhere: you’re anointed to make a difference! Like that candle in the auditorium, your light can’t be hidden. Shine in your family, your school, your community, and your nation. Let men see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

title: God’s Greatest Treasure
excerpt: The most important thing to God is human souls. It’s the reason Jesus came and gave His life.
scripture: “For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.”
subtitle: (Every Person Matters to God)
prayer: Dear Father, as your children around the world go forth preaching the Gospel today, men’s hearts are open to receive the message for their salvation; they’re delivered from Satan’s dominion into God’s Kingdom. I declare that in every nation in the earth, every resistance to the Gospel is broken, and the light of the glorious Gospel of Christ shines brightly into the hearts of men, women, boys and girls for a great harvest of souls into the Kingdom, in Jesus’ Name. extras.label: Act
extras.text: Make soul-winning your personal lifestyle. Share the word of God with at least one person this week.

message:
The most important thing to God is human souls. It’s the reason Jesus came and gave His life. The Bible says, “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life” (John 3:16). He didn’t come for the redemption of the mountains, hills and beautiful vegetation of the world. These creations, while majestic and valuable to God, were not the focus of His sacrificial mission.

He came to save human beings—men, women, boys and girls! His life, death, and resurrection were all centred on the salvation of mankind. This act of love underscores the immense value God places on each person. We must have that in our hearts and live always with the consciousness that every human being is important to God. If you live with this understanding, it’ll shape your interactions, decisions, and priorities.

It’ll drive you to live purposefully, knowing that according to the Scriptures, there’s a definite number of souls that must be won to the Lord before the Rapture of the Church. Therefore, evangelism becomes your heartbeat and lifestyle. Remain passionate and fervent in sharing the Gospel with others. Put your time, energy and resources into it. Recognize the intrinsic value of every soul and be determined to see them fulfil God’s destiny for them.

Pray earnestly for the salvation of souls around the world. Remember, the Bible says, “God is not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance” (2 Peter 3:9). So, in addition to fervently and radically preaching the Gospel, intercede for those who haven’t yet known the Lord that the light of the glorious Gospel of Christ will shine unto them for their salvation, prevailing over darkness, idolatry and deception. Hallelujah!

titleOriginal: REACHING THE WORLD WITH GOD’S WORD
excerpt: With so many English Bible versions available today, it’s easy for many to erroneously believe that the Bible was originally given in the English language.
scripture: “The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.”
subtitle: (The Mission of Evangelism Through Languages)
prayer: Dear Father, I pray for translators, missionaries, and evangelists of the message of the Gospel all over the world, that they continue to be effective witnesses for Christ, making your Word known without hindrance, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Remember you’re part of God’s mission to reach every nation. Pray for missionaries and Bible translators worldwide. Support Gospel projects that spread the Word.

message:
With so many English Bible versions available today, it’s easy for many to erroneously believe that the Bible was originally given in the English language. However, it was the translators who performed this crucial work, and the Holy Spirit continues to guide them even today to make the Bible and other Christian materials accessible to many more in their native languages.

Think about the fact that the sacred writings of the Scriptures were written in Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic. But it took dedicated individuals who loved the Lord and desired to spread His message to the entire world to make it available in various languages as we have today. This mission continues through the work of modern-day missionaries and evangelists who travel to distant lands, much like those early translators. They go into remote and often challenging environments to find those who have not yet heard the Gospel, and they bring it to them in the language they best understand.

The Lord Jesus instructed us to go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature (Mark 16:15). He sent us to find the lost, to seek them out in the byways and highways. This directive is clear in the Scriptures, and it drives the mission of Christians today. We carry on the vision that He gave us. This vision is about actively reaching out to those who need to hear the message of salvation, and this involves going beyond our comfort zones, reaching out to speakers of all languages, thus ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to hear and respond to the Gospel.

The work is far from over, and the vision of reaching every person with the Gospel remains as vital as ever. That’s why we’re grateful to the Lord to have those who are working with us in various nations to make it possible for this devotional to become accessible in all known languages and dialects of the world, and as a result, reaching the ends of the earth before the Lord’s return.

title: God’s Plan for Redemption
excerpt: When Adam was created, he existed in innocence, knowing only good because everything God created was good (Genesis 1:31).
scripture: “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”
subtitle: (Restoration Through Christ’s Obedience)
prayer: Dear Father, I’m eternally grateful for the redemption you’ve provided through the obedience of Jesus Christ. Thank you for what His vicarious sacrifice and His glorious resurrection have ushered us into. I’m the expression of your grace, love, and righteousness, living out the incorruptible, imperishable, impregnable life in Christ. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
When Adam was created, he existed in innocence, knowing only good because everything God created was good (Genesis 1:31). God entrusted Adam with authority over His creation, effectively making him the steward of this world. Along with this authority, God provided Adam with specific instructions: not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which was in the midst of the garden.

God clearly warned Adam of the consequences of eating of the tree: “…for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die" (Genesis 2:17). Adam, nonetheless, disobeyed God and ate of the forbidden tree. This act of disobedience constituted treason against God, and as a result, Adam forfeited his authority to Satan, who then became the god of this world. But God, in His infinite mercy and wisdom, had a plan for redemption.

He sent another Adam—the second and last Adam— Jesus Christ: “…The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit. The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven” (1 Corinthians 15:45 & 47). Recall what we read in our opening scripture: the Lord Jesus Christ, through His perfect obedience and sacrificial death on the cross, restored the broken relationship between God and humanity.

Jesus’ obedience countered Adam’s disobedience, offering justification and eternal life to all who believe in Him. Therefore, through Jesus Christ, God’s plan for redemption and righteousness was fulfilled. No wonder He declared in John 14:6, “I am The Way, The Truth, and The Life: no man comes to the Father, but by me.” He is the eternal salvation. Hallelujah!

excerpt: Maya was thrilled when her classmates invited her to a party hosted by one of the most popular guys in school. Everyone wanted to be there—loud music, no supervision, and “fun” everywhere.
scripture: “Do not be envious of evil men, Nor desire to be with them.”
subtitle: (Choosing the Right Company)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I don’t envy Godless men or desire to be in their company. I walk as a child of light, for I am light in the Lord. My delight is in pleasing the Lord Jesus, and I seek to honour Him always. extras.label: Act
extras.text: Say NO to environments that compromise your values, even if they look attractive. Make it your daily goal to please Jesus above all else.

message:
Maya was thrilled when her classmates invited her to a party hosted by one of the most popular guys in school. Everyone wanted to be there—loud music, no supervision, and “fun” everywhere. At first, she thought, this is my chance to fit in, but then Psalm 1:1 came to mind: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly...” She realized the Holy Spirit was reminding her of who she truly was: light in a dark world.

Sometimes, you find Christians who envy godless individuals and wish to be in their company. Some get really excited to identify with some “big names.” If, for some reason, they get invited to be in the company of certain well-known people, they consider it a big deal. But that’s not how God sees it. He doesn’t want you to envy Godless men and women.

Remember what He said in Psalm 1:1, “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.” You’re blessed for not hanging out with the wicked who despise the way of the Lord and the life of the Kingdom. Don’t envy or seek to please them. Even if they’re rich and influential, don’t be enticed by their wealth. I came across our opening verse when I was still very young, and it gave me good instruction about human relationships: what’s good for me and what’s not good for me.

So, right from a very young age, I had never been inspired by people who weren’t living for Christ, irrespective of who they were or what they had. The only person you should want to please is the Lord Jesus. That’s important because those who truly love Jesus Christ will be pleased with the things you do. But if those who don’t love Jesus are pleased with the things you do, then there’s a problem, and you should be concerned. In Galatians 1:10 CEV, Paul said, “I am not trying to please people. I want to please God. Do you think I am trying to please people? If I were doing that, I would not be a servant of Christ.”

The only person you should want to please is the Lord Jesus. That’s important because those who truly love Jesus Christ will be pleased with the things you do. But if those who don’t love Jesus are pleased with the things you do, then there’s a problem, and you should be concerned. In Galatians 1:10 CEV, Paul said, “I am not trying to please people. I want to please God. Do you think I am trying to please people? If I were doing that, I would not be a servant of Christ.”

## Speak

I don’t envy Godless men or desire to be in their company. I walk as a child of light, for I am light in the Lord. My delight is in pleasing the Lord Jesus, and I seek to honour Him always. I’m guided by the Spirit of God who lives in me and guides me in the path of righteousness, to produce fruits and works of righteousness, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Say NO to environments that compromise your values, even if they look attractive. Make it your daily goal to please Jesus above all else.

subtitle: (The Holy Spirit Your Inner Counsellor)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for the Holy Spirit, my divine Counsellor, who lives in me, granting me insight into mysteries and secrets, and sufficient information to make wise and informed decisions and choices. message:
The term “multitude of counsellors” is an interesting one that’s misunderstood by many to mean a multiplicity of counsellors. Even some Bible versions translate it this way. The NIV version, for instance, says, “For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.” It’s actually not about a multiplicity of counsellors; the Hebrew word translated “multitude” also means “greatness”, while the word translated counsellors is translated ‘counsel’ many more times in the ‘Authorized version.’ Counsellors provide information. A “multitude of counsellors” therefore, means that you’re getting sufficient or accurate information to help you decide an appropriate course of action.

Back in those days when this verse was written, they didn’t have access to as much information as we have today. They had what they called the “king’s advisors.” He depended on them for wise counsel. They were the “wise” men: the king’s counsellors, such as Ahitophel in the days of King David; his counsel was said to be as though one had heard from God (2 Samuel 16:23).

But today, we have lots of materials that we can study to get sufficient information on a subject that can help us make an informed decision. So, it’s about the quality of information, not about the number of people you’re calling to counsel you.

However, you have the most dependable Counsellor who can give you the most accurate information you require, and that’s the Holy Spirit. The Psalmist said,“I will bless the LORD, who hath given me counsel: my reins also instruct me in the night seasons” (Psalm 16:7). The Holy Spirit is the one who instructs you in your inward man. He gives you instructions by which He guides your life. Some of these may not even be expressly dealt with in the Scriptures.

For example, you could require information concerning travelling or making some purchases. The Counsellor in you— the Holy Spirit—can provide you with the necessary information to enable you make the right decision

excerpt: Aiden panicked when his science fair presentation didn't go as planned, and that stress followed him home. He felt sick for weeks.
scripture: “Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.”
subtitle: (How the Holy Spirit Helps)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the ministry of the Holy Spirit in my life. I’m always attentive to His guidance, as He leads me in victory in every aspect of my life: in my finances, health, job, family, relationships, and ministry. message:
Aiden panicked when his science fair presentation didn't go as planned, and that stress followed him home. He felt sick for weeks. Medicine didn’t do a thing—the headache lingered like a dark cloud. One night, he asked the Holy Spirit for help. Every day after that, he received clarity on the specific steps he needed to take to be healed, and as he acted on them, he got his healing. Oftentimes, when people get sick, many aren’t aware of the reason for their trouble. They try all kinds of drugs, some of which even cause more problems than they realize. When nothing changes, they begin to wonder, “Why am I going through these difficulties? Why am I feeling so sick? Why is this happening to me?”

Well, the Holy Spirit was sent to guide you into all truth, including the truth about your health. He can help you know the problem and also the solution. Did you know the Holy Spirit is a healer? Yes, He is. The Bible says, “if He lives in you, He will vitalize your physical body.” It doesn’t matter that you’ve been diagnosed with some disease; now that He lives in you, there’s the guarantee for a change. Glory to God!

Maybe you’re a student or you’re carrying out research for a project; the Holy Spirit is the Teacher inside you. You need to listen to Him because He knows everything. He’s the Spirit of wisdom, knowledge and understanding. He can fill you with the knowledge of God’s will, with all wisdom and spiritual understanding concerning anything. Just ask Him. The Holy Spirit has come to help you in all aspects of life, whether in business, in family, or in your finances.

He’s come to help you gain the mastery, to make you a wonder. Your greatest asset while you’re here in this world is the Holy Spirit. He’ll teach you the Word of God and remind you of things you’ve learned. You can speak with Him more than you do with anyone else. Thank Him for being your ever-present teacher, helper and guide.

title: Why You Believe
excerpt: The Lord Jesus made the statement above in one of the last meetings He had with His disciples before He was crucified.
scripture: “And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment.”
subtitle: (The Convincing Power of the Holy Spirit)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the ministry of the Holy Spirit around the world today. As your children proclaim the Gospel everywhere, our listeners are convinced and converted. There’s a great harvest of souls into the Kingdom today, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Trust Him when sharing the Gospel He makes your words effective.

message:
The Lord Jesus made the statement above in one of the last meetings He had with His disciples before He was crucified. During the long teaching, which started in the 13th chapter, He told them He was going away, and the disciples were puzzled. Then, He said, “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive...” (John 14:16-17).

In subsequent verses, He told them who the Comforter is: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost…”(John 14:26). This was the same person He was referring to in chapter 16 when He said, “And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment” (John 16:8). What did He mean by this statement? The word “reprove” is translated from the Greek word “elegcho”, which means “to convict” or “to convince.” This is the work of the Holy Spirit.

When Jesus preached, many didn’t believe. Even though certain individuals believed and received miracles, the people generally didn’t believe. The Bible says, “But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him” (John 12:37). They weren’t convicted. Why? Because the Holy Spirit hadn’t been poured out on the people. But Jesus said when the Holy Spirit comes, He will convict the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment.

Today, men can be convicted in their hearts— convinced—when they hear the Word of God because the Holy Spirit has been poured out. The reason you’re convinced that Jesus is the Son of God, even though you haven’t seen Him, is that the Holy Spirit brought that revelation to your Spirit. It wasn’t a man that convinced you; the Holy Spirit did that in your heart. You believe because He helped you to believe. That’s why when you go out to win souls, it’s important to do so by the power of the Holy Spirit. He’s the one who convicts the people; He convinces those listening to you and makes them believe. Glory to God

title: True Glory Is in Your Submission
titleOriginal: TRUE GLORY IS IN YOUR SUBMISSION
excerpt: Sometimes, when we tell people the Lord has glorified them, they expect to see something outwardly, like a ray of light glowing from their skin. But that’s not what the Bible teaches.
scripture: “But Jesus answered them, saying, “The hour has come that the Son of Man should be glorified.”
subtitle: (The More You Yield, the More You Shine)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for your glory in my life. Thank you for the privilege and blessing to experience ever-increasing glory as I do your Word and carry out every instruction of the Spirit that I receive, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Walk in the Spirit. Let His voice and leading guide your actions consistently.

message:
Sometimes, when we tell people the Lord has glorified them, they expect to see something outwardly, like a ray of light glowing from their skin. But that’s not what the Bible teaches. The glory of God isn’t necessarily felt or perceived by the senses. It’s something you recognize with your spirit. Look at Jesus. The Bible tells us in John 12 of some Greeks who sought an audience with Him. When He was told that they had come to see Him, He knew this was a sign: It was time for the salvation of the Gentiles.

This also signified that He was about to die. Jesus responded by saying, “...The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit” (John 12:23-24 KJV). When Jesus said, “The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified,” the Bible didn’t record that any spectacular event transpired. The heavens didn’t open up, and there was no earthquake. In the next chapter, while Jesus was sitting with His disciples at Passover, Judas got up after supper and went away hurriedly. Jesus then said, “... Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him” (John 13:31).

The Bible didn’t say lights started beaming everywhere because He was glorified. No. The glory was in His submission. Here’s what the Master did: He submitted Himself totally to the will of the Father and declared, “Now is the Son of man glorified.” The submission of one’s life to the Spirit is where the glory is. The more yielded you are to Him, the more your glory increases. The less yielded you are, the less of God’s glory is manifested in your life. So, what would you rather do? Be yielded to Him! Do the Word, walking in the Spirit, and you’ll experience greater manifestations of His glory in your life. Hallelujah!

## Prayer
