title: You Are the Light of the World
titleOriginal: YOU ARE THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD
excerpt: Jesus performed a miracle by turning clay into eyes, having said, “As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” Do you know what this means?
scripture: “As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
subtitle: (Bring Sight, Clarity, and Healing!)
prayer: Dear Father, you’ve made me a light in this world, equipped and empowered to bring hope, healing, and deliverance to those around me. Your light in me dispels darkness. Thank you for making me an oasis of love and a haven of peace, joy, hope and faith in a troubled world; what a privilege! Thank you, Father, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Boldly declare, “I am the light of the world!” Wherever you go today, let God’s light shine through you. Bring hope, direction, healing, and vision to someone who’s lost, broken, or blind to truth.

message:
Jesus performed a miracle by turning clay into eyes, having said, “As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” Do you know what this means? Every time Jesus used that expression “I AM”, He was reiterating what God said to Moses when he asked, “What is your name?” and God said, “I AM.” God was saying to Moses, “I am whatever you need me to be. If you need deliverance, I am your deliverance. If you need salvation, I am your salvation. If you need healing, I am your healing.

Whatever it is you need, I AM! So, when Jesus said, “I AM…,” He was saying the same thing God said: “I am what you need.” He saw a man who didn’t have eyes and said, “I am the light of the world.” After saying this, Jesus did something mind-blowing: He spat on the ground, made clay with the spittle, and rubbed it into the man’s eyes. Historians tell us the man wasn’t just blind; he had no eyeballs but empty sockets.

Remember what the Bible says, “The light of the body is the eye...” (Matthew 6:22, Luke 11:34). So, Jesus was saying, “I am the eyes of the world. Without me, the world can’t see.” Right away, He proved it and gave the man eyes. Now, here’s the most intriguing part: the same Jesus said, “Ye are the light of the world…” (Matthew 5:14). That means, just like Him, you give “eyes”—sight—to the world!

Without you, the world can’t see. You give direction, clarity, and vision to the world. Even now, boldly declare, “I am the light of the world!” It means that when you go out and meet someone who is down, you can lift such a person up. Someone can have his eyes restored just because you showed up; someone who was sick can get healed. Hallelujah!

title: The Fight of Faith
excerpt: As a Christian, you’re in a fight. Some people don’t like to hear this because they’re just not willing to fight. Instead, they hope that things will somehow just fall into place. No!
scripture: “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”
subtitle: (Engage in the Good Fight; Victory is Already Yours!)
prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for the victory you’ve given me in Jesus Christ. I stand firm in the authority you’ve given me, knowing that no weapon formed against me shall prosper. Thank you for the divine life in me, working in every fibre of my being. I’m victorious in every situation, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Refuse to walk by sight, renew your mind with God’s Word, and meditate on it consistently.

message:
As a Christian, you’re in a fight. Some people don’t like to hear this because they’re just not willing to fight. Instead, they hope that things will somehow just fall into place. No! You’ve got to fight. Why? Because there’s an adversary working to ensure that things don’t fall into place for you.

Understand that the world is hostile to your faith; it’s hostile to the Kingdom of God. Jesus, however, said, “but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world” (John 16:33 NKJV). So, we’re not trying to overcome the world; we already did in Christ Jesus and keep it in that position with our faith. The Bible says our faith is the victory that triumphs over the world: “For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith” (1 John 5:4 KJV).

Now you can understand why He tells us to fight the good fight of faith. Faith is the victory, so always see with the eyes of faith. See the end from the beginning and stay focused on the Word, knowing that no matter what happens, your victory is guaranteed. It’s called the good fight of faith because you always win.

Here are three important things to note as you fight the good fight of faith: refuse to consider sensory perceptions and focus on the Word. Secondly, keep renewing your mind with the Word, and let it be your motivation (Romans 12:2; James 1:25). Then, meditate on the Word to deepen its impact in your life (Joshua 1:8). Hallelujah!

Now you can understand why He tells us to fight the good fight of faith. Faith is the victory, so always see with the eyes of faith. See the end from the beginning and stay focused on the Word, knowing that no matter what happens, your victory is guaranteed. It’s called the good fight of faith because you always win.

Here are three important things to note as you fight the good fight of faith: refuse to consider sensory perceptions and focus on the Word. Secondly, keep renewing your mind with the Word, and let it be your motivation (Romans 12:2; James 1:25). Then, meditate on the Word to deepen its impact in your life (Joshua 1:8). Hallelujah!

## Prayer

Dear Father, I thank you for the victory you’ve given me in Jesus Christ. I stand firm in the authority you’ve given me, knowing that no weapon formed against me shall prosper. Thank you for the divine life in me, working in every fibre of my being. I’m victorious in every situation, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Refuse to walk by sight, renew your mind with God’s Word, and meditate on it consistently.

scripture: “A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.”
subtitle: (Speak The Word; Words Are Seeds!)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: When I speak, it comes to pass because my words are powerful; they produce what I say, because I speak from God and speak His Word. extras.label: Act

message:
Dami kept declaring, “I walk in divine health,” even though the doctor’s report said otherwise. Friends thought she was in denial, but Dami knew better. When you speak, things happen. Your words are powerful; they create or destroy. The Bible says death and life are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21 KJV). This is the reason we emphasize speaking right, affirming God’s Word on all occasions.

What you say is what you get. Ponder again what we read in our opening scripture: through the words you speak, you bring forth good or evil, life or death, sickness or health, poverty or wealth. It’s up to you. It’s about what you say. You may say, “I’ve been speaking, but nothing has been happening.” Who told you nothing has been happening? That’s like planting your seeds and digging them out of the ground before they grow. Seeds don’t germinate overnight, but once they’re planted in the right environment, they most certainly will grow.

Therefore, you have to keep speaking the Word. Like we often say, “Keep saying it; don’t stop talking it!” When you affirm the Word, it works. In Isaiah 55:10-11 KJV, the Lord said, “For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.”

This shows the power, immutability, impregnability and infallibility of the Word of God. Are you aware that your words hold the same power? Remember, you’re like Him; you’re created in His image and in His likeness. As He is, so are you in this world (1 John 4:17). The Word of God in your mouth is God talking. Quit thinking it’s not working. Don’t allow Satan to get you into the sense-realm of trying to observe lying vanities.

excerpt: As a child of God, your life is different; you’re not an ordinary person. You’re not subject to the limitations and corrupting influences of this world.
scripture: “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”
subtitle: (Stirring Your Spirit Strengthens Your Health Reality)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the reality of my divine nature in Christ. I refuse to accept the limitations, sicknesses, and conditions that the world prescribes. My body is full of life, health and strength. No infirmity can thrive in me because the Spirit of God quickens my body. I live victoriously, walking in divine health and supernatural vitality, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
As a child of God, your life is different; you’re not an ordinary person. You’re not subject to the limitations and corrupting influences of this world. Never accept the verdict from man’s limited knowledge stemming from the wisdom of this world with respect to your health. Your body is not subject to the elements of this world and the vagaries of nature. You’re in Christ and from Christ, where divinity rules.

Many today have been conditioned to expect certain ailments or health challenges when they get to a certain age in life. They’ve been told that between certain ages their bodies will begin to slow down, pains will set in, heart problems may arise. These conclusions have been drawn from mere human wisdom and experience, not divine truth. 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

This means no inherited sickness or weakness because you’re born of God, inundated with eternal life. Your identity is not in your earthly lineage. It doesn’t matter what ran in your biological family— heart problems, diabetes, high blood pressure, etc.—those things have no hold on you! You’re a new creation in Christ, born into a new family—the family of God. If sickness tries to attach itself to your body, you say, “In the Name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, I rebuke this sickness. I remove it from my body!”

Your words have power; use them to establish your divine health. Take charge of your body. Speak in tongues and charge your spirit and then give the Word concerning your health. Your body will respond to the Word of God. You belong to the divine class, full of the life of God! Even now, say, “I refuse to be sick. I live above age-related or environment-related conditions. My blood pressure is normal, my heart is perfect, and all my organs function perfectly. I walk in divine health and strength all my days, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.”

The words you speak determine your health, your appearance, and even your future. Your thoughts and words shape not just your life but even your physical appearance. That’s because words are thoughts clothed in vocabulary, and every person is a reflection of their thoughts.

Therefore, if words are an expression of thoughts, then your words reveal your character. No one can live beyond the character of their words; your words define you. Have you seen people who constantly look worried, even when they’re not frowning? Their faces carry the imprint of their thoughts and words. Their health, their emotions, and even their physical features are affected by what they’ve been saying and thinking. That’s because your words are the forces that mould your life.

When you speak words of faith, victory, power, success and divine health, your life will align with those words. Proverbs 15:4 says, “A wholesome tongue is a tree of life….” Proverbs 18:21 declares, “Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.” 1 Peter 3:10 takes it to a climax; it says, “For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile.” Speak the right words, for you’re what you say. What you say is what you get (Mark 11:23). Praise God!

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for the power of words and the ability to speak and shape my future in line with your perfect will. My words are filled with faith, strength and divine wisdom, bringing health to my body, joy to my spirit and success to my path. I walk in victory always, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Practise speaking faith-filled words aloud about your health, family, school, and future.

Proverbs 18:21 AMPC; James 3:5-6; Mark 11:23

message:
A young lady was born with a severe blood condition. After years of failed treatments and endless reports of “no hope” from doctors, she was overwhelmed. When she shared her story, it was clear she thought more about the size of her problem than the greatness of God. But in just a moment, with a simple declaration, “In the Name of Jesus Christ, you are made whole,” everything changed. A couple of weeks later, she did all the medical tests and there was no trace of the sickness in her body anymore.

As a child of God, never find yourself in situations of desperation or lack where you’re constrained to beg. Even in prayer, God doesn’t want you to beg Him; He has honoured you too much for that. Instead, take your rightful place as His heir. Embrace your position as a child of the Monarch of the universe, honoured, dignified and glorified. The challenge with some folks is that they think about the size of their problems instead of putting their focus on the Lord. What you need is to prove God in your life.

Observe what He says in Malachi 3:10, “...prove me now herewith....” Prove Him and see; He’s not intimidated by the greatness of your need. Trust God with your life. Do your part, and He will do His part. He’s more willing and enthusiastic for your success than you could ever be for yourself. That’s why when you pray, don’t plead or act as though He’s reluctant to bless you.

Jesus said in Matthew 7:11, “If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?” Simply exercise your faith, and trust in the Lord, for He loves you more than you love yourself, and He’s more than able to sustain you in the realm of superabundance. Prove Him in your life.

scripture: “Meditate on these things; give yourself entirely to them, that your progress may be evident to all.”

prayer: Dear Father, I thank you for the light of your Word that illuminates my path and teaches me the principles for a successful life. message:
In life, there’s success, and then there’s good success. Good success is God’s will for you, and it has a key recipe: meditating on the Word! God said in Joshua 1:8, “This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success.”

The instruction is clear: keep the Word in your mouth, meditate on it constantly so that you may act on it. This is the divine recipe for good success and prosperity. Notice that the scripture doesn’t say God will make your way prosperous; it says you will make your way prosperous as a result of doing the Word—acting on what you meditate upon day and night. The Amplified Classic (AMPC) puts it this way: “This Book of the Law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe and do according to all that is written in it. For then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall deal wisely and have good success.”

The Word of God in your mouth and heart, coupled with consistent action, produces wisdom, prosperity and good success. When I discovered this as a young teenager, it settled everything for me. I knew I was destined for success because I found the principle that produces it. I even declared to my classmates that I was going to be very successful. Why? I could see it in the Word. God already showed me what to do, and I was going to act on it. At such a young age, I held “Success in Life Seminars,” teaching these principles to others. I had seen the truth in God’s Word and I knew it worked. Even now, the principle remains the same: meditate on the Word; act on it, and good success, not just success, will be the inevitable result. Hallelujah!

excerpt: Praying in the Spirit is the primary way for Christians to pray; it means praying in other tongues.
scripture: “Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints”
subtitle: (The Constant Prescription for All Prayers)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the privilege of prayer and the opportunity it gives us to invoke heaven’s blessings on earth. As I pray in the Spirit, my spirit is aligned with your divine purpose. extras.label: Act
extras.text: Pray in tongues daily; make it your priority prayer language. Expect transformation: supernatural health, spiritual strength, and consistent victories.

furtherStudy: Jude 1:20 AMPC; 1 Corinthians 14:14-15 AMPC; Ephesians 6:18 AMPC
message:
Praying in the Spirit is the primary way for Christians to pray; it means praying in other tongues. When you pray in tongues, it’s your spirit praying, even though your understanding is unfruitful. Thus, the spiritual man prays first with the spirit and then with the understanding also.

Sadly, many reverse this order; they pray predominantly with their understanding and sparingly in tongues. That’s not going to work. Recall what we read in our opening scripture; it means there’re different kinds or forms of prayer.

However, irrespective or alongside all these various types of prayers, you should pray in the Spirit, that is, pray in other tongues. Think of this like a doctor’s prescription that says, “Take these tablets with every meal.” Now, breakfast, lunch and dinner are different meals, yet the tablets are a constant addition to each. Similarly, God says, with all types of prayer—be it the prayer of intercession, prayer of faith, prayer of worship, etc.—pray in the Spirit.

Speak in tongues. The Apostle Paul sheds light on this in 1 Corinthians 14:14-15: “For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful. What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also….” 1 Corinthians 14:2 says, “For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.”

Make this a priority in your life. Cultivate the habit of praying in tongues every day, and you’ll experience extraordinary victories in your life. Your spiritual walk will be transformed and you’ll always be steps ahead of trouble before they manifest. Plus that, your health will blossom supernaturally as your physical body is constantly vitalized and rejuvenated by doses of divine currents through praying in the Spirit.

Even though that military base is physically located outside its home country, it functions as an extension of its government, wielding the full authority and power of its homeland. Every action, directive, and purpose of the base reflects the instructions and vision of its home government.

Likewise, we’re ambassadors of Christ, functioning with the power and jurisdiction of our heavenly kingdom. Our presence in this world is a declaration of heaven’s rule, as we manifest God’s righteousness and judgment everywhere we are. 2 Corinthians 5:20 says, “Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.” Walk in the consciousness of your heavenly identity, functioning as an extension of God’s Kingdom on earth.

Establish His righteousness and judgment in your sphere of influence. Philippians 3:20 (AMPC) says, “But we are citizens of the state (commonwealth, homeland) which is in heaven....” As citizens of heaven, we extend God’s influence and dominion to the nations. The beauty of this divine arrangement is that our identity and operations remain rooted in God’s Kingdom. Whatever we bind on earth is bound in heaven, and whatever we loose on earth is loosed in heaven (Matthew 18:18). Blessed be God.

Dear Father, I thank you for making me a king and a priest unto you, reigning with divine authority. I walk in the consciousness of my heavenly identity, functioning as an extension of your kingdom on earth. Through me, your righteousness and judgment are established in every sphere of influence and my life is a manifestation of your power and dominion, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

Live as an ambassador, representing Christ in speech, actions, and decisions.

For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.”

This is not speaking in tongues. It is the Holy Ghost interceding for us with groanings, deep, heartfelt expressions that words can’t articulate. Have you experienced moments when words fail, and instead, your spirit is burdened with groanings and deep sighs? These are times when the Holy Ghost takes over, interceding in your behalf. When this happens, continue in prayer until you have a release in your spirit. This kind of prayer is so powerful. It allows the Holy Ghost to address situations beyond your understanding; it’s a divine strategy for living an ever-victorious life in Christ.

The power and the effect when the Spirit prays through us like that are incontrovertible; we invoke the power and dominion of heaven on earth, manifesting divine realities. message:

message:
Think about your heart for a moment. Doctors can show you where it is, how it pumps blood, and even measure its beats per minute. But here’s the thing: the heart, though vital, isn’t the true source of life; it’s just a vessel through which life flows. Scientists can replace a failing heart with a new one, but they still can’t explain the real force that makes life happen.

The reality of Christ in you is a profound truth that science struggles to define. Scientists can’t locate the essence of life within the human body. They can pinpoint the heart, the brain, and other organs, but the life-force itself remains elusive. Life—the very thing that animates every living being—is undetectable. Now consider this: the life that scientists can’t find, the essence they can’t locate, the phenomenon they’re unable to explain became flesh: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us…”(John 1:14).

Jesus Christ is eternal life encapsulated in human flesh; this is the greatest miracle to ever occur. Who is Christ? He’s the divine essence, eternal life personified, the embodiment of life itself. He said, “...I am the way, the truth, and the life...” (John 14:6). When you have Christ, you have life, the very essence that sustains all creation. Light is another phenomenon that challenges human understanding. It is difficult to describe light without referencing a greater light. In the presence of a stronger light, a lesser light fades into paltriness. For example, a candle light in the bright noon sun has no visible effect. Jesus said, “...I am the light of the world...” (John 8:12).

body:
Think about your heart for a moment. Doctors can show you where it is, how it pumps blood, and even measure its beats per minute. But here’s the thing: the heart, though vital, isn’t the true source of life; it’s just a vessel through which life flows. Scientists can replace a failing heart with a new one, but they still can’t explain the real force that makes life happen.

The reality of Christ in you is a profound truth that science struggles to define. Scientists can’t locate the essence of life within the human body. They can pinpoint the heart, the brain, and other organs, but the life-force itself remains elusive. Life—the very thing that animates every living being—is undetectable. Now consider this: the life that scientists can’t find, the essence they can’t locate, the phenomenon they’re unable to explain became flesh: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us…”(John 1:14).

Jesus Christ is eternal life encapsulated in human flesh; this is the greatest miracle to ever occur. Who is Christ? He’s the divine essence, eternal life personified, the embodiment of life itself. He said, “...I am the way, the truth, and the life...” (John 14:6). When you have Christ, you have life, the very essence that sustains all creation. Light is another phenomenon that challenges human understanding. It is difficult to describe light without referencing a greater light. In the presence of a stronger light, a lesser light fades into paltriness. For example, a candle light in the bright noon sun has no visible effect. Jesus said, “...I am the light of the world...” (John 8:12).

This is the light that lights every man who comes into the world (John 1:9). When He declared Himself as the light of the world, He wasn’t referring to a physical light but to a spiritual illumination that transcends all understanding. He is the source of all light, the essence that gives meaning and purpose to life. To have Christ in you, therefore, means that the very life and light of God dwells in you. It means you carry within you the hope of glory, the power that sustains the universe, and the wisdom that confounds the world.

## Prayer

Dear Father, thank you for the supernatural life you’ve given me in Christ. I’m grateful for your life and light in my spirit. I stand firm in the truth of who I am in Christ; I walk in the consciousness of this truth, illuminating my world and bringing glory to you, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Declare it boldly every day: “Christ is my life. His light shines through me. I carry the essence of God inside me!”

However, just as a newborn child is fully human at birth but must grow to maturity, so also the child of God must grow spiritually. message:
Sarah woke troubled. In her dream the night before, she saw herself losing her job, and all day she couldn’t shake the fear. She spoke nervously to her friends, made decisions out of anxiety, and carried a heaviness in her heart—all because of a dream.

But Scripture invites us to see dreams differently. Through the prophet Jeremiah, God draws a sharp line: “The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream; and he who has My word, let him speak My word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat?” says the Lord.” (Jeremiah 23:28 NKJV).

Dreams, Jeremiah says, are like chaff—the husks that blow away in the wind when wheat is threshed. They may seem impressive, even alarming, but they have no weight, no substance. The Word of God, however, is wheat: nourishing, grounding, life-giving.

In the Old Testament, God sometimes used dreams to guide His people. But with the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost, a greater way was given. Now God speaks by His Spirit and through His Word, not through dreams that confuse or mislead.

That means Christians are not to be guided by what they see in the night but by the eternal Word that never changes. To live by dreams is to cling to chaff; to live by the Spirit and the Word is to hold the grain that feeds and sustains.

message:
Farmers know the quiet patience of waiting for rain. They till the soil, plant their seeds, and look to the sky. Days may pass with no sign of water, yet they keep tending the ground because they understand a truth written into creation: when the clouds are full, they will pour themselves upon the earth (Ecclesiastes 11:3).

Prayer works in much the same way. Some requests are answered swiftly, but other kinds of prayer must be heaped upon one another, built up day after day, until the “cloud” is heavy enough to release its blessing. Every day, you add some more. And then, you add some more, and some more, until you reach the climax where the results burst forth like a gusher, blowing the lid open.

We often grow impatient, wondering why answers seem delayed. But just as a farmer cannot rush the clouds, neither can we rush the Spirit’s timing. Our role is to persevere, to pray without ceasing (1 Thessalonians 5:17), trusting that no prayer is wasted. Sometimes, the Spirit of God can lead you to fast for a certain number of days because He wants you to keep filling up your cloud. It’s not so much about staying away from food; that’s not what He’s getting at. Rather, it’s about focusing your attention on the Spirit and having the kind of meditation and prayer that conditions your spirit for the work He wants to do in you, for you or through you.

And when the cloud finally bursts, it is rarely a trickle. It comes as a gusher—answers overflowing. Yet even then, prayer does not end. For new clouds are always forming, and new rain is always needed. So, lift your eyes to heaven. Keep adding your prayers, your worship, and your intercession. The clouds are filling. And when they’re full, they’ll empty themselves upon your life in abundance, in God’s perfect time.

message:
Praying in the Spirit is not a casual exercise; it is a vital spiritual practice that sustains and strengthens you. God designed prayer—especially praying in tongues— as a divine means of keeping your spirit healthy, vibrant, and strong. When you pray in tongues, you edify yourself. It’s like charging a battery until it is full. Your spirit is energised, fortified, and refreshed, enabling you to function effectively in the things of God. No wonder Paul declared in Romans 1:9 NKJV, “For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of His Son....” We serve God with our spirit, and for that spirit to remain effective, it must continually be built up.

As you do, you rise higher and higher like an edifice, strong and unshakeable. Paul understood this deeply. He prayed that the Ephesian church be strengthened with might through God’s Spirit in their inner man (Ephesians 3:16). The word “might” here refers to miracle-working ability infused into your spirit by the Holy Ghost. That was Paul’s secret to his continuous growth, victories, and extraordinary accomplishments. He could boldly say, “I thank my God I speak with tongues more than you all” (1 Corinthians 14:18 NKJV).

Paul’s consistency in praying in tongues was key to his continuous progress, victories and extraordinary accomplishments. It wasn’t something he did occasionally; it was a lifestyle. If you desire consistent growth, success, and advancement, then praying in the Spirit must be something you do consistently. It’ll help you make consistent progress as you experience continuous increase in grace and victory after victory. Hallelujah!

message:
A certain sculptor sat before a massive block of marble. He didn’t rush to strike it with his chisel. Instead, he spent hours sketching, envisioning, and aligning his mind with the form he intended to reveal. Only then did he begin to work.

Prayer is much like that. Many approach God’s throne hastily, with unformed words and scattered thoughts, hoping that sheer length or repetition will suffice. But the Lord Jesus taught us in Matthew 6:7 not to pray “vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.” True prayer is not careless utterance; it is a spiritual alignment, a purposeful engagement with the Father.

When you plan your prayer, you bring order to your fellowship. You’re not reducing the time spent with God— you’re elevating it. By taking a moment to write down the matters of your heart—your desires, the areas where you need His guidance, and even the thoughts He has already impressed upon you—you position yourself to pray with clarity and faith.

Then, as you yield to the Spirit in tongues, you transcend human vocabulary. You speak mysteries, articulating divine secrets that only heaven can decode. It’ll help to always take a moment to write down the things you want to talk to the Lord about. Think about the areas of your life where you desire His guidance, intervention and blessings. Also, consider the thoughts and insights He might have already stirred in your heart. Then, you speak in tongues. Through speaking in tongues, you articulate divine mysteries and gain insight into realities beyond human comprehension.

message:
One of the most beautiful realities of the Christian life is the assurance that God is at work in you. Every day, as you rise and step into your assignments, you must be conscious of this truth: God is at work in me! He isn’t watching from afar; He is actively involved, faithfully perfecting the good work He began in you.

The Bible says in Philippians 2:13 NKJV, “For it is God who works in you both to will and to do for His good pleasure.” This is absolute truth. It’s God Himself working in you, making you willing and giving you the ability to fulfil His divine purpose. You’re His living tabernacle, His outstretched arm, His operational headquarters on the earth. How could you fail when His power and wisdom are at work in you?

In Judges 6:14 NKJV, the Lord said to Gideon, “… Go in this might of yours, and you shall save Israel from the hand of the Midianites. Have I not sent you?” What he had was sufficient because the presence of God was with him. The same is true of you. What you have is more than enough. Christ in you is enough! God at work in you is enough!

You can win souls in multitudes, you can change your world, and you can accomplish the extraordinary. The Spirit of God is working mightily in you, and His glory is revealed through you. You’re a burning and shining light, drawing men and women into the Kingdom. Glory to God!

message:
How extraordinary to know that the life we have in Christ is a life of glory. In the master’s profound prayer to the Father, recorded in John 17, the Lord Jesus declared, “And the glory which You gave Me I have given them…” (John 17:22 NKJV). What a revelation! The very glory that the Father bestowed upon the Son, the Son has given to us.

This isn’t a promise awaiting fulfilment; it’s a present-hour reality. Many, out of religious sentiment, pray, “Lord, we will not take Your glory.” But that contradicts the words of the Master Himself. He said, “I have given them.” To deny this is to refuse what Christ has freely bestowed. In the Old Testament, the priest’s garment was called the robe of glory and beauty. It symbolised righteousness, splendour, and divine acceptance. Now, we are not merely symbolically adorned—we have been clothed with Christ Himself. His glory is our garment, His righteousness our robe, His life our very essence. Blessed be God!

Walking in this glory means manifesting the excellence, beauty, and perfections of divinity. You have been called to a life of victory, abundance, health, and righteousness. It is inconsistent with the glory life to dwell in sickness, poverty, defeat, or sin. These are not reflections of the glory of God. The Bible says, “But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light” (1 Peter 2:9).

Therefore, refuse to settle for anything less than the life Christ has made available. Walk in the consciousness of your glory life. Manifest His splendour everywhere, for you are His glory revealed.

message:
The destiny of nations is not first decided in parliaments or presidential offices; it is determined in the unseen arena of the spirit. History has shown that policies may guide a nation, but it is prayer that governs its soul. The Word of God reveals to us that the quietness, peace, and prosperity many long for do not emerge by chance—they are birthed when God’s people take their place in intercession.

Scripture admonishes us in 1 Timothy 2:1-2 NKJV: “Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence.” This is God’s blueprint for national peace.

Make it your daily culture to lift your leaders in prayer—your president, governors, lawmakers, judges, community heads, law enforcement, and all in positions of influence. Pray that God’s wisdom guides their decisions, that righteousness prevails in their policies, and that peace is established in your land. Isaiah 1:19 NKJV declares,“If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land.” There’s more wealth in your nation than you can imagine, but the onus is on God’s people to do the needful: act on the Word. Pray for your nation and its leaders as God has instructed.

The solution is not in protests or complaints, nor is it in merely changing one leader for another. True transformation begins when we, God’s people, align with His Word and intercede earnestly. Create the conditions for a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty in your nation through your heartfelt prayers as directed by the Spirit.

title: The Wisdom of His Process
excerpt: Life with God is a journey of divine order. Just as a wise builder doesn’t lay the roof before the foundation, so the Lord doesn’t thrust His children into seasons they’re not prepared for.
scripture: “Then it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, “Lest perhaps the people change their minds when they see war, and return to Egypt.”
subtitle: (The Lord Prepares And Trains You For Each Level)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for leading me in the way I should go and preparing me for the life of victory and excellence you’ve ordained for me. I trust in your divine wisdom and timing as I grow in competence and capacity to fulfil your purpose for my life, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Excitedly thank the Lord for where He has brought you to and where He’s leading you.

message:
Life with God is a journey of divine order. Just as a wise builder doesn’t lay the roof before the foundation, so the Lord doesn’t thrust His children into seasons they’re not prepared for. In His love, He guides each step, ensuring that every phase equips us for greater glory.

When Israel came out of Egypt, the Lord deliberately avoided the shorter route through Philistine territory. Though quicker, it wasn’t safer. They were fresh out of slavery—untrained for war and unready for confrontation. So He led them through the wilderness, where they encountered His provision and guidance. Through this journey, God revealed Himself to them as Jehovah Rapha, their physician, and Jehovah Rohi, their shepherd. When they eventually faced battles, they called Him Jehovah Nissi, their banner who gives them victory.

This is how God works with us. At times, the path may seem longer, but it is the path of preparation. Through it, He strengthens your faith, enlarges your vision, and equips you for greater victories. I recall my first crusade at just fifteen years old. Before then, I preached house to house, on the streets, and in schools—even during workers’ lunch breaks. The results were beautiful but small compared to what God is doing with me today. Back then, He didn’t give me twenty thousand souls to minister to at once because I wasn’t yet ready for that magnitude. Growth was necessary.

We often want things to move fast, don’t we? Faster phones, faster computers. But God doesn’t work according to man’s timing. He works according to His divine patterns, timing and purpose, and when He brings you to that place, you’ll discover that every step was necessary.

Dear Father, thank you for leading me in the way I should go and preparing me for the life of victory and excellence you’ve ordained for me. I trust in your divine wisdom and timing as I grow in competence and capacity to fulfil your purpose for my life, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Act

Excitedly thank the Lord for where He has brought you to and where He’s leading you.

Psalm 37:23; Deuteronomy 8:2

message:
One of the greatest blessings of our Christian journey is belonging to the body of Christ. The church is not a man-made idea; it is the living vision of the Lord Jesus Himself, who declared, “I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matthew 16:18 KJV). What a glorious truth! Yet, there are those who have withdrawn from fellowship because of offences—words spoken, actions taken, or misunderstandings that wounded them. Beloved, that should never be your response. Don’t let anything or anyone separate you from God’s house.

Often, people carry into the church the same patterns they learnt at home or in life. Some left their families because of correction or discipline they disliked, and they carry that same resistance into the household of God. But in Christ, we are called to a higher life. We receive correction with humility and guidance with joy, and we forgive quickly when offended. Why? Because salvation means Jesus is Lord. You are no longer in charge of your life; He is.

The church is divinely structured. “And He Himself gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and some pastors and teachers, for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ, till we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God…” (Ephesians 4:11-13 NKJV). This order is for your growth, maturity, and effectiveness in Christ.

So, never say, “I was offended by what the pastor said; therefore, I won’t attend anymore.” No! The Lord Himself leads His Church (John 10:4). When you yield to His lordship, you also yield to the structures He has set in place. Through fellowship, correction, and instruction, your spirit is trained, your mind renewed, and your walk strengthened.

message:
When a child is born, no parent would dream of leaving that little one unattended. The baby must be fed, cared for, and nurtured into maturity. It’s the same with those who come to Christ. Salvation is not the end but the beginning of a glorious journey, a brand-new life that requires guidance, feeding, and training in righteousness.

When someone receives salvation, he/she is a spiritual infant. Their recreated human spirit craves nourishment, and the Word of God is that nourishment—the only food that guarantees growth. Just as a newborn depends on milk to grow, a newly born-again Christian depends on the Word to be strengthened, rooted, and established in Christ. This is where the church plays a vital role. It’s God’s training ground, the place where His children are taught, equipped, and nurtured.

When you win a soul, don’t tell them, “Go to any nice church.” No! Bring them to your church, where you know the Word is taught in truth and power. They trusted your message of Christ; therefore, let them experience the fellowship of the same family from which you came. Introduce them to your pastor, leaders, and fellow brethren. Show them that heaven rejoices over their salvation, and so does the church family. In this atmosphere of love and teaching, they will grow into strong, vibrant Christians who in turn will win and disciple others.

Make your evangelism complete. Help them see that their growth in Christ is a priority and that the church is the best environment for them to flourish spiritually. If you’re not yet a member of a local church, or seeking one, you could begin by contacting the person or church who gave you this book, or log on to www.christembassy.org for more information.

title: Be Bold!
excerpt: There’s something remarkable about a man or woman who knows who they are in Christ. Such knowledge stirs an inner boldness that can’t be quenched.
scripture: “For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.”
subtitle: (Courage And Audacity Are Important In Life)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I walk with the assurance of who I am in Christ, speaking up and making my voice count for God’s kingdom and for His glory in these last days. I remain humble as I boldly declare His truth, knowing that He is with me always. I refuse to be intimidated by fear or timidity, for the Spirit of power, love, and a sound mind is at work in me. extras.label: Act

message:
There’s something remarkable about a man or woman who knows who they are in Christ. Such knowledge stirs an inner boldness that can’t be quenched. You walk into a room, and you carry yourself with dignity, assurance, and quiet strength. Even when faced with challenges, you remain fearless because your confidence is not in the flesh but in the Spirit of God.

Think about the Lord Jesus as He stood before Pontius Pilate. He wasn’t intimidated; He gave a bold testimony. Though He was the embodiment of humility, He was never fearful or unsure. That’s the picture of dominion—calm, assured, yet unwavering. And this is the same life God has called you to live.

I recall, as a young schoolboy, I was bright and intelligent, yet hesitant. Even when I knew the right answers, I often kept quiet. Others, less knowledgeable but bolder, got the attention, the commendation, or the correction. But things took a different turn when I received the Holy Spirit. I lost my fears, and boldness flooded my spirit. I became audacious and unafraid to speak out.

This is exactly what God told Joshua when he was stepping into leadership: “Only be strong and very courageous…” (Joshua 1:7 NKJV). Strength and courage are not optional—they’re vital! Many know the truth, and many have wisdom to contribute, yet fear silences them. But those who speak—whether right or wrong—get noticed, and God can guide and refine them.

So don’t shrink back. When you greet people, do it with confidence. When you speak, let your voice ring with clarity. Boldness isn’t arrogance—it’s a reflection of the Spirit of power within you. Balance it with humility, and you’ll shine as a true ambassador of Christ.

title: Choose the Love Way
excerpt: I once witnessed two children at play. One accidentally pushed the other, and in a flash, tears filled the boy’s eyes.
scripture: “Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and evil speaking be put away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ forgave you.”
subtitle: (Love Is The True Mark Of Your Christian Identity)

extras.label: Speak
extras.text: I choose to walk in love, just as Christ loved me and gave Himself for me. I embrace the love-way and respond with kindness; I’m quick to forgive. Thank you, Lord, for making me an expression of your love, bringing healing, joy and peace to those around me.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: Choose today to respond in love and replace every urge to retaliate with a smile, a prayer, or a kind word.

message:
I once witnessed two children at play. One accidentally pushed the other, and in a flash, tears filled the boy’s eyes. But before I could say a word, he smiled, reached out, and hugged his friend. No grudges, no bitterness—just love in its purest expression. How beautiful!

The Lord Jesus calls us to live this way every day—in love. He said, “By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another” (John 13:35 NKJV). Love is the true mark of our Christian identity. It’s not how loud we pray, nor how often we attend church, but how well we love—especially when it’s not convenient. Challenges will surely come. People may speak against you, hurt you, or mistreat you. Yet, the Master said, “…love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you” (Matthew 5:44 NKJV). That’s the way of victory!

Bitterness, anger, and resentment are heavy weights. They clog the wheel of progress and hinder your growth in the spirit. No matter who it is—family, colleague, neighbour, or even a stranger—never allow bitterness a place in your heart. Instead, choose the love way. Love is not just a smile or a kind word; it’s a divine force. It begins in your heart and flows into your actions. It’s seeing others the way God sees them—precious and valuable to Him. When you live this way, your life becomes an inspiration, and your impact spreads far beyond what you can imagine.

So, refuse to retaliate when insulted. Be unflustered when challenged. Like Jesus, lift your hands and say, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” Let love be your response, your language, your lifestyle. For in walking in love, you walk in the fullness of God. Hallelujah!

extras.label: Speak

message:
In our last study, we saw how sound codes carry divine energy and meaning. Today, let’s take it a step further—into your very body. Years ago, a groundbreaking experiment showed the effect of words on water. Water placed in jars was exposed to different words. When kind and uplifting words like “You are beautiful, you are wonderful” were spoken, the water crystals formed into stunning, harmonious patterns. But when harsh words like “You’re ugly, useless” were directed at other jars, the crystals became deformed and chaotic.

This experiment reveals a significant lesson. Recall that the human body is over seventy per cent water, which accounts for more than two-thirds of its composition. Therefore, the words you speak to yourself and your body have a tangible effect. This isn’t just science; it’s a spiritual law. The Bible already revealed it long ago: “Death and life are in the power of the tongue” (Proverbs 18:21 NKJV).

When you speak negatively to yourself—saying things like, “This headache is killing me” or “I’m always sick”—you are literally coding your body with destruction. Those words send sound codes into the water molecules in your system, disfiguring them and, over time, manifesting as sickness, weakness, or inexplicable conditions.

However, the opposite is also true! When you speak words of life, health, and strength, those same crystals align beautifully, carrying the energy of life throughout your body. You can renew your health, strengthen your body, and invigorate your mind by the consistent release of faith-filled sound codes.

This is why you must be mindful of your speech; the crystals in your body respond to words, and your speech has the potential to heal, transform and invigorate your physical being. Take this seriously.

title: Create Sound Codes
excerpt: Some years ago, I watched a little child mimic her mother’s words with such passion—even though she didn’t yet understand what those words meant.
scripture: “By faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that the things which are seen were not made of things which are visible.”
subtitle: (Your Words Are Carriers Of Divine Energy)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the creative power of words. Through your Word, all things were made, and by speaking in faith, I align with your divine principles. I use my words wisely to encode life, meaning and purpose in everything I say. Thank you for teaching me these profound truths and for making me a creator through the power of my words, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.text: Right now, speak in tongues and release faith-filled declarations.

message:
Some years ago, I watched a little child mimic her mother’s words with such passion—even though she didn’t yet understand what those words meant. But soon enough, as the days passed, she began to respond, communicate, and even instruct using the very words she had heard. That’s the mystery of sound coding—the assignment of meaning, interpretation, and communication of sound or the cognitive process for the creation of sound.

In the beginning, God set this eternal principle in motion. He didn’t just think creation into existence; He spoke it. “Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.” (Genesis 1:3 NKJV). Why did He speak? Because words are carriers of divine energy. They aren’t mere sounds; they are codes—sound codes—that embed instruction, meaning, and purpose into creation itself. When you teach a child a language, you are transferring sound codes into that child. Over time, those codes form memory, identity, and expression. In the same way, when God spoke, He encoded creation with His divine purpose. Every tree, every star, every living thing resonates with the sound code of His Word.

Your words are not empty. They’re sound codes filled with creative power. Every time you speak, you release energy into the atmosphere. This is why the Bible declares, “Death and life are in the power of the tongue” (Proverbs 18:21 NKJV). Your tongue is not just for communication—it’s for creation. Therefore, refuse to speak carelessly. Instead, fill your mouth with faith-filled words. Speak health to your body. Speak progress into your life. Speak peace into your home.

Remember: everything in creation responds to the sound code of your words. Just as God’s Word framed the worlds, your words—spoken in faith—frame your reality today.

excerpt: There’s a reason people often say, “Actions speak louder than words.” Think about a friend who promises to always be there for you, but when the time comes, they fail to show up.
scripture: “For our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit and in much assurance, as you know what kind of men we were among you for your sake.”

prayer: Dear Father, I live in alignment with your Word as I express my love, gratitude and worship through my words and actions, through my offerings and different oblations. I honour you fully, empowered by the Holy Spirit to worship you in spirit and in truth, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act

message:
There’s a reason people often say, “Actions speak louder than words.” Think about a friend who promises to always be there for you, but when the time comes, they fail to show up. Their words lose meaning because there’s no action to back them.

In many contexts in Scriptures, we see how God gave us the precedence of words and actions going together. For example, Genesis 2:7 tells us, “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” He didn’t use words only in creating man. The Apostle John, in 1 John 3:18, admonishes us, “My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.” It’s not enough to say, “I love the Lord,” or “I love people.” Love is proven in action. It’s demonstrated.

Even in thanksgiving, we don’t just say, “Thank you, Lord.” We show it. We lift our voices in worship, yes, but we also present offerings to the Lord, we serve, and we give of ourselves. The Scriptures are replete with this principle: the Word must be backed by action for it to produce results in your life. In 1 Thessalonians 1:5, as read in the theme verse, we see that the Gospel didn’t come to the Christians in Thessalonica in word only but in power and in the Holy Ghost. Our preaching must be accompanied by the power of the Holy Spirit.

Likewise, James teaches us it’s the doer of the Word who is blessed, not the hearer only (James 1:22–25). Even the Lord Jesus Himself rebuked those whose worship was only lip service, saying, “‘These people draw near to Me with their mouth, and honor Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.”(Matthew 15:8 NKJV). Words alone, without corresponding action, are insufficient in expressing our devotion to the Lord. It also reminds of what the Bible says about faith without works or corresponding action—it’s dead: “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also” (James 2:26 NKJV).

message:
Growth is God’s design. Everything He created is made to grow, to advance, and to reach fullness. The seed becomes a tree. The child becomes an adult. In the same way, God expects His children to grow into spiritual maturity.

The Apostle Paul wrote about Epaphras, who prayed fervently for the Christians in Colossae, “that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God” (Colossians 4:12 NKJV). Notice the Spirit’s desire: perfection and completeness. The words “perfect,” Greek (teleios), and “complete,” Greek (plēroō), in this context are synonymous and often used interchangeably in the Scriptures to specifically refer to being full-grown or mature. They denote a state of spiritual maturity where one becomes a full-grown Christian.

Just as earthly parents raise their children to be responsible and able to take on life, God also desires for you to be mature and take responsibilities in the Kingdom, influence others, and establish His righteousness in the earth. He doesn’t want you tossed about by circumstances or deceived by false ideas. He wants you strong, discerning, and fruitful. 2 Timothy 3:17 NKJV says, “That the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.” Maturity in Christ means reaching a level where you are grounded in the Word, able to discern God’s will, and fully equipped to carry out His purposes. James 1:4 says, “But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.”

This is God’s will and desire for His children. Ephesians 4:13 (AMPC) says, “...until we all attain oneness in the faith and in the comprehension of the [full and accurate] knowledge of the Son of God, that [we might arrive] at really mature manhood (the completeness of personality which is nothing less than the standard height of Christ’s own perfection)....” Blessed be God!

message:
In Christ Jesus, you’ve been called to a life of victory, glory, and excellence. This is God’s plan for you. Yet many people, knowingly or not, resist this truth. They say things like, “We are all human” or “Nobody is perfect.” But these are excuses that keep them living below the divine life God has given us in Christ. The Bible tells us,“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new” (2 Corinthians 5:17 NKJV).

When you were born again, you became a new person—no longer just human, but born of God. You’re now a partaker of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). So when someone says “Nobody is perfect,” remember the words of Jesus: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect” (Matthew 5:48 NIV). Perfection here means to be full-grown in maturity, blameless, unspotted, wanting nothing; a completeness. This is the life Christ has made possible for you.

Another phrase you often hear is “We all make mistakes.” But God’s Word shows us something different: “Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God” (1 John 3:9 NKJV). The very life of God in you empowers you to live above sin, above failure, and above limitation. Don’t let human traditions or negative ideas shape how you see yourself. God’s Word is your truth.

In Christ, you’ve been called to a life of excellence, righteousness, dominion, and victory over every circumstance. This is your reality. Refuse to accept mediocrity or failure. Look to the Word, believe it, and live by it. We’ll delve more into this in our next study.

message:
As a child, your parents made decisions for you. They decided where you lived, what school you went to, and even what food you ate. Even the Lord Jesus experienced this. For instance, when He was born, He was laid in a manger—not by His choice, but by His parents’ decision. Later, when Herod sought to kill Him, the angel did not speak to Jesus but to Joseph, saying, “…Arise, take the young Child and His mother, flee to Egypt”(Matthew 2:13 NKJV). The Lord Jesus did not decide this; He was carried along as a child.

Even as He grew, He remained subject to Joseph and Mary. But when He became a man, He took responsibility for His own life and purpose. Moses also, when he came of age, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter (Hebrews 11:24). In the same way, you must take charge of your life. Over the years, I have taught God’s people all around the world that though you may not have been responsible for the family into which you were born, nor for the circumstances that surrounded your birth, you are absolutely responsible for the life you choose to live when you come to maturity and the age of accountability.

You can’t allow your environment, the economy, or the opinions of others dictate how you live. Choose victory every day. Determine to succeed in all that you do because that is the life you have in Christ. The Bible says, “But thanks be to God, Who in Christ always leads us in triumph [as trophies of Christ’s victory] and through us spreads and makes evident the fragrance of the knowledge of God everywhere” (2 Corinthians 2:14 AMPC). And again, “For whatever is born of God is victorious over the world…” (1 John 5:4 AMPC).

You’re born of God and have overcome the world. You’re victorious in Christ. Therefore, choose to live victoriously every day. Live above the systems of this world.

message:
If you’ve ever gone mountain climbing, one of the most fascinating things you’ll discover is how insignificant everything below seems. From above, the tallest buildings shrink, the busiest roads fade, and what once demanded attention becomes insignificant. There’s a higher realm of life to which we’ve been called in Christ Jesus. It’s a place of glory and dominion, far above the distractions and limitations of this world. The Word declares, “Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things” (Colossians 3:2 NIV). This is the mountaintop life.

It brings to mind something remarkable that the Lord told me many years ago; He said, “Son, see from the mountaintop.” The interesting thing is, I didn’t even realise I was on the mountaintop until He told me. I know that some Christians say they are “journeying” and trying to get to the mountaintop. But being born again, you’re on the mountaintop. You’re risen with Christ and are seated together with Him, far above principalities and powers. Therefore, see from there. Live from there.

From the mountaintop, your vision is clear. You see victory, strength, health, prosperity, and continual progress. You’re above the distractions and limitations of the world. You’re in the realm of the Spirit, where all you see is glory. Ponder again what we read in Colossians 3:2 (NIV), “Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.” Your thoughts, desires, focus and devotion should be directed towards heavenly realities, not earthly distractions. Align your mind with the heavenly perspective and live victoriously every day.

## Speak

I see from the mountaintop. My affection is set on heavenly things, and my vision is clear and focused; I live above the distractions and limitations of this world. I function from my exalted place in Christ, far above principalities and powers, far above defeat, sickness, and lack. My thoughts are aligned with God’s Word, and my life is the manifestation of His glory.

title: Only Believe
excerpt: As a sequel to our previous article—“It’s a Message That Works”—it’s important to understand how to position yourself for the results the Gospel produces. The principle is clear: believe.
scripture: “Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”
subtitle: (Accept God’s Word As Truth)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for your Word, which is true and dependable. I act on your Word with boldness and confidence, knowing that what you have said is true and unchanging. My faith is alive and effectual because I act on your Word. I journey from glory to glory, walking in the light of your Word, and fulfilling your purpose for my life victoriously, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: As you study the Word today, declare: “This is truth; this is my reality, and it’s producing results in me.”

message:
As a sequel to our previous article—“It’s a Message That Works”—it’s important to understand how to position yourself for the results the Gospel produces. The principle is clear: believe. To believe is to accept God’s Word as absolute truth and to act accordingly.

What a statement from the lips of the Master in our opening scripture above! Notice the profound but very simple instruction: “Only believe.” He says ALL things are possible to you if you believe. What does it take to believe? It simply means to accept that what the Lord has said is true.

The story of Jairus in Mark 5 illustrates this perfectly. His daughter was at the point of death, and he urgently sought the Lord’s help. But while they were still on the way, the news came that the child had died. Jesus immediately said to him, “Don’t be afraid; just believe” (Mark 5:36 NIV). At Jairus’ house, the Lord took the girl by the hand and said, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!” (Mark 5:41 NLT). Instantly, she rose to life. What made the difference? Jairus refused to succumb to fear; he chose to accept the Master’s words as truth. That’s faith. Faith is the response of the human spirit to the Word of God.

This year, anchor your life on the authority of God’s Word. When He speaks concerning your health, your success, or your future, affirm it boldly: “Yes, Lord, this is truth, and it’s working in my life.” That unwavering response ushers you into a realm of limitless possibilities where all things are possible.

title: It’s a Message That Works
excerpt: Having established the need to be resolute about the divine mission, there’s something even more inspiring I want you to see: the message we carry is not empty; it produces results.
scripture: “For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God to salvation for everyone who believes….”
subtitle: (The Gospel Of Jesus Christ Produces Undeniable Results)
prayer: Dear Father, thank you for the glorious Gospel of Jesus Christ that works everywhere, every time, and for everyone who believes it. I preach this Gospel with boldness and confidence, bringing healing, salvation, and transformation to all who believe. Amen.

extras.label: Act
extras.text: As you go about your day, look for one opportunity to share the Gospel with someone and do it boldly.

message:
Having established the need to be resolute about the divine mission, there’s something even more inspiring I want you to see: the message we carry is not empty; it produces results. It’s the reason you must be quick and bold to share it with others.

The Gospel of Jesus Christ isn’t mere words—it produces undeniable results for anyone who believes. I once ministered to a man with a severe heart condition. Doctors had diagnosed him with heart failure and recommended a transplant. As I shared the Gospel with him, I said, “While I’m talking to you, a change will take place in your heart. Just believe it.” He agreed. After a few minutes of sharing the Word, I declared, “It’s done.” He responded, “Yes, it’s done.” Tests later confirmed it—he had a new heart!

I’ve seen this happen several times. It doesn’t matter what the case is; this Gospel works. The Bible says, “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever” (Hebrews 13:8 NKJV). If He did it then, He’s still doing it now. The message has no borders. It works in every country, every city, and for everyone who believes. It transforms lives, brings healing and health to the sick, prosperity to the poor, and salvation to the lost.

How can we be quiet about such a message that transforms destinies and catapults men and women from despair to victory? body:

message:
In our last study, we saw that God has already marked out a predestined path for your life (Romans 8:29, Ephesians 2:10). The question then is, how do you walk that path with accuracy? The answer is simple: by the Spirit.

Life is filled with choices—some minor, others defining. Opportunities will open before you this year, and you may ask yourself: Should I take this step? Is this the right path? The good news is that you’re not left to guess. The Holy Spirit knows the details. He sees beyond what you can perceive and knows the path of success and victory.

Romans 8:26 NKJV tells us that “the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” When you pray in the Spirit, the Holy Ghost grants to you God’s counsel and unveils the precise course you must follow. There’s so much you don’t know about the year ahead—the people you’ll meet, the places you’ll go, the decisions you’ll face. Yet, the Holy Spirit knows them all. He knows and understands the fine details – things about your life and the things beyond human perception – and He intercedes for you accordingly.

This is why prayer in the Spirit is indispensable. When you pray in the Spirit, you align yourself with God’s perfect plan. Instead of confusion, you receive clarity. Instead of struggling in uncertainty, you walk in divine precision. As you set your vision for the year, refuse to grope in the dark. Engage the Spirit in fellowship; pray much in tongues. Yield to His guidance, and every day of 2026 will unfold with the accuracy of God’s design.

Romans 8:29 (NLT) says, “For God knew his people in advance, and he chose them to become like his Son….” Predestination is at work in you. God has a divine plan for your life, and He has set events and their sequence in motion in line with His divine plan.

Think about John the Baptist. His entire calling was to reveal Jesus to Israel. Yet God didn’t simply tell him who the Messiah was. Instead, John had to wait for the sign: “…The man on whom you see the Spirit come down and remain is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.” (John 1:33 NIV). When Jesus finally stood before him, the moment unfolded exactly as God planned (John 1:29–34).

Or consider Samuel’s mission to anoint Israel’s new king (1 Samuel 16). He thought Eliab, Jesse’s tall and impressive son, was the one. But God corrected him: “People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” 1 Samuel 16:7 (NIV). One by one, Jesse’s sons were rejected until David—the forgotten shepherd boy—was brought in. Then the Lord said, “Rise and anoint him; this is the one.” 1 Samuel 16:12 (NIV). Step by step, God’s plan came into focus.

In the same way, God has a plan for your life, and it’s a good one. He has already set the path and the sequence

1010 of events that will shape you into who He has called you to be. You don’t have to panic or force things to happen. What matters is that you stay yielded to Him, trusting His timing.

message:
The Apostle Paul declares in 2 Corinthians 3:5 NKJV, “...our sufficiency is from God.” The Greek word translated sufficiency is “hikanotēs”, meaning “competence” or “ability”. This means as a child of God, you’re not ordinary; your competence is divine. As you journey into this new year, approach it with this consciousness. Your goals, dreams, and aspirations must be seen through the ability of God at work in you. You’re not limited to natural strength or human intellect; the Spirit of God has infused you with His wisdom and excellence.

This is why it matters what you say. Knowledge alone doesn’t establish divine reality; affirmation does. The Word must be on your lips. Declare often: “My sufficiency is of God. I function with divine competence. I accomplish my dreams with excellence and fulfil every vision by the power of the Spirit.” Each time you affirm this truth, you align your spirit with God’s Word. The Holy Spirit then guides your thoughts, inspires your creativity, and opens opportunities that position you for success. You’ll find yourself walking in paths that manifest God’s power and ability in you.

Understand also that growth is progressive. Competence in every area may not appear at once, but consistency in your confession and sensitivity to the Spirit will bring steady advancement. Each step you take will reveal more of God’s ability in you until your life becomes the unfolding of His wisdom and glory.

So, as you embrace 2026, set your vision high. Don’t think small. Don’t plan as one who is limited. Your sufficiency is of God, and with His competence at work in you, every dream is possible, every goal attainable, and every vision achievable.

message:
Happy New Year! Today isn’t just the first day of a new calendar; it’s the beginning of a new chapter in your journey with God. God has brought you into 2026 for a reason, and He wants you to grow, make progress, and change levels. No matter what last year looked like, this year offers a fresh opportunity to rise—spiritually, mentally, and in every area of your life. But change doesn’t happen automatically. You have to be intentional about it.

Today, as you start the year, take time to reflect: Where am I now? What areas of my life need to go to the next level? Be honest with yourself. Whether it’s your prayer life, school performance, habits, confidence, relationships, or mindset—identify what needs to grow.

Next, visualise where you want to be. Set clear and specific goals. What does your next level look like? Is it reading more books this year? Passing that exam? Starting a small business? Could you be more consistent in your walk with God? Picture it. Write it down.

Then, ask yourself: What actions must I take to get there? Every level change requires effort. You can’t expect a new result from an old routine. Do you need to wake up earlier? Start a Bible plan? Find a mentor? Study smarter? Whatever it is, commit to doing it.

And please keep in mind the most important part: involve God. Pray about your plans and let the Holy Spirit lead you. He knows the best way forward and will give you the strength, wisdom, and grace to make progress.
